questions.question_text: The difference between compound interest and simple interest on a certain sum borrowed at R% per annum for a period of 2 years is Rs.384 and for a period of 3 years is Rs.1344. Find the time in which the sum becomes 6 times itself at simple interest.
questions.solution_text:
Let the borrowed sum be P 
Now, we know that 
The difference between compound interest and simple interest for a period of 2 years is given by: $P\left(\frac{R}{100}\right)^2$ 
The difference between compound interest and simple interest for a period of 3 years is given by:$P\left(\frac{R}{100}\right)^2\left(\frac{R}{100}+3\right)$
so, substituting the given values we get :
$P\left(\frac{R}{100}\right)^2$=384         (1)
$P\left(\frac{R}{100}\right)^2\left(\frac{R}{100}+3\right)$ = 1344     (2)
Dividing equation (2) and (1) we get
$\left(\frac{R}{100}+3\right)$=$\frac{1344}{384}$
⇒$\left(\frac{R}{100}+3\right)$=$\frac{7}{2}$
⇒$\left(\frac{R}{100}\right)$=$\frac{1}{2}$
⇒R=50%
Now let sum becomes 6 times itself in T years at simple interest
We know that 
Amount = Principal (sum borrowed)+Interest(in this case it is simple interest)
⇒6P=P+$\frac{\left(P\times\ 50\times\ T\ \right)}{100}$
⇒5P=$\frac{PT}{2}$
⇒T=10
Hence the sum becomes 6 times itself in 10 years.

To minimize the given expression we have to maximize $\frac{8}{3x^2+1}$
This will be maximum when $3x^2+1$ will be minimum.
The least value of $3x^2+1$ is 1 when $x=0$
Thus the minimum value of the given expression 1 is 
$=1-8=-7$
Expression 2: $\frac{2x^2-5}{2x^2+5}$
$=1-\frac{10}{2x^2+5}$
To minimize the given expression we have to maximize $\frac{10}{2x^2+5}$
This will be maximum when $2x^2+5$ will be minimum.
The least value of $2x^2+5$ is 5 when $x=0$
Thus the minimum value of the given expression 2 is 
$=1-2=-1$
Thus the minimum value of the given expression is $-7-1 = -8$

questions.question_text: 3 prime numbers(all greater than 101) are in an arithmetic progression. Which of the following can be the difference between 2 of these consecutive numbers?
questions.solution_text:
Let the prime numbers be x, x+a and x+2a.
We know every prime number is of the for 6k±1.
Let x = 6k±1.
Let us take all options and verify.
Option a: 6:-
If a = 6, then x+a = 6k±1+6 = 6k+7 or 6k+5.
x+2a = 6k±1+12 = 6k+13 and 6k+11
Both of these are of the form 6k±1
Thus, a = 6 is possible.
Option b: 8:-
If a = 8, then x+a = 6k±1+8 = 6k+9 or 6k+7
and x+2a = 6k±1+16 = 6k±15 or 6k±17
As we can see, the numbers are not of the form 6k±1. Therefore, a cannot be 8
Option c: 4:-
If a = 4, then x+a = 6k±1+4 = 6k+5 or 6k+3
and x+2a = 6k±1+8 = 6k±7 or 6k±9
The numbers are not of the form 6k±1 and hence, a cannot be 4
Option d:- 5:-
5 is not possible as we know all prime numbers above 101 are odd.
Hence, option A is the correct answer.

A table is sold at 20% profit from a manufacturer to a whole seller. 
Price of the table for the whole seller =1.2 M
The whole seller sold the tables at 60% profit, with an offer of 1 table free with a purchase of 5 tables. 
Price of 5 tables for the whole seller =  1.2 M * 5= 6M
The retailer bought 30 tables {free tables included} at Rs 24000.
Price of 6 tables( +1 free) for retailer = 1.6*6M=  9.6M
Price of 30 tables = 5* 9.6M = 24000
M= Rs 500
Price of each table for Retailer = 24000/30= Rs 800
Price for the customers= 1.1*800= Rs 880
The difference between the manufacturing cost and the customer price of the table= Rs 880-Rs 500= Rs380

questions.question_text: Find the sum upto 20 terms of the series: 6, 7, 10, 15, 22, 31….
questions.solution_text:
For the given series, the differences between two consecutive terms become equal at the second level. So, each term of the series is of the form $f(x)=ax^2+bx+c$
Now, $f(1)=a+b+c$
=> $a+b+c=6$ ___(1)
$f(2)=4a+2b+c$
=> $4a+2b+c=7$ ____(2)
$f(3)=9a+3b+c$
=> $9a+3b+c=10$ ____(3)
On subtracting (2) from (3) we get
$5a+b=3$ ___(4)
Similarly, on subtracting (1) from (2) we get
$3a+b=1$ ___(5)
On subtracting (5) from (4) we get
$2a=2$ => $a=1$
So, we have $b=-2$ and $c=7$
$\therefore$ $f(x)=x^2-2x+7$
Now, $\sum f(x) = \sum (x^2-2x+7)=\frac{x(x+1)(2x+1)}{6}-\frac{2x(x+1)}{2}+7x$
=> $\sum f(x)=\frac{x(x+1)(2x-5)}{6}+7x$
$\therefore$ $\sum f(20)=\frac{20\times21\times35}{6}+7\times20=2590$
Hence, option D is the correct answer.

questions.question_text: Find the number of integers satisfying $4 < ||x-5|+4| < 10$ ?

=> $-1< x < 5$

questions.question_text: A milkman bought 15 litres of milk and mixed it with 3 litres of mineral water (which is not free). He claims to his customers, who do not know about mixing, that he is making a profit of 10% only. However, his actual profit is 20%. What is the ratio of the cost of milk/litre and water/litre.
questions.solution_text:
Let the CP of milk be Rs. 100/litre
As he is claiming 10% profit, SP of the total mixture = Rs. [(15 + 3) * 110] = Rs. 1980
Actual profit = 20%
Let actual CP be Rs. x. 
Then, x + 20% of x = Rs. 1980
Solving for x, we get x = Rs. 1650
So, Actual CP = Total CP of milk + Total CP of water
Or, Total CP of water = Rs. 1650 - (15 * 100) = Rs. 150
Or, CP of water = Rs. 50/litre
Required ratio = 100:50 = 2:1
Hence, option C is correct.

questions.question_text: A broken clock loses 45 seconds in 3 minutes, while another damaged clock gains 30 seconds in 6 minutes. Both clocks were set right at 9 AM in the morning. What will be the absolute value of the difference in the angle made by the minute and hour hand of the two clocks on the next day at 3 PM?
questions.solution_text:
The first clock loses 45 seconds in 3 minutes or 15 minutes an hour while the second clock gains 30 seconds in 6 minutes or 5 minutes per hour. In the next 30 hours (from 9 AM to 3 PM the next day), the first clock would have lost 7 hours 30 minutes, while the second clock would have gained 2 hours 30 minutes. Thus, at 3 PM, the first clock would show the time as 7:30 AM, while the second will display 5:30 PM.
The angle between the hour hand (H) and minute hand (M) = $ \theta\ =\left | 30H-\frac{11}{2}M \right |$ ; for the first clock  $\theta\ =45^{\circ\ }$ while for the second clock $\theta\ =15^{\circ\ }$
The absolute difference of the values = $30^{\circ\ }$
Hence, Option A is the correct choice.

questions.question_text:
Ram and Shyam are running on different circular tracks. In the time that Ram completes 4 rounds of his track, Shyam completes 3 rounds of his track. 
If Ram and Shyam interchange their tracks the time taken by both of them to complete 1 round is same. What is the ratio of speeds of Ram and Shyam?
questions.solution_text:
Let the radius of Ram’s track be a and that of Shyam’s track be b.
In the time that Ram travels 4 rounds, Shyam travels 3 rounds so
Distance travelled by Ram in 4 rounds = 4*2πa 
Distance travelled by Shyam in 3 rounds = 3*2πb, So if both of them take same time then the ratio of their speeds is given by
$\frac{\textrm{speed of Ram}}{\textrm{Speed of Shyam}} = \frac{4*2πa }{3*2πb} = \frac{4a}{3b}$ (I)
Now when they interchange their tracks
They cover 1 round in same time, so we have
$\frac{\textrm{speed of Ram}}{\textrm{Speed of Shyam}} = \frac{2πb }{2πa} = \frac{b}{a}$ (II)
So we have $\frac{4a}{3b} = \frac{b}{a} $
=> $ \frac{a^{2}}{b^{2}} = \frac{3}{4}$
=> $\frac{a}{b} =\sqrt{\frac{3}{4}}$
Putting this value in equation II, we get
$\frac{\textrm{speed of Ram}}{\textrm{Speed of Shyam}}$ = $\sqrt{\frac{4}{3}}$

questions.question_text: Point B is taken at random in a circle of radius r units. Let x be the distance of the point B from the centre and y be the shortest distance of B from the circle's circumference. What is the probability that x$\ge\ $2y?
questions.solution_text:
The distance of the point B from the centre is of x units. The distance of the point from the nearest point on the circle will be (r-x) units, where r is the length of the radius. 
It is given that $x\ge2\left(r-x\right)\ $
=>$x\ge2r-2x\ $
=>$3x\ge2r\ $
=>$x\ge\ \frac{\ 2r}{3}$
Now, the point selected at random must lie anywhere between the two circle (the region which is not coloured), because the boundary of the blue circle is the minimum distance of the point from the circle. 
So, area of the unshaded region= $\pi\ r^2-\pi\ x^2=\pi\ \left(r^2-\frac{4r^2}{9}\right)=\ \frac{\ 5\pi\ r^2}{9}$
The sample space can be the entire circle with radius r units, which is $\pi\ r^2$
Therefore, required probability= $\ \frac{\ 5\pi\ r^2}{9\pi\ r^2}=\ \frac{\ 5}{9}$

questions.question_text: It takes 1 pipe of type A, 2 pipes of type B and 2 pipes of type C to fill an empty tank completely in 3 hours. Instead, if 2 pipes of type A and 1 pipe of type B are used as inlets, and 1 pipe of type C is used as an outlet, the tank is filled in 12 hours. What will be the time taken to fill the tank using 5 pipes of type A and 4 pipes of type B all used as inlets?
questions.solution_text:
Assuming the flow rate of pipe A, pipe B and pipe C is a, b and c respectively and the capacity of the tank is A units.
Then, 3(a+2b+2c) = A
=> a+2b+2c = $\frac{A}{3}$.......(1)
Also, 12(2a+b-c) = A
=> 2a+b-c = $\frac{A}{12}$ ......(2)
Now,  the combined flow rate of 5 pipes of type A and 4 pipes of type B = 5a+4b
(a+2b+2c)*3 = (2a+b-c )*12
6c = 7a+2b
Let x be the number of days taken by 5 pipes of type A and 4 pipes of type B all used as inlets to fill the tank
(5a+4b) * x = (a+2b+2c)*3
(5a+4b)*x= 10a+8b
x = 2
So, time taken to fill A completely = 2 hours

$ 3\times(x-n)=(y-n)$
$ 4\times(x-2n)=(y-2n)$

questions.question_text: The sum of the numerical values of the perimeter and area of a rectangle is 140. The perimeter of the rectangle is at least
questions.solution_text:
Let the sides of the triangle be $x$ and $y$
It is given that,
$2(x + y) + xy = 140$
Adding $4$ to both sides of the equation
$2x + 2y + xy + 4 = 144$
or,  $x(2 + y) + 2 (y + 2) = 144$
or,  $(x + 2)(y + 2) = 144$
Applying AM $\geq $ GM
$\dfrac{(x + 2) + (y + 2)}{2} \geq \sqrt{(x + 2)(y + 2)}$
Replacing the value of $(x + 2)(y + 2)$ by $144$ , we get
$\dfrac{(x + 2) + (y + 2)}{2} \geq \sqrt{144}$
or,  $(x + y + 4) \geq 24$
or,  $(x + y) \geq 20$
=>  $2(x + y) \geq 40$
Thus, the perimeter of the rectangle is at least $40$ units.
Hence, option C is the correct answer.

At first we select c1, c2, c3, c4, c5 and then we can arrange them in 5! ways.

So, we can select the chocolates in 26 ways and then arrange each in 5! ways.
Total no. of permutations = 26 x 5! ways.

questions.question_text: Kapre is standing 1500 meters away from the base of the tree such that his line of sight towards the top of the tree makes an angle of 30 degrees with the ground. Suddenly, the tree starts growing at 5 meters per second. Kapre starts running towards the tree at a speed of 10 meters per second, and after how many seconds does his angle of sight towards the top of the tree make 60 degrees with the ground?
questions.solution_text:
Initially:
Let BT be the tree, K is the position of Kapre => BK = 1500m and Angle BKT = 30 degrees.
$Tan\left(30\right)=\dfrac{BT}{BK}=\dfrac{BT}{1500}$ => $BT=\dfrac{1500}{\sqrt{\ 3}}=500\sqrt{\ 3}$
After 't' seconds, the height of the tree becomes $500\sqrt{\ 3}+5t$, and Kapre travels a distance of 10t => The final configuration looks like this:
Here BT = $500\sqrt{\ 3}+5t$ and BK = 1500 - 10t and Angle BKT = 60 degrees.
Now, $Tan\left(60\right)=\dfrac{BT}{BK}=\dfrac{\left(500\sqrt{\ 3}+5t\right)}{1500-10t}$
=> $1500\sqrt{\ 3}-10\sqrt{\ 3}t=500\sqrt{\ 3}+5t$
=> $300\sqrt{\ 3}-2\sqrt{\ 3}t=100\sqrt{\ 3}+t$
=> $t=\dfrac{200\sqrt{\ 3}}{\left(2\sqrt{\ 3}+1\right)}=\dfrac{\left(1200-200\sqrt{\ 3}\right)}{11}$ seconds.

=> $\dfrac{\left(25\right)^{16\times\ 32^{95}}}{13}$
=> $\dfrac{\left(-1\right)^{16\times\ 32^{95}}}{13}$ (25 when divided by 13, leaves a remainder of -1.
Since the power of -1 is even ($16\times\ 32^{95}$ is an even number, as 2 power any number is always even)
=>$\dfrac{\left(1\right)^{16\times\ 32^{95}}}{13}$
=> Therefore, the remainder is 1 
Thus, the answer is option C

questions.question_text: There are three friends: Aman, Bablu and Charan. Aman's age is one-third of that of Bablu, and Bablu's age is twice that of Charan. If the average age of Aman and Bablu is two less than the average age of Bablu and Charan, what is the sum of the ages of all three friends?

Let us assume Bablu is 'x' years old.
=> Age of Aman is x/3 and Age of Charan is x/2.
Average age of Aman and Bablu is $\dfrac{\left(\dfrac{x}{3}+x\right)}{2}=\dfrac{2x}{3}$
Average age of Bablu and Charan is $\dfrac{\left(\frac{x}{2}+x\right)}{2}=\dfrac{3x}{4}$
Given that $2+\dfrac{2x}{3}=\dfrac{3x}{4}$
=> $\dfrac{3x}{4}-\frac{2x}{3}=\frac{x}{12}=2$ => x = 24 years.
Required sum of ages = 24 + 24/3 + 24/2 = 24 + 8 + 12 = 44 years

questions.solution_text:
Let us assume Length and breadth of the rectangle to be L and B respectively.
Let the speed of Trains A and B be 3S and S respectively.
Since Both the trains have arrived at the same time, we can say that distance covered by them upon their respective speed should be equal.
Distance covered by A = 12 *(L +B) + L
Distance covered by B = 4(L+B) + B
$\ \ \frac{\ 13L+12B\ \ }{3S}$ = $\ \ \frac{\ 4L+5B\ \ }{S}$
13L + 12B = 12L + 15B
L= 3B
Hence, Option A is the correct answer.

questions.question_text:
Mr. Khanna owns an electronics shop. To boost his sales, he decided to offer a 30% discount on each TV. 
Additionally, he offered one free TV for every three TVs purchased to clear out his stock. 
Find the price above the cost price at which the TV was marked (in 
percentage) if he made an overall profit of 32% in selling the entire 
stock of TVs.
questions.solution_text:
Let the cost price of a TV be x
Cost price is the amount Mr Khanna pays to buy a TV from the manufacturer or supplier.
He made a profit of 32%
This means the selling price (SP) is 32% more than the cost price (x). 
So, SP = 1.32x. He's selling each TV for 1.32 times the cost price.
Now, he sells 4 TVs for every 3 TVs
Here, Mr. Khanna decides to offer a deal: for every three TVs a customer buys, they get an extra TV for free. This is essentially a 25% discount on the price of one TV because you're getting 4 TVs for the price of 3. 
(SP)(1-0.25) = 1.32x
SP = 1.76x
Now, a discount of 25% was given
This means Mr Khanna applies a 25% discount to the marked price (M.P) of the TV before selling it.
M.P * 0.70 = 1.76x
M.P = 2.51x
Therefore, (2.51x - x) / x * 100 = 151.4%
So, the marked price is 151.4% above the cost price. This means that Mr Khanna set the price of the TV to be 151.4% higher than what it cost him to buy it.

Assuming P, Q. R and S be the number of residents who got 1, 2, 3, and 4 types of newspapers, respectively.

Also, P+2Q+3R+4S = 60%+65%+70%+75% = 270% 
P=20% ( Percentage of residents who get exactly one newspaper)
2Q+3R+4S = 250% 
Q+R+S = 80%
To maximize the percentage of residents who received exactly three types of newspapers, we will assume Q = 0
=> 3R+4S = 250% and R+S = 80%
=> R = 70% and S = 10% 
Thus the maximum percentage of residents who received exactly three newspapers= 70%

questions.question_text: In an Arithmetic Progression, nth term of the series is 'p' and (2n-1)th term of the series is 'q'. Which of the following represents (4n-3)rd term of the series?
questions.solution_text:
Let us consider the Arithmetic progression whose first term is 'a' and the common difference is 'd'.
Given that nth term of the progression is 'p'
=> $a+\left(n-1\right)d=p$ ----(1)
Also given that (2n-1)th term of the progression is 'q'
=> $a+\left(2n-1-1\right)d=q=>a+2\left(n-1\right)d=q$ ----(2)
(2) - (1)
=> $\left(n-1\right)\left(d\right)=q-p$ => $d=\dfrac{q-p}{n-1}$
Substituting in (1), we get a = p + (p-q) = 2p - q.
T(4n-3) = a + (4n-3-1)*d = $2p-q+\dfrac{4\left(n-1\right)\left(q-p\right)}{n-1}=2p-q+4q-4p=3q-2p$

=> $x^2-10x+16<0$
=> $\left(x-2\right)\left(x-8\right)<0$
=> 2 < x < 8 -----(2)
From (1) and (2), the common values of x are 3, 6, 7. => Required sum = 3 + 6 + 7 = 16.

What is the average age of the employees in the Marketing and Tech departments combined?
questions.solution_text:
Let the number of employees in Sales, Marketing and Tech departments be S, M and T respectively.
The average age of employees in Sales = 50 years
The average age of employees in Marketing = 40 years
The average age of employees in Tech = 42 years
Also, the average age of employees of Sales and Tech department = 38 kg
=> Total age of employees of Sales and Tech departments = 50S  + 42T = 48(S+T)
=> 50S + 42T = 48S + 48T 
=> 2S = 6T
=> S:T =3:1
Similarly, the average weight of employees from all three departments = 45 kg
=>Total age of employees of all departments = 50S + 40M + 42T = 45(S+M+T)
=> 50S + 40M + 42T = 45S + 45M + 45T
=> 5S = 5M + 3T   (S = 3T)
=> 5S = 5M + S
=> 4S = 5M
=> S:M = 5:4
Therefore, S:M: T = 15:12:5
The average age of the marketing and tech department = $\dfrac{\left(40\times\ 12\right)+\left(42\times\ 5\right)}{17}=\dfrac{690}{17}$

questions.question_text: If x and y are two real numbers such that $x^5y^7=1$, what is the value of the expression $\dfrac{1+\log_x\left(x^4y^5\right)}{3+\log_y\left(x^6y^5\right)}$ ?
questions.solution_text:
Given that $x^5y^7=1$
Taking logarithm to the base x on both sides, and using the relation - $\log\left(xy\right)=\log x+\log y$, we get
$\log_xx^5+\log_xy^7=0$
$5+7\log_xy=0$
$\log_xy=-\dfrac{5}{7}$ => $\log_yx=-\dfrac{7}{5}$
Simplifying the given expression, we get:
$\dfrac{1+\log_xx^4+\log_xy^5}{3+\log_yy^5+\log_yx^6}=\dfrac{1+4+5\left(-\frac{5}{7}\right)}{3+5+6\left(-\frac{7}{5}\right)}=-\dfrac{25}{7}$

questions.question_text: In a right angled triangle, if one of the angles is $30^{\circ\ }$, find the ratio of inradius to circumradius.
questions.solution_text:
It is given that the triangle is right-angled, and one angle is $30^{\circ\ }$.
The another angle will be $60^{\circ\ }$
In $30^{\circ},\ 60^{\circ}\ \&\ 90^{\circ}$ triangle, the sides will be in the form $x,\ \sqrt{\ 3}x\ \&\ 2x$, where $x$ is a constant.
Inradius, r = $\frac{ \text{sum of perpendicular sides - Hypotenuse}}{2}\ =\frac{x+\sqrt{\ 3}x-2x}{2}$
=$\frac{\sqrt{\ 3}x-x}{2}$.....(1)
Circumradius, R = $\frac{Length\ of\ hypotenuse}{2}=\frac{2x}{2}=x$
Hence the ratio, $\frac{r}{R}=\frac{\frac{\sqrt{\ 3}x-x}{2}}{x}=\frac{\sqrt{\ 3}-1}{2}$
The answer is option D.

questions.question_text: 15 men can complete a work in 108 days. 12 women will take 60 days to do the same work. How many days do 6 men and 4 women will take to complete $\frac{3}{4}th$ of the work.
questions.solution_text:
Let the amount of work be 'W'.
Let the amount of work done by one man in a day be 'm' and by a woman in one day be 'n'.
From the given information,
$W=15m\times\ 108$...............(1)
$W=12n\times\ 60$.................(2)
Equating (1) and (2), we get
$15m\times\ 108=12n\times\ 60$
$9m=4w$.....(3)
Let the time taken by 6 men & 4 women to complete three-fourths of work be 'x'.
$\left(6m+4w\right)\times\ x=\frac{3W}{4}$
$\left(6m+9m\right)x=\frac{3W}{4}$        From EQ(3)
$\left(15m\right)x=\frac{3}{4}\times\ W$
$\left(15m\right)x=\frac{3}{4}\times\ 15m\times\ 108$
$x=81$
The answer is Option (B).

questions.question_text: What is the ratio of the number of diagonals in a polygon of 18 sides to the number of diagonals in a polygon of 24 sides?
questions.solution_text:
The number of diagonals in a polygon with 'n' sides = $\frac{n\left(n-3\right)}{2}$ 
Therefore, the number of diagonals in a polygon with 18 sides = $\frac{18\left(18-3\right)}{2}=135$ and the number of diagonals in a polygon with 24 sides = $\frac{24\left(24-3\right)}{2}=252$ 
Required ratio = 135:252 = 15:28
The answer is option D

questions.question_text: Surbhi took a loan of an amount 'P' for 3 years at a 20% compound interest rate per annum. Rs. 14,400 is the instalment paid at the end of each year, starting from the first year. Find the value of the loan amount 'P'. (Approx value)
questions.solution_text:
It is given that an annual installment of Rs 14,400 is paid, and the compound interest rate is 20%.
Instalment paid after one year of Rs 14,400 would grow to $14400\left(1.20\right)^2$ at the end of three years.
Similarly, Instalment paid after two years of Rs 14,400 would amount to $14400\left(1.20\right)$ at the end of three years.
Now, let's consider that an amount 'P' is taken as a loan for three years.
The final amount at the end of three years can be expressed as $P\left(1.20\right)^3$.
So, we have the equation:
$14400\times\ \left(1.20\right)^2+14400\times\ 1.20\ +14400\ =\ P\times\ \left(1.20\right)^3$
Simplifying, we get:
$14400\ \times\ \ \frac{91}{25}=P\ \times\ \frac{216}{125}$. 
Solving this equation yields P = Rs 30,333.33
Therefore, the answer is 30333

questions.question_text: Six concentric circles are drawn whose circumferences are in the ratio of 3:4:7:9:11:16. What is the ratio of the area of the third innermost circle to the fifth innermost circle?
questions.solution_text:
It is given that six concentric circles are drawn whose circumferences are in the ratio of 3:4:7:9:11:16, which implies $2\pi r_1:2\pi r_2:2\pi r_3:2\pi r_4:2\pi r_5:2\pi r_6=3:4:7:9:11:16\ =>r_1:r_2:r_3:r_4:r_5:r_6=3:4:7:9:11:16$
Therefore, $r_1:r_2:r_3:r_4:r_5:r_6=3:4:7:9:11:16\ =>r_1^2:r_2^2:r_3^2:r_4^2:r_5^2:r_6^2=9:16:49:81:121:256$
We know that the area of a circle is $\pi r^2$, which implies the ratio of their area will be the same as the ratio of $r_1^2:r_2^2:r_3^2:r_4^2:r_5^2:r_6^2=9:16:49:81:121:256$
Hence, the ratio of the third innermost circle to the fifth innermost circle is 49:121
The correct option is C.

questions.question_text: There are two friends, Arun and Balu, who sell fridges. Both friends bought a fridge from the same manufacturer. It is known that the manufacturer gives a discount of $30\%$ to Arun and $40\%$ to Balu. Arun and Balu mark up the prices by $50\%$ and $60\%$, respectively, while selling them to the final customer. Suppose it is known that the difference between the prices at which the customers bought the fridges from the two friends is Rs. 720, Find the price at which Arun purchased the fridge from the manufacturer.
questions.solution_text:
Let the selling price of the manufacturer be 'c'.
The prices at which he sells it to Arun and Balu will be $\dfrac{7c}{10}$ and $\dfrac{6c}{10}$ respectively.
It is given that they mark up the prices by 50% and 60%, Therefore their selling prices will be $\dfrac{150}{100}\times\ \dfrac{7c}{10}=\dfrac{21c}{20}$ and $\dfrac{160}{100}\times\ \dfrac{6c}{10}=\dfrac{24c}{25}$ respectively.
The difference between them is Rs. 720/-
=> $\dfrac{21c}{20}-\dfrac{24c}{25}=720$ => c = Rs. 8000/-
Therefore Arun purchased the fridge for $\dfrac{7c}{10}=\dfrac{7}{10}\times\ 8000=5600$.

questions.question_text: Ram borrowed a certain amount from Shyam at a compound interest of a% for the first year and b% for the second year. Shyam noticed that the total interest he gets after two years is twice the interest he gets after one year. Find the value of $\frac{1}{b}-\frac{1}{a}.$
questions.solution_text:
Let the amount borrowed by Ram = P
The interest earned on P after 1 year =  $\frac{Pa}{100}$
The interest earned on P after 2 years =$P(1+\frac{a}{100})(1+\frac{b}{100})-P$ 
= $P\left(1+\frac{b}{100}+\frac{a}{100}+\frac{ab}{10000}-1\right)$
=$P\left(\frac{b}{100}+\frac{a}{100}+\frac{ab}{10000}\right)$
It is given that interest earned after two years is equal to twice the interest earned after the first year.
$P\left(\frac{b}{100}+\frac{a}{100}+\frac{ab}{10000}\right)=\frac{2Pa}{100}$
$\frac{b}{100}+\frac{a}{100}+\frac{ab}{10000}=\frac{2a}{100}$
$\frac{ab}{10000}=\frac{a}{100}-\frac{b}{100}$
$\frac{1}{b}-\frac{1}{a}=\frac{1}{100}$
The answer is Option (C)

questions.question_text: A drum contains 75 litres of water. 15 litres of the water is removed and substituted with milk. The least number of such substitutions so that milk is at least 50% of the solution?
questions.solution_text:
We know that if a container has 'a' litres of liquid A and if 'b' litres of the solution is withdrawn and is replaced with an equal volume of another liquid B and the operation is repeated for 'n' times, then after nth operation,
Final quantity of liquid A in the container = $\left(\ \frac{\ a-b}{a}\right)^{n\ }\times\ a$
a - initial quantity, b - quantity replaced
In this question, a = 75 and b = 15 
It is given, the final quantity of water should be less than or equal to 50% (since the final quantity of milk in the solution is at least 50%). 
We need to find the value of n when 
$\left(\ \frac{\ 75-15}{75}\right)^{n\ }\times\ 75\ \le\ 75\times\left(\ \frac{\ 1}{2}\right)$
$\left(\frac{4}{5}\right)^{n\ }\le\frac{1}{2}$
$n = 4$
The answer is 4.

questions.question_text: In a parallelogram ABCD of 189 sq cm, CD and AD sides have 21 cm and 15 cm lengths, respectively. Let R be a point on CD such that AR is perpendicular to CD. Find the area, in sq cm, of triangle ARD.
questions.solution_text:
Area of parallelogram ABCD = 189 sq cm  = $CD\ \times\ \ AR$. 
It is given that the length of CD = 21 cm. Let's assume that the length of AR = x cm. 
Therefore, $21\times\ x\ =21x\ =\ 189\ =>\ x\ =\ 9$ cm.
In right-angled ARD, $AR^2+RD^2=AD^2\ =>\ 9^2+RD^2=15^2$ (since the length of AD = 15 cm)
RD = 12 cm. 
The area of the right-angled triangle ARD = $\ \frac{\ 1}{2}\times\ AR\ \times\ RD\ =\ \frac{1}{2}\times\ 9\times\ 12\ =54$ sq cm.
The answer is option B.

questions.question_text: Find the number of integers that do not satisfy the inequality $\dfrac{1}{2\left|x\right|-5}<\dfrac{3}{16}$
questions.solution_text:
We need to solve the inequality to find the values of x for which the inequality is valid.
$\dfrac{1}{2\left|x\right|-5}-\dfrac{3}{16}<0$
$\dfrac{\left(16-6x+15\right)}{\left(2x-5\right)\left(16\right)}<0$
$\frac{\left(31-6\left|x\right|\right)}{16\left(2\left|x\right|-5\right)}<0$
Either the numerator is positive and the denominator is negative, or vice versa, for the whole term is negative
=> 31-6|x| > 0 and 2|x|-5 < 0 or 31-6|x| < 0 and 2|x|-5 > 0
=> |x| < 5/2 or |x| > 31/6
Therefore the values of x for which the inequality is valid is $\left(-\inf,-\dfrac{31}{6}\right)\ U\ \left(-\dfrac{5}{2},\dfrac{5}{2}\right)\ U\ \left(\dfrac{31}{6},+\inf\right)$.
The only integers absent from the range are 3, 4, 5 and -3, -4, -5 => 6 integers.

questions.question_text: A shopkeeper purchases rice at a certain price and marks it up by 68%. However, a customer requests a discount of 75%. The shopkeeper realises he can take advantage of this situation to make a 20% profit by using false weights. To achieve this profit margin, what percentage decrease in weight should he manipulate?
questions.solution_text:
Let the cost price of rice be Rs. 100 per kg 
Then, marked up price of rice = $\ 100\times\left(1+\ \frac{68}{100}\right)$ = Rs. 168 per kg
Now, the customer is demanding a discount of 75% 
So total price of rice per kg after giving discount = $\ 168\times\left(1-\ \frac{75}{100}\right)$ = Rs. 42 per kg
But he will be at a loss if he sells at this price.
Therefore, the shopkeeper uses a false weight to gain a 20% profit.
Let the actual quantity he sold to the customer be y kg to gain a profit of 20%
The cost price of y kg rice = Rs. 100y
The selling price is 20% more than the cost price of y kg rice = $100y\left(1+\ \frac{20\ }{100}\right)$ = Rs.120y
It is given that 120y is equal to Rs 42
Therefore, y = $\ \frac{42}{120}$ = 0.35 kg
Therefore, the weight of rice should be decreased by 65%.
The answer is option A.

questions.question_text: Train A starts from city M to city N, and after one hour, train B also starts from city M towards city N. Train B takes 20 minutes to reach city N after crossing train A. Train A arrives at city N 10 minutes after train B's arrival. If the speed (in km/hr) of both the trains are integers, which of the following can be the distance between city M and city N?
questions.solution_text:
Let the distance between cities M and N be 'd' km, and the speeds of train A & train B be 'a' kmph and 'b' kmph, respectively.
Let two trains meet after d-x.
Train B travels x in 20 min.
$\frac{x}{b}=\frac{20}{60}=\frac{1}{3}$......(1)
Train A reaches N 10 minutes after B. Hence A takes 30 min to travel x km.
$\frac{x}{a}=\frac{30}{60}=\frac{1}{2}$......(2)
From Eq(1) and Eq(2) we get, $\frac{a}{b}=\frac{2}{3}$....(3)
$\frac{d-x}{a}=1+\frac{d-x}{b}$
$\frac{d}{a}-\frac{d}{b}=1+\frac{x}{a}-\frac{x}{b}$
$\frac{d}{a}-\frac{d}{b}=1+\frac{1}{2}-\frac{1}{3}$
$\frac{d}{a}-\frac{d}{b}=\frac{7}{6}$
Let a = 2k then b = 3k
$\frac{d}{2k}-\frac{d}{3k}=\frac{7}{6}$
$d=7k$
The distance 'd' is a multiple of 7. 
From the options, only option B satisfies the condition.
The answer is option B.

questions.question_text: Two regular polygons, P1 and P2, with x and y sides, respectively. Suppose it is given that y = 2x and each interior angle of polygon P2 is $\ \frac{5}{4}$ times each interior angle of polygon P1. In that case, the value of each interior angle in degrees of a regular polygon with 2x+y sides is?
questions.solution_text:
Interior angle of a n sided polygon is given by = $\ \frac{\left(n-2\right)\times\ 180}{n}$
P1 is of x sides so interior angle of x sided polygon will be 
=> $\ \frac{\left(x-2\right)\times\ 180}{x}$  ------ equation(1)
P2 is of y sides so interior angle of y sided polygon will be
=> $\ \frac{\left(y-2\right)\times\ 180}{y}$  ------ equation(2)
It is given that each interior angle of polygon P2 is $\ \frac{5}{4}$ times each interior angle of polygon P1
Thus, $\ \frac{\left(y-2\right)\times\ 180}{y}$ = $\ \frac{5}{4}$ $\ \frac{\left(x-2\right)\times\ 180}{x}$
=> $4xy-8x\ =\ 5xy\ -10y$ --------equation(3)
=> $xy-10y+8x\ =0$ (It is given that $y\ =2x$)
=> Putting values of y in equation (3)
=> $2x\left(x-6\right)=0$ 
Thus, $x\ =\ 6\ $ and $y\ =\ 12$
Therefore, interior angle of a polygon with $2x+y$ sides (24 sides)
=> $\ \frac{\left(n-2\right)\times\ 180}{n}$ 
=> $\ \frac{\left(22\right)\times\ 180}{24}$ = 165 degrees
The answer is option D.

questions.question_text: The cost of fish varies directly as the cube of its weight. If the fish is cut into three pieces with weights in the ratio of 2:2:1, then the fishmonger will get 43200 rupees less after selling all the pieces. Find the original price (in rupees) of the whole fish.
questions.solution_text:
Let the weight of the pieces of fish be 2x,2x, and x kg, respectively. 
The weight of the whole fish is (2x+2x+x) = 5x kg. 
Let the cost of the whole fish be C.
It is given, the cost of fish varies directly as the cube of its weight.
Therefore, the cost of the whole fish $C=k\left(5x\right)^3\ =>\ 125kx^3$ 
Similarly,
The cost of the first piece $\left(C_1\right)$ = $k\left(2x\right)^3\ = 8kx^3$
The cost of the second piece $\left(C_2\right)$ = $8kx^3$
The cost of the third piece $\left(C_3\right)$ = $kx^3$
The cost of the whole fish after cutting it into pieces will be = $8kx^3+8kx^3+kx^3\ =17kx^3$ 
It is given that,
$125kx^3-17kx^3=43200$
$108kx^3$ = 43200 
Therefore, $kx^3$ = 400
The original cost of whole fish = $125kx^3$ = 125*400 = 50000
The answer is 50000.

questions.question_text: If 17 men and 14 women can do a piece of work in 12 days and 6 men and 3 women do the same piece of work in 40 days. If there are n women and n-1 men working together, they can complete the work in 20 days. Find the value of n.
questions.solution_text:
Let the work done by men be = m units/ day and work done by women be = w units/day
Work done by 17 men and 14 women in one day = 17m+14w
Work done by 17 men and 14 women in 12 days = 12*(17m+14w)   ------equation(1)
Similarly, work done by 6 men and 3 women in 40 days = 40*(6m+3w) -------equation(2)
Equating both equations - 12*(17m+14w) = 40*(6m+3w)
=> 51m+42w = 60m+30w
=> 12w = 9m
Let work done by one men be "4 units/day" , work done by one women will be "3 units/day"
Total amount of work = 12*(17*4+14*3) = 1320 units
If n women and n-1 men work for 20 days, work done by them 
=>20*[3*(n)+4*(n-1)] = 1320
=> 7n-4 = 66
=> 7n = 70
Therefore, n = 10
10 Women and 9 men can complete the work in 20 days.

questions.question_text: There are five integers which are in arithmetic progression. It is given that the sum of terms is 45 and the product of the terms is 45045. Which of the following is not part of the progression?
questions.solution_text:
Let the terms in A.P. be a-2d, a-d, a, a+d, a+2d.
Sum of the terms = 5a = 45 => a = 9.
Therefore, 9-2d, 9-d, 9, 9+d and 9+2d are the terms.
Given, product of terms = 9*(9-d)*(9+d)*(9-2d)*(9+2d) = 45045.
=> $\left(81-d^2\right)\left(81-4d^2\right)=$ = 5005
=> $4d^4-405d^2+1556=0$
Using the formula to find roots of the quadratic equation, we get$\frac{\left(405\ \pm\ \sqrt{\ 405^2-4\cdot4\cdot1556}\right)}{2\cdot4}$
=> $d^2=4\ or\ \frac{389}{4}$, we only consider d = 2 as it is given that the terms are integers.
Therefore, the terms in A.P. are 5, 7, 9, 11, 13.

questions.question_text: If 4 kg of pure nickel is combined with a certain amount of nickel and chromium alloy A1, the resulting alloy A2 will contain 80% nickel by weight. New alloy A3 will contain 72% nickel by weight if alloy A1 is combined with 4 kg of another alloy A4 that contains 80% nickel by weight. Find the weight of alloy A1(in kg) used to form alloy A2.
questions.solution_text:
Let the amount of nickel and chromium in the alloy(A1) be $x$ kg  and $y$ kg respectively,
When 4 kg pure nickel is mixed, resulting alloy(A2) contain 80% nickel by weight
=> $\ \frac{\ x+4}{x+y+4}=\ \frac{8}{10}$
=>$10x+40=8x+8y+32$
=> $x$ = 4$y$-4
The same initial mixture of nickel and chromium alloy (A1) when mixed with 4 kg of alloy(A3) that contain 80 % nickel we get alloy(A4)
=> $\ \frac{\ x+\left(4\times\ .8\right)}{x+y+4}=\ \frac{72}{100}$
=>$100x+320=\ 72x+72y+288$
=>$28x+32\ =\ 72y$
=> 7$x$+8 = 18$y$
Putting the value of $x$=4$y$-4
=> 28$y$-20 = 18$y$
=> $y$=2, and $x$=4
Alloy(A1) contains $x$ kg nickel and $y$ kg chromium   
$\therefore\ $ $x$+$y$ = 6

questions.question_text: In the following figure, AB is the diameter, MT is the tangent to the circle touching at B, and the radius of the circle is 5m. Find the length of AC.

$\angle\ ABT=\angle\ ABC+\angle\ CBT$
$90^{\circ\ }=\angle\ ABC+60^{\circ\ }$
$\angle\ ABC=30^{\circ\ }$.

$\frac{1}{2}=\frac{AC}{10}$
$\text{AC}\ =\ 5\ m$

questions.question_text: Sourabh had sufficient money to purchase 24 bottles of orange juice or 18 bottles of mango juice, or 12 bottles of milk. Find the maximum number of bottles of orange juice he purchased if he purchased exactly two milk bottles, at least one mango juice and spent all the money left.

He retains 16.66% of the total funds for transportation costs, which is equal to = 1/6 *72 =12 rupees. The remaining fund = (72-12)=60 rupees.
If he purchased exactly two milk bottles, the cost = 6 *2 =12 rupees
The funds left with him to purchase orange juice = 60 - 12 = 48 rupees.
Let the number of mango juices and orange juices bought be x and y, respectively.
4x + 3y = 48
Minimum value of x can take is 1.
y takes a integer values, only when x = 3
x = 3 and y = 12
Therefore, the maximum number of bottles of orange juice he can purchase is 12.

$\angle $BEC$-\angle\ $DBE$=\left(70\ +\ x\right)-x=70^{\circ\ }$
 The answer is option A.

questions.solution_text:
Given that, the roots of the quadratic equation $\ x^2-px+q\ =0$ are in the ratio of 2:5
Let the roots be 2$k$ and 5$k$, respectively.
Then, 2$k$+5$k$ = $\frac{p\ }{1}$ = $p\ =$7$k$  (sum of roots)

It is given that the maximum value of $20p-q-480$ is $\alpha\ $
putting values of $p,\ q$ in the equation
=> 20(7$k$)-10$k^2$-480
=>140$k$-10$k^2$-480 
=> 10(14$k$-1$k^2$-48)
=> $-10\left(k^2-14k+48\right)$
=> $-10\left[\left(k-7\right)^2-1\right]$
=> $-10\left(k-7\right)^2+10$ (This will be maximum when $\left(k-7\right)^2$ will be equal to zero.
Therefore, the maximum value of the $20p-q-480$ is $\alpha\ $ = 10
Alternate explanation -

=> 14$k$-1$k^2$-48
As the equation formed is a quadratic equation with the coefficient of $k$ as negative, the maxima occur at $k$ = $\ \frac{-b\ }{2a}$ and the maximum value is given by $\ \frac{-D}{4a}$
=> $D={\left(14\right)^2-4\left(-1\right)\left(-48\right)}$
=> $D={196-192}$ = $D=4$
=> $\frac{-D\ }{4a}=\ \frac{-4\ }{4\left(-1\right)}=1$
The maximum value of  14$k$-1$k^2$-48 is 1 
So, the maximum value of 140$k$-10$k^2$-480 will be 10*1 = 10 (As the whole equation was divided by 10)
Therefore, the maximum value of the $20p-q-480$ is $\alpha\ $ = 10

questions.question_text: Hari is in a shopping mall and needs to use an upward escalator. His friend Giri, who is twice as fast as Hari, climbs the same escalator in 12 seconds. When Hari is halfway up, his friend calls him, and he starts descending on the same escalator. Given that Giri's climbing speed is 20 steps per second and the total steps on the escalator are 300, what is the duration (in seconds) of Hari's travel on the escalator?
questions.solution_text:
Let the speed of the escalator be $'x'$.
Giri climbs up the escalator in 12sec.
$\left(x+20\right)\times\ 12=300$
$x=5$steps/second.
Speed of Hari = $\frac{20}{2}=10$ steps/second.
Hari was at half the distance. (i.e. 150 steps).
Time taken by Hari to go there, = $\frac{150}{\left(10+5\right)}=10 \text{ seconds}$.
Time taken by Hari to come down = $\frac{150}{10-5}=30 \text{ seconds}$
Total time = 30 + 10 = 40 seconds.
The answer is C.

questions.question_text: A contractor hires 3 persons, A, B and C, to complete certain work. A and B started work. C joined them 7 days before finishing the work and left 2 days before finishing the work. The ratio of time taken by A, B, and C to finish the work alone is $\frac{1}{2}:\frac{1}{3}:\frac{1}{5}$. If C alone can finish half work in 9 days, find how many days did A work.
questions.solution_text:
The ratio of time taken by A, B, and C to finish the work alone is $\frac{1}{2}:\frac{1}{3}:\frac{1}{5}$. Then the ratio of their efficiencies is 2:3:5.
Let n be the total number of days.
C joined them 7 days before finishing the work and left 2 days before finishing the work, which means 'C' worked for 5 days.
Total work = $5\times\ 5x+n\times\ 5x$ = $5nx+25x$.
It is given that C alone can finish half work in 9 days,
$\frac{5nx+25x}{2\times\ 5x}=9$
$n+5=18$
$n=13$
A worked for 13 days.
The answer is Option (C).

x = 6000

The answer is 60000.

questions.question_text: Bablu has a farm in the shape of a Rhombus. Bablu wants to put a fence along the sides of the farm and makes the following calculations. He notes that the area of the farm is 24000 square meters, and the sum of the length of the diagonals of the farm is 460 meters. If it costs Rs. 1200 to fence 1 meter of length, how much should Bablu spend (in lakhs) to fence all the sides of his farm?
questions.solution_text:
Let the diagonals of the rhombus be 'a' and 'b' meters, respectively.
We know that the area of the rhombus = 0.5 * a * b = 24000 => a * b = 48000.
Given that a + b = 460 => a = 460 - b
=> (460 - b)*(b) = 48000
=> $b^2-460b+48000=0$
=> b = $\dfrac{\left(460\ \pm\ \sqrt{\ 460^2-4\cdot48000}\right)}{2}$
=> b = 160 or 300
=> a = 300 or 160.
In either the shape of the rhombus is identical.
Now, the side of rhombus = $\sqrt{\ \left(\dfrac{a}{2}\right)^2+\left(\dfrac{b}{2}\right)^2}=\sqrt{\ 80^2+150^2}=170$
Therefore, the length of 4 sides of the rhombus = 4 * 170 = 680 meters.
Therefore, the amount required to fence all four sides = 680 * 1200 = 816000 = 8.16 lakhs.

questions.question_text:
Find the product of unique roots of x in the equation given below:

$x^{y^2-5y+7}=27\ $, where $y=\log_3x$
questions.solution_text:
Take log on both sides with base 3, since $y=\log_3x$ 
Therefore the equation will be $\left(y^2-5y+7\right)y\ =\ \log_327\ =\ 3\ =>\ y^3-5y^2+7y-3=0$ which can be written as $\left(y-1\right)\ \left(y^2-4y+3\right)=0\ =>\ \left(y-1\right)\left(y-3\right)\left(y-1\right)=0\ \ =>\ y=1,1,3$ 
Since y = $\log_3x$ , therefore $\log_3x\ =1\ =>3\ $ and $\log_3x\ =3\ =>x=27$ 
Hence, unique roots of the equation are 27 and 3. 
Product = 27*3 = 81
The answer is 81.

The roots of quadratic equations $f(x) = x^2+ax+b$ and $g(x) = x^2+cx+d$ are 3,4 and 5,4 respectively. If $\alpha\ $ and $\beta\ $ are roots of $h(x)=f(x)+g(x)$, find the value of $\frac{\ \alpha\ }{1+\alpha\ }+\frac{\ \beta\ }{1+\beta\ }$

g(x) = (x-5)(x-4)

questions.question_text: A locker in Ankit's room can be opened by dialling a fixed four digits code (between 0000 to 9999). Ankit can only recall that the first digit of the password is greater than 2,  and that it has exactly one eight. Using this information, he tries to open the locker by randomly dialling four digits. The probability that he succeeds in his first attempt is:
questions.solution_text:
Since the password is a four-digit number and consists of only one eight and the first digit is greater than 2, which implies that the thousand place's digit can be 3 to 9 and there is only one eight, and it can place in any of the places among thousands, hundreds, tenth and unit's place.
Case 1:
If 8 is placed in the thousands place, then the total four-digit number can be formed = _ _ _ _  = 1*9*9*9 =729 ( since 8 is already in the thousands place, which implies that 8 cannot be placed in hundreds, tenth, and units place. Therefore, all the digits from 0 to 9 except 8 can be placed in hundreds, tenths, and units place.) Hence, hundreds, tenth, and units place can be filled in 9, 9, and 9 ways. Therefore, the total four-digit number will be = 1*9*9*9 =729
Case 2:
If 8 is placed in the hundreds place, then the total four-digit number can be formed = 6*1*9*9 = 486 ( since 8 is already in the hundreds place, which implies that 8 cannot be placed in thousands, tenth, and units place and we also know that 0,1,2 can't be placed in thousands place because the first digit is greater than 2 . So, thousands of places can be filled in 6 ways, and the tenth and unit places can be filled in 9 ways. Therefore, the total four-digit number = 6*1*9*9  = 486
The same is true when 8 is placed in tenths and units places.
In case 2, The total four-digit number = 3*(6*1*9*9) = 1458. Total four-digit number = (729+1458) = 2187
The probability = $\dfrac{1}{2187}$
The correct option is D

The number of 5-digit integers less than 30000 = 2*5*4*3*2 = 240
Total number of integers less than 30000 = 6 + 25 + 100 + 300 + 240 = 671
The answer is 671.

questions.question_text: Ankit bought some bottles and glasses. While spending the same amount as Ankit, Rahul bought twice as many bottles and 20 fewer glasses. Let the cost of a bottle be x, and cost of a glass be y, as well as the number of bottles be B and the number of glasses be G
The total amount paid by Ankit = Bx+Gy
Rahul bought 2B bottles and G-20 glasses
Total amount paid by Rahul = 2Bx+(G-20)y
It is given that amount spent by Ankit, and Rahul is the same.
=> Bx+Gy = 2Bx+(G-20)y
=> Bx = 20y
It is given,
y = x+50 
=> Bx = 20x+1000
=> x = $\ \frac{1000}{B-20}$
Therefore, minimum number of Bottles bought by Ankit will be 21.
This implies Rahul bought 42 Bottles.
The minimum number of bottles bought by both Ankit and Rahul = 21 + 42 = 63 Bottles
The answer is 63.

questions.question_text: There are two cans A and B with a capacity of 40 litres and 30 litres, respectively. The can A has 60% alcohol, and the can B has 46.67% alcohol. If 15 litres from can A and 12 litres from can B are exchanged between both the cans, what is the final ratio of the amount of alcohol present in can A to can B?
questions.solution_text:
Can A has 60% alcohol content, and 15 litres have been removed.
Amount of alcohol removed from can A = $15\times\ 0.6=9\ litres$
Amount of water removed from can A = 15 - 9 = 6 litres.
Can B has 46.67% alcohol content, and 12 litres have been removed.
Amount of alcohol removed from can B= $12\times\ \frac{7}{15}=5.6\ litres$.
Amount of water removed from can B = 12 - 5.6 = 6.4 litres.
Removed quantities from both cans are exchanged.
The final alcohol content in can A = $40\times\ 0.6-9+5.6=20.6\ litres$
The final alcohol content in can B = $30\times\ \frac{7}{15}-5.6+9=17.4\ litres$
The ratio of alcohol content of can A to can B = $\frac{20.6}{17.4}=\frac{103}{87}$
The answer is option A.

questions.question_text: Three machines, M1, M2, and M3, created a stockpile of goods, with M1 and M2 producing 35% and 25%, respectively. Products from M1 have a defect rate of 2%, M2 have a defect rate of 1.2%, and M3 have a defect rate of x%. Suppose the overall defect ratio of the stockpile of products is y%. If it is given that x and y are natural numbers and y < 8. Find the total number of possible pairs of x and y.

Let the number of total goods be 1000a
M1 produces 35% goods = 350a
M2 produces 25% goods = 250a
M3 produces 40% goods = 400a
Defective products by M1 = 7a
Defective products by M2 = 3a

Therefore 7a+3a+4ax = 10ay
=>10+4x = 10y
It is given x, and y are natural numbers such that  y < 8
=> 4x = 10y-10
RHS is always a number multiple of 10
The value of x should be such that LHS is multiple of 10.
Therefore, x = 5, 10, 15.....
If x = 5, y = 3
If x = 10, y = 5
If x = 15, y = 7
For the remaining values of x, y is greater than 8. 
Therefore, only 3 pairs of x and y are possible.
The answer is option B.

questions.question_text: In triangle ABC, the coordinates of A, B and C are (7,3), (4,2) and (3,5). AD is altitude from A to BC. Find the coordinates of point 'D'.
questions.solution_text:
The coordinates of A, B & C are (7,3), (4,2) & (3,5)
The equation of line BC is, $\frac{y-2}{x-4}=\frac{2-5}{4-3}$
$\frac{y-2}{x-4}=\frac{-3}{1}$
$y-2=-3\times\ \left(x-4\right)$
$y-2=-3x+12$
$3x+y-14=0$
Altitude AD is perpendicular to BC. Hence, $\text{Slope of BC}$ $\times$ $\text{Slope of AD}$  = -1.
$(-3)\times\ \text{Slope\ of\ AD}=-1$
$\text{Slope of AD}$ = $\frac{1}{3}$.
The line AD passes through point 'A' and has a slope equal to $\frac{1}{3}$.
Hence, the line equation of AD is, $\frac{y-3}{x-7}=\frac{1}{3}$
$3\left(y-3\right)=x-7$
$3y-9=x-7$
$x-3y+2=0$
Point D is the intersection of lines AD & BC.
$3x+y-14=0$.......(1)
$x-3y+2=0$.........(2)
3 $\times$ EQ(1) + EQ(2) gives,
$9x+3y-42+x-3y+2=0$.
$10x=40$.
It implies $x=4\ \&\ y=2$
The coordinates of point D are (4,2).
As points B and D coincide, triangle ABC is a right-angled triangle.
The answer is option C.

questions.question_text: On a festival, the expenses are partly constant and partly vary as the square root of the number of guests on that festival. When there are 100 guests, the costs are Rs. 2650. When there are 64 guests, the expenses are Rs.2200. Find the cost(in rupees) when there are 1444 guests.
questions.solution_text:
Let the costs are denoted by C, and the number of guests are denoted by n. 
Hence, C can be written as $a+b\sqrt{\ n}$ (where a is constant and b is proportionality constant)
For 64 guests, the expenses are 2200, which can be written as 
$a+b\sqrt{\ 64}=a+8b\ =\ 2200\ $  ........  eq(1)
For 100 guests, the expenses are 2650, which can be written as,
$a+b\sqrt{\ 100}=a+10b\ =\ 2650$  ........  eq(2)
Subtracting Eq(1) from Eq(2), we get
2b = 450  
=> b = 225
Substituting b = 225 in Eq(1), we get a = 400
The expenses for 1444 guests is $a+b\sqrt{\ 1444}=a+38b\ =\ 400+38\times\ 225=8950$
The answer is 8950.

Find the area (in sq metres) of the triangle ABC.

In a circle, the angle made by a chord with a tangent to one of the ends of the chord is equal to the angle subtended by the chord in the other segment. As shown in the figure, $∠ACB=∠BAT$
Hence in the triangle ABC, $∠ACB=∠BAC=\angle CBA=60^{\circ\ }$

Area of ABC = $\frac{\sqrt{\ 3}\left(4\sqrt{\ 3}\right)^2}{4}$=$12\sqrt{\ 3}$ m$^2$
The answer is Option (C).

questions.question_text: Ram can complete a task in 50 days, while Sham takes 100 days to complete the same task. They started working on the task together, but after 25 days, both fell sick. Instead of them, Talram began to work on the task from the 26th day. Ram and Sham recovered and joined back the next day, and together, all three of them completed the task within 3 days. If they were paid Rs 10,000 for the task, find the amount of money earned by Talram per day.

Let's assume the total quantity of work to be done is 100 units.
Efficiency of ram = 100/50 = 2 units per day 
Efficiency of sham = 100/100= 1 unit per day 
In the given scenario ram and sham worked for 25 days, then they took a break for 1 day and again worked for next 3 days .
Hence, ram and sham both worked for a total of 28 days.
Work done by ram = 28*2 = 56 and work don by sham = 28*1 = 28 units .
Remaining work would be done by Talram = 100 - (56+28) = 16 units.
Talram worked for a total of 4 days, Hence work done by him per day = 16/4 = 4 units.
Rs 10,000 is paid for 100 units of task.
Hence, for 4 units of work per day, Talram will earn Rs 400 per day
The answer is option B.

questions.question_text: A and B are running in the same direction on a 5000m circular track. The speed of A is 50m/s and the speed of B is X m/s where X is a natural number less than 50. When they run in the same direction they meet at 8 distinct points on the track. If they both participate in a 7000m running race with A giving B a head start of 200m, by how much time does A beat B?
questions.solution_text:
Let a and b be the final ratio of the speed of A and B,
It is given that both A and B meet at 8 distinct points on the circular track, and also that A is faster than B.
$a-b=8$.
$a$ and $b$ are ratios, hence a is one of the factor of 50 m/s.
Values $a$ can assume are 1, 2, 5, 10, 25, and 50.
$a$ have to be greater than 8, as the difference is 8. Out of 10, 25 and 50, it can take the value of 25 alone, for other values the final ratio won't be the same.
$25-b=8$
$b=25-8=17$
$\frac{A}{B}=\frac{a}{b}$
$\frac{25}{17}=\frac{50}{B}$
$B=34 m/s$.
A gives B a head start of 200m. 
Time taken by A to finish 7000m race = $\frac{7000}{50}=140\ s$
Time taken by B to finish 6800m race = $\frac{6800}{34}=200\ s$
A beats B by = 200 - 140 = 60 seconds.
The answer is Option (B).

questions.question_text: Find the remainder that $7^{51}+3^{29}$ leaves when divided by 8.
questions.solution_text:
Given number = $7^{51}+3^{29}$
= $\left(7\times\ \left(7^2\right)^{25}\right)+\left(3\times\ \left(3^2\right)^{14}\right)$
= $7\left(48+1\right)^{25}+3\left(8+1\right)^{14}$
Let us expand the terms using Binomial expansion, we get
$7\left(25_{c_0}48^0\left(1\right)^{25}+25_{c_1}48^1\left(1\right)^{24}+....\right)+3\left(14_{c_0}8^0\left(1\right)^{14}+14_{c_1}8^1\left(1\right)^{13}+....\right)$
We see that in both expansions we have 8 common in all the terms respectively except the first team.
= $7\left(1+8k\right)+3\left(1+8j\right)$
= 10 + 8z
= 2 + 8y (where k, j, z, y are some constants)
Therefore it leaves a remainder of 2, when divided by 8.

questions.question_text: Find the sum of the terms $\frac{1}{2},\frac{1}{6}, \frac{1}{12} ,\frac{1}{20} .......\frac{1}{132}$
questions.solution_text:
$\frac{1}{2},\frac{1}{6}, \frac{1}{12} ,\frac{1}{20} .......\frac{1}{132}$n terms
$S(1) = \frac{1}{2}$
$S(2) = \frac{2}{3}$
$S(3) = \frac{2}{3} + \frac{1}{12} = \frac{3}{4}$
$S(4) = \frac{2}{3} + \frac{1}{12} + \frac{1}{20} = \frac{4}{5}$
From the above we can see that the sum of the first n terms $= S(n) = \frac{n}{n+1}$
$\frac{1}{132}$ is the eleventh term as 132 = 11 x12.Thus, sum of first 11 terms = $\frac{11}{11 + 1}$ = $\frac{11}{12}$

questions.question_text: For how many values of $‘n’$ does $n!$ have more than 150 but less than 160 trailing zeroes?
questions.solution_text:
The number of trailing zeroes should be from 151 to 159, total of 9 values. For each trailing zero there will be five values. 
For 151 trailing numbers the value of $n$ would be approximately $4\times151=604$
Number of trailing zeroes for 604! is 148
Number of trailing zeroes for (605! - 609!) is 149
Number of trailing zeroes for (610! - 614!) is 150
Number of trailing zeroes for (615! - 619!) is 151
Number of trailing zeroes for (620! - 624!) is 152
But, Number of trailing zeroes for (625! - 629!) is 156 
Similarly, Number of trailing zeroes for (630! - 634!) is 157
Number of trailing zeroes for (635! - 639!) is 158
Number of trailing zeroes for (640! - 644!) is 159
$\therefore$ total number of such numbers = $6\times5=30$.
Hence, option C is the correct answer.

questions.question_text: A cylinder and a cone have the same base radius and the same height. The radius of the cylinder is doubled and its height is tripled while the radius of the cone is tripled and its height is doubled. What is the ratio of the new volumes of the cylinder and the cone?
questions.solution_text:
Let the initial radius of cylinder and cone be ‘r’ and height be ‘h’
So for cylinder, the new radius is 2r and height is 3h
The volume of the cylinder is $ \pi (2r)^{2}*3h = 12 \pi r^{2}h$
The new radius of cone is 3r and its new height is 2h
So the required volume is $\frac{1}{3}\pi(3r)^{2}*2h = 6 \pi r^{2}h$
Hence the required ratio is 2:1

questions.question_text: The average weight of 10 items is 20 kg. The weight of each item has an integral value. When the weights are arranged in descending order, the first three weights are 25 kg, 22kg and 21 kg. What can be the lowest possible weight of an item?

The average weight of 10 items is 20 kg.
Then the sum of all the weights is 20*10 = 200kg
Now top three heaviest weights are 25kg, 22kg and 21kg.
Then to minimize the weight of an item, we have to maximise the 4th heaviest to the 9th heaviest items.
The maximum value which the 4th heaviest to the 9th heaviest items can take is 21 kg
Hence, the lowest possible weight of an item = 200-25-22-21*7 = 6 kg

questions.question_text: An ATM machine contains 100 rupee, 200 rupee and 500 rupee notes. The machine contains 200 notes in total and the total value of the notes is Rs. 45,000. If the number of 500 rupee notes and 100 rupee notes are interchanged, then the net value of the notes in the machine increases by Rs. 20,000. What will be the total value of the notes in the machine if the number of 100 rupee notes and 200 rupee notes are interchanged?
questions.solution_text:
Let the number of 100 rupee notes be x, 200 rupee notes be y and 500 rupee notes be z.
It has been given that,
x + y + z = 200 -----------------(1)
100x + 200y + 500z = 45,000 ------------(2)
If the number of 100 rupee and 500 rupee notes are interchanged, then the value increases by 20,000.
Therefore, 500x + 200y + 100z = 65,000--------(3)
Subtracting (2) from (3), we get,
400x - 400z = 20,000
x-z = 50
x = 50+z -------(4)
Multiplying (1) by 200 and subtracting it from (2), we get,
-100x + 300z = 5000
3z - x = 50
x = 3z - 50 ---------(5)
Equating (4) and (5), we get, 
50 + z = 3z - 50
2z = 100
z = 50
We know that x = 50+z
=> x = 100
x+y+z = 200
100 + y + 50 = 200
y = 50
Therefore, x = 100, y = 50 and z =50.
If the number of 100 and 200 rupee notes are interchanged, then the net value will be
50*100 + 100*200 + 50*500 = 5,000 + 20,000 + 25,000.
Total value = Rs.50,000.
Therefore, option B is the right answer.

questions.question_text: The distance between Chandigarh and Amritsar is 500 kms. A train starts from Chandigarh to Amritsar on Monday. In the midst of the journey, a technical glitch forces the driver to reduce the speed of the train by 20%. Had the glitch occurred 40 kms later, the train would have reached Amritsar 7 mins and 30 seconds earlier. Find the original speed of the train (before the glitch).
questions.solution_text:
Let the speed of the train be $a$ km/hr and the point at which the glitch occurs, say P be $x$ kms from Chandigarh. 
In the given case, we do not know the actual distance when the glitch happens. Since the question states the difference between the total time taken to complete the journey, we will express the situation in terms of time taken. 
Total time taken for the journey in the first case $t_{1} = \dfrac{x}{a} + \dfrac{500-x}{0.8a} $ (the first term in RHS is the time take to reach P while the second term in RHS is the time taken to travel the remaining distance at the reduced speed) 
Similarly, total time taken for the journey in the second case $t_{2} = \dfrac{x+40}{a} + \dfrac{500-(x+40)}{0.8a} $ (the first term in RHS is the time taken to reach a point 40 kms ahead of P, say Q and the second term is the time taken to travel the remaining distance at the reduced speed) 
Since in the second case, the train travels faster for a longer duration, the time taken in the first case will be greater. 
Given, $t_{1} - t_{2} = \dfrac{7.5}{60} hr $
$\dfrac{x}{a} + \dfrac{500-x}{0.8a} - (\dfrac{x+40}{a} + \dfrac{500-(x+40)}{0.8a}) = \dfrac{1}{8} hr$
$\Rightarrow \dfrac{x - (x+40)}{a} + \dfrac{500-x-(500-x-40)}{0.8a}) = \dfrac{1}{8} $
$\Rightarrow \dfrac{-40}{a} + \dfrac{40}{0.8a} = \dfrac{1}{8} $
$ \Rightarrow \dfrac{-40}{a} + (\dfrac{5}{4} \times \dfrac{40}{a}) = \dfrac{1}{8} $
$ \Rightarrow \dfrac{-40}{a} + \dfrac{50}{a} = \dfrac{1}{8} $
$ \Rightarrow \dfrac{10}{a} = \dfrac{1}{8} $
$ \Rightarrow a = 80$ km/hr

questions.question_text: Ramesh was supposed to board a flight from an airport which has 15 gates in a straight line. The distance between any adjacent pair of gates is 80 feet. His departure gate was initially assigned at random. After waiting at the assigned gate, Ramesh is informed that the departure gate has been changed to a different gate. If the probability that Ramesh covered a distance of 400 feet or less to reach to the new gate can be represented as $\dfrac{a}{b}$, where ‘$a$’ and ‘$b$’ are relatively prime numbers, then find out the remainder when '$b$' is divided by ‘$a$’?
questions.solution_text:
Total ways of selecting two different gates out of 15 gates = 15*14 = 210.
If Ramesh was assigned previously gate no. 1 or 15 then, there are a total of 5 other gates within 400 feet. 
Similarly, Ramesh was assigned previously gate no. 2 or 14 then there are a total of 6 other gates within 400 feet. 
Ramesh was assigned previously gate no. 3 or 13 then there are a total of 7 other gates within 400 feet.
Ramesh was assigned previously gate no. 4 or 12 then there are a total of 8 other gates within 400 feet
Ramesh was assigned previously gate no. 5 or 11 then there are a total of 9 other gates within 400 feet
Ramesh was assigned previously gate no. From 6 to 10 then, there are a total of 10 other gates within 400 feet. 
Hence total number of favourable cases = 2[5+6+7+8+9]+5*10 = 120
Therefore the required probability = $\dfrac{120}{210}$
$\Rightarrow$ $\dfrac{4}{7}=\dfrac{a}{b}$
We can see that, 7 mod 4 = 3.

questions.question_text:
If p, q and r are 3 natural numbers such that $\dfrac{p}{q}$ = $\dfrac{4}{3}$ then which of the following can be a value of 
{$\dfrac{p}{q}+\dfrac{q}{r}+\dfrac{r}{p}+\dfrac{r}{q}+\dfrac{p}{r}+\dfrac{q}{p}$}
questions.solution_text:
Given, $\dfrac{p}{q}$ = $\dfrac{4}{3}$
Therefore, $\dfrac{q}{p}$ = $\dfrac{3}{4}$
Hence, $\dfrac{q}{p}$+$\dfrac{p}{q}$ = $\dfrac{4}{3}$+$\dfrac{3}{4} = \dfrac{25}{12}$
For any natural number x we know, $x+\dfrac{1}{x} \geq 2$
Hence, $\dfrac{p}{r}+\dfrac{r}{p} \geq 2$
Also, $\dfrac{q}{r}+\dfrac{r}{q} \geq 2$
$\dfrac{p}{r}+\dfrac{r}{p}$ = 2 if $r=p$
$\dfrac{q}{r}+\dfrac{r}{q}$ = 2 if $r=q$ i.e. $r=p=q$
But that is not the case as $\dfrac{p}{q}$ = $\dfrac{4}{3}$
Hence, if $\dfrac{p}{r}+\dfrac{r}{p} = 2$ then $\dfrac{r}{q}+\dfrac{q}{r}$ is definitely greater than 2.
Hence, {$\dfrac{p}{q}+\dfrac{q}{r}+\dfrac{r}{p}+\dfrac{r}{q}+\dfrac{p}{r}+\dfrac{q}{p}$} $> \dfrac{25}{12} + 2 + 2$
Hence, {$\dfrac{p}{q}+\dfrac{q}{r}+\dfrac{r}{p}+\dfrac{r}{q}+\dfrac{p}{r}+\dfrac{q}{p}$} $> \dfrac{73}{12}$
The only option here greater than $\dfrac{73}{12}$ is $\dfrac{27}{4}$ Which comes for r = 6, p = 4 and q = 3.
Hence, option D is the correct answer.

questions.question_text: If the area of a regular hexagon is $6\sqrt{3}$ sq units, find out the area of a regular octagon that shares a side with the regular hexagon.
questions.solution_text:
The area of a regular hexagon = 6 x Area of an equilateral triangle having the same side
$6\sqrt{3}$ = $6\frac{\sqrt{3}}{4}a^2$
a = 2
Now, if we have an octagon of side 2, the area of the octagon = $2\left(1+\sqrt{\ 2}\right)a^2=8\left(1+\sqrt{\ 2}\right)$
The area can also be calculated without the formula.
Area of 4 rectangles + Area of square + Area of 4 triangles
$(4\times\ 2\times\ \sqrt{\ 2})+( 2\times\ 2 ) + (4\times\ \frac{1}{2}\times\ \sqrt{\ 2}\times\ \sqrt{\ 2})=8+8\sqrt{\ 2}$

questions.question_text: If $x^2+4ax+20-2a$ > 0 for all real x, then which of the following holds true for all the values of a?
questions.solution_text:
The co-efficient of $x^2$ is greater than 0, so the discriminant should be less than zero, if the given expression is greater than 0 for all values of x.
$(4a)^2$ - 4*1*(20-2a) < 0
=> $16a^2 - 80+8a$ < 0
=> $2a^2+a-10$ < 0
=> $2a^2 + 5a - 4a - 10$ < 0
=> a(2a+5)-2(2a+5) < 0
=> (a-2)(2a+5)<0
$\frac{-5}{2}$ < a < 2
B is the correct answer.

questions.question_text: In an equilateral triangle, another triangle is formed using 2 vertices of the triangle and the incenter of the equilateral triangle. What is the ratio of the in-radius of the equilateral triangle and the in-radius of the triangle so formed?
questions.solution_text:
Let ABC be the equilateral triangle and I be the incenter. Join BI and IC to form triangle BIC as shown below:-
Let the side of the equilateral triangle be $2\sqrt{3}$ cm
As we know the length of the in-radius of an equilateral triangle = $\dfrac{side}{ 2\sqrt{3}} = \dfrac{2\sqrt{3}}{2\sqrt{3}} $
Thus, the in radius of the equilateral triangle = 1 cm.
Thus, IJ = 1 cm.
We know BC = $2\sqrt{3}$ cm
Thus, $BJ = \sqrt{3}$…..(median bisects the side)
Thus, BI = $\sqrt{1+3} = 2$
Thus, BI = CI = 2 cm.
Area of triangle BIC = $\dfrac{1}{2}*IJ*BC = \dfrac{1}{2}*1*2\sqrt{3} = \sqrt{3}$
Also, Area of triangle BIC = sr
s = $\dfrac{2+2+2\sqrt{3}}{2} = 2+\sqrt{3}$
Thus, $(2+\sqrt{3})*r = \sqrt{3}$
Thus, $r = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{(2+\sqrt{3})}$
Thus, the required ratio = $1:\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{(2+\sqrt{3})}$ = $(2+\sqrt{3}):\sqrt{3}$
Hence, option A is the correct answer.

questions.question_text: Sumitra has to solve 384 questions. She decides to solve a particular number of questions per day to complete the task in a certain number of days. Shalini, her friend, suggests that if she solves eight more questions per day than what Sumitra has decided, she will take eight fewer days to finish the task than what Sumitra has calculated. In how many days can the task be completed if Sumitra follows what Shalini suggested?
questions.solution_text:
Let the number of questions to be solved per day be $x$, and the number of days required be $y$ as per Sumitra's plan.
So, $xy = 384$
As per Shalini, 
$(x + 8)(y - 8) = 384$
or,  $xy - 8x + 8y - 64 = 384$
or,  $8y - 8x = 64$
or,  $y - x = 8$
Putting $y = \dfrac{384}{x}$, we get
$\dfrac{384}{x} - x = 8$
or,  $384 - x^2 = 8x$
or,  $x^2 + 8x - 384 = 0$
On solving, we get $x = -24$ or $x = 16$
But,  $x$ cannot be negative.
So,  $x = 16$
=>  $y = \dfrac{384}{x} = 24$
According to Shalini, number of days required =  $ (y - 8) = 16$ days
Hence, 16 is the required answer.

questions.question_text: Bombs are fired on a bridge such that a probability of a bomb hitting the bridge is 0.5. A minimum of two bombs are required to hit a bridge in order to destroy it. Find the minimum number of hits required such that probability of destroying a bridge is greater than 0.8.
questions.solution_text:
We need the probability of atleast two hits
= 1 - probability of less than two hits
= 1 - (probabilty of 0 hits + probability of 1 hit)
Let n be the number of hits,
Then probability of 0 hits = $(\frac{1}{2})^n$ , since for each turn probability of missing = 1/2
Probability of 1 hit = $n*\frac{1}{2}*(\frac{1}{2})^{n-1}$ = $n*(\frac{1}{2})^n$, since the turn which will hit can be selected in $^nC_1$ ways and probability of hitting in that turn = 1/2 and probability that all other n-1 turns will miss is $(\frac{1}{2})^{n-1}$.
Hence probability of atleast two hits = 1 - $(\frac{1}{2})^n$ - $n*(\frac{1}{2})^n$
The minimum value of n for which the above value is greater than 0.8 is 5

questions.question_text:
If $t>2$, what is the solution set of the inequality

$(t-2)^{t^2 - 6t + 8} > 1$?
questions.solution_text:
Taking logarithm on both sides, we get,
$(t^2 - 6t + 8) log (t-2) > log 1 = 0$
=>$(t - 2)(t - 4) log (t-2) > 0$
For t < 2 and t > 4, (t-2)(t-4) > 0. In this case, for the inequality to hold, log (t-2) > 0
=> t - 2 > 1 => t > 3
The common interval is t > 4
For 2 < t < 4, (t-2)(t-4) < 0. In this case, for the inequality to hold, log (t-2) < 0
=> t - 2 < 1 => t < 3
The common interval is 2 < t < 3
So, the solution set is 2 < t < 3 U t > 4

questions.question_text: One of the roots of the equation $x^2 - (m - 2)x + 6 = 0$ lies between (0, 2) and the other root lies between (3, 4). It is known that $m$ is an integer. What is the sum of all the possible values of $m$?
questions.solution_text:
We know that the graph of a quadratic polynomial cuts x-axis at the points which are also the roots of the quadratic equation. Therefore, the value of the polynomial will be opposite in sign on the two points between which the roots lie.
In this graph, we can observe that the polynomial changes its sign at the roots.
In the given question, one of the roots lie between (0, 2) and the other root lie between (3, 4)
Let $f(x) = x^2 - (m - 2)x + 6$
So, $f(0) > 0$.................(i)
So, $f(2) < 0$.................(i)
So, $f(3) < 0$.................(i)
So, $f(4) > 0$.................(i)
We can write (i) as $6>0$ which is always true
We can write (ii) as
$(14 - 2m) < 0$
$m > 7$
We can write (iii) as
$9-3*(m-2)+6<0$
or $m > 7$
We can write (iv) as
$16-4*(m-2)+6>0$
or, $m<7.5$
Therefore, $m$ belongs to $(7, \dfrac{15}{2})$
Thus, no integral value of $m$ satisfies it.
Hence, option D is the correct answer.

questions.question_text: p, q, r and s are four distinct real numbers such that $p^2 - q = q^2 - r = r^2 - s = s^2 - p$, what is the value of (p + q)(q + r)(r + s)(s + p)?
questions.solution_text:
$p^2 - q = q^2 - r$
$p^2 - q^2 = q - r$
=> $ p + q = \frac{q - r}{p - q}$ -(1)
Similarly, $ q + r = \frac{r - s}{q - r}$(2)
$ r + s = \frac{s - p}{r - s}$ - (3)
$ s + p = \frac{p - r}{s - p}$ - (4)
From (1), (2), (3) and (4) we get (p + q)(q + r)(r + s)(s + p) = $\frac{q - r}{p - q} \times \frac{r - s}{q - r} \times \frac{p - q}{r - s} \times \frac{p - r}{ s - p} = 1$

questions.question_text: What is the absolute difference between the number of 3-digit even numbers that have at least one 2 in them and those that do not have any 2 in them?
questions.solution_text:
Number of 3 digit numbers is 999 - 100 + 1 = 900
Since it starts with an even number and ends with an odd number, it has an equal number of even and odd numbers.
So, the number of even numbers = 900/2 = 450.
Now we need to count the number of even numbers with no 2 in it.
Unit's digit can be filled with any of 0, 4, 6 and 8, since it is an even number and does not contain 2. Count = 4
Ten's digit can have any number from 0 to 9 except for 2. Count = 9
Hundred's digit can have any number from 1 to 9 except for 2. Count = 8
Hence, total number of 3-digit even numbers with no 2 in them = $4\times\ 9\times\ 8=288$
Hence, total number of 3-digit even numbers with at least one 2 in them = 450 - 288 = 162
Hence, difference = 288 - 162 = 126

questions.question_text: A right cylinder of radius = $\sqrt{12}$cm and height = 8 cm is melted and transformed into a cone of same height. If the ratio of lateral surface area of cone to the lateral surface area of cylinder can be represented as a : b$\sqrt{3}$, where a and b are co-primes, what is the value of a + b ?
questions.solution_text:
Since the volume will remain constant, we can equate the volume of cylinder to cone.
$\pi * r^2 * h$ = $\frac{1}{3} * \pi * R^2 *h$
where r is the radius of cylinder and R is the radius of cone
Putting values and solving we get R = 6 cm
So the slant height of cone, l = $\sqrt{6^2 + 8^2}$ = 10 cm
Ratio of lateral surface areas of cone and cylinder = $\frac{\pi Rl}{2\pi rh}$
= $\frac{6 * 10}{2 * \sqrt{12} * 8}$
= $\frac{15}{8\sqrt{3}}$
So, a = 15 and b = 8 and a + b = 23.

questions.question_text: If |x+1|<6 and |y-1|<6 where x,y are integers, what can be the maximum value of x$^{2}$+y$^{2}$-xy
questions.solution_text:
We have, |x+1|<6 and |y-1|<6
|x+1|<6   => -6<x+1<6  =>  -7<x<5
|y-1|<6 => -6< y-1<6 => -5<y<7.
Since x$^{2}$+y$^{2}$ is positive, the value will be maximized when xy is negative.
The highest negative value of x = -6 and highest positive value of y is 6.
Hence the maximum value of x$^{2}$+y$^{2}$-xy will be (-6)$^{2}$+(6)$^{2}$-(-6)(6) = 108

Consider Circle C1 represented by the curve $x^2+y^2-10x-8y+25=0$ and C2 represented by $x^2+y^2-8x-8y+23=0$. The area formed by the tangent common to C1 and C2, a tangent of C2 parallel to x axis and the line y=x+8 is:

A. 32 sq. units

B. 2 sq. units

C. 16 sq. units
questions.solution_text:
C1 is given as: $x^2+y^2-10x-8y+25=0$, which can be re-written as $x^2-10x+25+y^2-8y+16=16$
Or, C1= $\left(x-5\right)^2+\left(y-4\right)^2=4^2$.
C1 has the centre at (5,4) and radius = 4 units.
Similarly, C2 is given as: $x^2+y^2-8x-8y+23=0$, which when manipulated becomes $x^2-8x+16+y^2-8y+16=9$
or, C2 is given as $\left(x-4\right)^2+\left(y-4\right)^2=3^2$, which has a centre at (4,4) and radius 3 units.
The circles, its common tangent, tangents of C2 parallel to X-axis and the line y=x+8 can be drawn as:
The common tangent is represented by the dotted line x=1. The purple line shows y= x+8
The two tangents of the circle C2 are y=1 and y=7.
So, there are two possible triangles formed using the information given in the question, $\triangle ABC\ \ $ and $\triangle ADE\ $
Point C is simply the intersection of y=7 and x=1. So, C=(1,7)
In $\triangle ABC\ \ $, Base AC= 2 units, height BC= 2 units. So, area= $\ \frac{\ 1}{2}\times2\times2=2\ $sq. units
In $\triangle ADE\ $, Base AE= 8 units, Height ED= 8 units. So, area= $\ \frac{\ 1}{2}\times8\times8=32\ $sq. units
therefore both A and B are correct

questions.question_text:
Mohit and Narayan started a company by investing their life savings. The company faced huge losses because of which its value halved. Narayan took out all of his remaining money but Mohit kept on working hard. He made a 300% profit next month. Meanwhile, Narayan found out a scheme of ‘Double your money in 30 days’ and invested half of the money he had left with him. They met at the end of the month and found out they had exactly the same amount of money, as Narayan lost all the money he had invested in the bogus scheme.

If both of them invested money in multiples of Rs. 1000, which of the following can be the total money they had invested in the company initially?
questions.solution_text:
Let the amount Mohit invested be 1000M and that Narayan invested be 1000N Rupees, where M and N are natural numbers.
The value of the company halved. Hence, their investments will also be halved and will become 500M and 500N respectively.
Mohit made a 300% profit the next month. This means, a profit of 3 times 500M. Thus, the final amount with him at the end of the month will be $4\times\ 500M=2000M$.
Narayan lost half of what he had to a bogus scheme. Thus, the total amount with him at the end will be 250N.
It has been given that 2000M=250N. (Money at the end of the month is the same).
Or N=8M.
Total amount in the beginning= 1000M+1000N = 1000M+8000M = 9000M.
Since M is a natural number, the total sum must be a multiple of 9000. Only Option C satisfies this criterion, and hence, is the correct answer.

questions.question_text: An empty tank can be filled in 70 minutes by water flowing from a pipe of square cross section of side 3 cm at the rate of 4 cm/sec. Now another pipe of a circular cross section is added at the bottom of the tank which empties the tank at the rate of 7 cm/sec. When both the pipes are present the tank when empty gets filled completely in 180 minutes. What is the radius of the circular pipe at the bottom of the tank (in cm)?
questions.solution_text:
Volume of flow of water into the tank per second = Rate of flow * Area of cross section of pipe
In first case with only one pipe, Volume flow per sec = $3^2 \times 4$ = 36 units
In second case, Volume flow per sec = 36 - $ \pi r^2\times7$ = 36- $ 7\pi r^2$ units
Ratio of times taken is the inverse ratio of volumes flow per sec
=> $\frac{70}{180}=\frac{36-7\pi r^2}{36}$
Solving, we get r = 1 cm.

Option D : First Simple  interest of 15 percent per annum followed by Compound Interest at 15 percent per annum :

13000(1.15)(1.15) = Rs 17192.5
Option A gives you the maximum returns .

= $1^3 + 2^3 + 3^3$ = 36
Now we have to find the last two digits of $36^{172}$
= $6^{344}$
The remainder when $6^{344}$ is divided by 100 is calculated using Chinese remainder theorem.
6 and 100 are not co-prime to each other.
Calculate $6^{344}$ mod 25 and $6^{344}$ mod 4 
$6^{20}$ mod 25 is 1   [From Euler theorem, Euler of 25 = 25*(1-$\frac{1}{5}$) = 20]
$6^{344}$ mod 25 = $6^{340}*6^4$ mod 25 = 1*1296 mod 25  = 36*36 mod 25= 11*11 mod 25 = 121 mod 25 = 21
$6^{344}$ mod 4 is 0
25p+21 = 4q+0
Using trial and error p = 3 and q = 24
25p+21 = 25*3 + 21
=96 is the last two digits of $6^{344}$
Sum of the digits = 15
15 is the correct answer.

questions.question_text: Pipe A, pipe B and pipe C are used to fill a tank. The flow rate of pipe C is 25% less than pipe B. To fill the empty tank completely, Pipe A and Pipe B together take one third the time taken by Pipe C alone. If all three pipes can fill the tank in 15 hours, then find the time taken (in hours) by A alone to fill the tank completely.
questions.solution_text:
Assuming the flow rate of pipe A is a  and  that of the pipe B is b, then the flow rate of pipe C = 0.75b
The capacity of the tank = Flow rate of all the tanks*Time taken  = 15(a+b+0.75b) = 15(a+1.75b)
To fill the empty tank completely, pipe A and pipe B together take one-third time than pipe C alone. It means that the flow rate of A and B combined is equal to 3 times that of C.
Hence, a+b  = 3*0.75b
=> a = 1.25b
Hence, the total capacity of the tank = 15(1.25b+1.75b) = 45b
Time taken by A to fill the tank = $\dfrac{45b}{1.25b}\ $  = 36 hours

questions.question_text: PQRS is an isosceles trapezium as shown in the figure. The lengths of the parallel sides are 8 cm and 10cm. The length of the non-parallel side is 8 cm. Which among the following can be the ratio of lengths of one of the parallel sides and the diagonals of the trapezium?
questions.solution_text:
PQRS is an isosceles trapezium and it is inscribed in a circle so it is a cyclic isosceles trapezium.
So all the properties of a cyclic quadrilateral can be applied here.
In an isosceles trapezium, the non-parallel sides are equal.
The diagonals of an isosceles trapezium are equal, so PR = SQ
From Ptolemy Theorem,
PQ*SR+ PS*QR = PR*QS
8*10 +8*8 = PR*PR
PR = 12 cm
The possible ratio of one of the sides and the diagonal = 8:12, 10:12
=2:3, 5:6
B is the correct answer.

questions.question_text: The cost price of a pen is Rs. 20. A merchant sells the first pen for Rs. 2, second pen for Rs.4, third pen for Rs.6 and so on. What is the number of pens he should sell to make an overall profit of 20%?
questions.solution_text:
The total selling price of the n pens is 2+4+...+2n. 

2+4+6+..........2n can be written as 2(1+2+..............n) = 2 (n(n+1)/2) = n(n+1)

As the profit percentage is 20%, it implies that n(n+1) = 120%*20n=24n.
Hence, $n^2=23n$. Hence, n=23.

questions.question_text: A manufacturer produces two types of products - A and B, which are subjected to two types of operations, viz. grinding and polishing. Each unit of product A takes 2 hours of grinding and 3 hours of polishing whereas product B takes 3 hours of grinding and 2 hours of polishing. The manufacturer has 10 grinders and 15 polishers. Each grinder operates for 12 hours/day and each polisher 10 hours/day. The profit margin per unit of A and B are Rs. 5/ - and Rs. 7/ - respectively. If the manufacturer utilises all his resources for producing these two types of items, what is the maximum profit that the manufacturer can earn in a day?
questions.solution_text:
Let the number of units of A and B produced be $x$ and $y$ respectively.

For product A, time taken for grinding = $2x$ and polishing = $3x$

For product B, time taken for grinding = $3y$ and polishing = $2y$

Total number of hours of grinding done per day = $10 \times 12 = 120$ hrs

Total number of hours of polishing done per day = $15 \times 10 = 150$ hrs

=> $2x + 3y = 120$ ---------Eqn(I)

and $3x+ 2y = 150$ ----------Eqn(II)

Applying the operation : 3* Eqn(I) - 2* Eqn(II), we get :

=> $(6x - 6x) + (9y - 4y) = 360 - 300$

=> $y = \frac{60}{5} = 12$

=> $x = 42$

$\therefore$ Profit made by the manufacturer = $(42 \times 5) + (12 \times 7)$

= $210 + 84 = Rs. 294$

questions.question_text: Ravi purchased a new car for Rupees 6 lakhs. He spent another 50,000 in the registration process. Three months later, his car was in an accident, and since the damages were not covered under the insurance policy, he had to spend 20,000 on the repairs. Over the next 18 months, he spends another 20000 on repairs. The purchase value of any car depreciates every year by 10%. Moreover, each repair of rupees 'x' depreciates the car's purchase value by 'x/2'. Ravi sells his car at the end of two years. What can be the minimum loss that he will have to bear?
questions.solution_text:
Let us first calculate the total investment made by Ravi.
600000 + 50000 + 20000*2 = 690000.
We know that the value of the car's purchase value [600000] depreciates by 10 percent every year. Hence, the value of the car at the end of 2 years will be
600000*.9*.9 = 486000. Further, the depreciation on account of repairs = 20000. [40000/2]
Hence, the net value of the car at the end of two years = 466000.
Hence, the loss incurred = 690000 - 466000 = 224000
In percentage terms, this will be 224*100/690 = 32.46 %

questions.question_text: In any given ball, a batsman can hit either of 0, 1, 2, 3, 4 or 6 runs. There is no possibility for wickets or extra runs. The probability of hitting a six is 1/10, the probability of hitting a four is also 1/10. The probability of hitting any other run out of all possible runs is the same. In the final of 2019 WC between New Zealand and England, New Zealand needs to score a minimum of 34 runs in the Super Over (6 balls) to defend the WC Title. What is the probability that New Zealand retains the title?
questions.solution_text:
P(hitting a 6) = $\frac{1}{10}$
P(hitting a 4) = $\frac{1}{10}$
To get 34 runs, they can hit 6,6,6,6,6,4 or 6,6,6,6,5,5 runs. But 5 runs can not be scored in a ball.
P(6,6,6,6,6,4) = $^6C_1\times\ \left(\frac{1}{10}\right)^5\left(\frac{1}{10}\right)=\frac{6}{10^6}$ [$^6C_1\ $ is included since they can hit a 4 in any of the 6 balls].
To get 35 runs, they can hit 6,6,6,6,6,5 runs. But 5 runs can not be scored in a ball, so this is not possible.
To get 36 runs, they can hit 6,6,6,6,6,6 runs.
P(6,6,6,6,6,6) = $\left(\frac{1}{10}\right)^6=\frac{1}{10^6}$
Hence, total probability = $\frac{7}{1000000}$
