questions.question_text: Seven tennis players are to be seated in a row, with the only three female players sitting together. If two specific male players refuse to sit next to each other, how many valid seating arrangements are possible?
questions.solution_text:
From the question, we can infer that there are three female tennis players; let us reference them as F1, F2, F3
Let us reference four male players: M1, M2, M3, and M4. 
We are told that two particular male players don't want to sit next to each other; let us set them as M1 and M2. 
F1, F2, and F3 should sit together. 
The number of ways to arrange (F1, F2, F3), M3, M4 will be 3!x3! since there are three groups we want to arrange, and F1, F2 and F3 can be placed in three factorial ways. 
M1 and M2 will go into the spaces; four spaces will be available.
For example, if we place _(F1, F2, F3)_M3_M4_
We will have four available spaces to select to place M1 and M2. The number of ways to arrange M1 and M2 will be the number of ways of selecting two spaces out of four, which will be $^4C_2$, and we can arrange M1 and M2 between those chosen spaces in 2! ways.
Hence, the total number of valid seating arrangements will be, 
$^4C_2\times2!\times3!\times3!$
6x2x6x6=432.

questions.question_text: A group of men of the same efficiency can build a wall in 45 hours. But when the work started, all the men did not begin working together. Each worker joined the work one after the other after a regular interval. Once joined, every worker stayed till the completion of the work. If the first man does 5 times as much work as the last man, then for how many hours did the first man work?
questions.solution_text:
Let the total number of men working be M.
In 45 hours, the work done by M men is calculated as 45M.
In this case, each man joined after an interval of time,
The work done by each man would be in an AP as the time for which they are working is also in AP.
Let the time worked by the first man be 5t, and the time worked by the last man, according to the question, is t.
So, the work done by all the men across the time is given by,
5t, 5t - d, 5t - 2d, ...., t
$Work\ done\ =\ \dfrac{n}{2}\left(first\ term\ +\ last\ term\right)\ =\ \dfrac{M}{2}\left(5t\ +\ t\right)\ =\ 3Mt$
The work done remains the same in both cases, and equating them, we get,
3Mt = 45M
t = 15 hours.
The time for which the first man worked is  5t = 5 * 15 = 75 hours.
Hence, the correct answer is option C.

questions.question_text: The roots of the equation $x^3 - x^2 + px + q = 0$ are in AP and the common difference is an integer. Which of the following is a possible value of p+q?
questions.solution_text:
Let the roots be a -d, a, a+d.
Sum of roots = 3a = 1. So, a = 1/3
Product of roots = (1/3-d)(1/3)(1/3+d) =-q
=> q = $-1/27 + d^2/3$
Sum of the roots taken 2 at a time = 1/9 -d/3 +1/9+d/3 +1/9 -$d^2$ = p
=> p = 1/3 - $d^2$
So, p+q = 8/27 - $2d^2/3$
The values that $d^2$ can take are 1, 4, 9,…
Substituting $d^2$ = 1, we get p+q = -10/27

questions.question_text: Two identical rectangles overlap, as shown in the figure below. It is also known that HF = 2 cm, AC = 8 cm and HD = 4 cm. Determine the area of the shaded region shown in the figure below.
questions.solution_text:
The given figure can be drawn as,
We are given that both rectangles are identical, so in the figure, the length of AE becomes 8. The length of BH becomes 4 as the other part is given as 4 in the question. Let the length AB be x and AH be y, then the length EH becomes x - 2, as we have assumed the whole length to be x above.
Now, we have two right-angled triangles, AEH and ABH, to apply Pythagoras' theorem twice and obtain the values x and y.
In triangle AEH,
$AE^2\ +\ EH^2\ =\ AH^2$
$8^2\ +\ \left(x\ -\ 2\right)^2\ =\ y^2$ ---(1)
In triangle ABH,
$AB^2\ +\ BH^2\ =\ AH^2$
$x^2\ +\ 4^2\ =\ y^2$  ---(2)
Equating (1) and (2), we get,
$x^2\ +16\ =\ x^2\ +\ 4\ -\ 4x\ +\ 64$
$4x\ =\ 52$
$x\ =\ 13$
Area of the rectangle can be calculated as length * breadth = 8 * x = 8 * 13 = 104 $cm^2$
The area of the overlap region can be calculated as, 
Area of AEH + Area of ABH = $\dfrac{1}{2}\ \times\ 8\ \times\ 11\ +\ \dfrac{1}{2}\ \times\ 4\ \times\ 13\ =\ 44\ +\ 26\ =\ 70\ cm^2$
The non-overlapped region area can be calculated as 
2 * (Area of the rectangle - Area of the overlapped region) = 2 * (104 - 70) = 2 * 34 = 68 $cm^2$
Hence, the correct answer is option D.

questions.question_text: If f(x) = 3x+5 and g(x) = 2x+3, then find the value of x for which f(g(f(g(x)))) = 26.
questions.solution_text:
If f(x) = 3x+5 and g(x) = 2x+3, then find the value of x for which f(g(f(g(x)))) = 26.
We know g(x) = 2x+3
f(g(x)) = 3*(2x+3)+5 = 6x+14
g(f(g(x))) = 2*(6x+14)+3 = 12x+31
f(g(f(g(x)))) = 3*(12x+31)+5 = 36x+98
We know f(g(f(g(x)))) = 26
Thus, 36x+98 = 26
36x = -72
x = -2

questions.question_text: A sphere and a cone have the same total surface area and share the same radius r. The cone is then melted and reshaped into a hemisphere. Find the ratio of the total surface area of the hemisphere to that of the sphere.
questions.solution_text:
Let the height of the cone be h and slant height be l.
A sphere and a cone have the same curved surface area and share the same radius r.
=> $\pi r^2+\pi rl=4\pi r^2$
=> $l=3r$
Now we know - $l^2=r^2+h^2$
=> $h=2\sqrt{2}r$
The cone is then melted and reshaped into a hemisphere.
=> $\dfrac{1}{3}\pi r^2h=\dfrac{2}{3}\pi R^3$
=> $\dfrac{1}{3}\pi r^2\left(2\sqrt{2}r\right)=\dfrac{2}{3}\pi R^3$
=> $R=2^{\frac{1}{6}}r$
Thus, the ratio of the total surface area of the hemisphere to that of the sphere will be -
$\dfrac{3\pi R^2}{4\pi r^2}=\dfrac{3\times\ 2^{\frac{1}{3}}\times\ r^2}{4\times\ r^2}=\dfrac{3}{2^{\frac{5}{3}}}$

=> $h=2\sqrt{2}r$
The cone is then melted and reshaped into a hemisphere.
=> $\dfrac{1}{3}\pi r^2h=\dfrac{2}{3}\pi R^3$
=> $\dfrac{1}{3}\pi r^2\left(2\sqrt{2}r\right)=\dfrac{2}{3}\pi R^3$
=> $R=2^{\frac{1}{6}}r$
Thus, the ratio of the total surface area of the hemisphere to that of the sphere will be -

questions.question_text: In Ghanshyam supermarket, a bottle of Pepsi costs 13 rupees, and a bottle of Coke costs 17 rupees. Aaron went to the supermarket and bought x bottles of Pepsi and y bottles of Coke, which cost him exactly 10000, and the value of |x - y| is minimum, which means x and y are as close as possible. Now David goes to the same supermarket and spends a little more than 10000 for x bottles of Coke and y bottles of Pepsi; how much did David spend?
questions.solution_text:
Aaron spent 10,000 on x Pepsi and y Coke bottles.
13x + 17y = 10000
Let us calculate a pair of x and y that satisfies the above equation,
We know, 13 * 3 + 17 * (-2) = 5,
13 * 3 * 2000 + 17 * (-2) * 2000 = 5 * 2000
13 * 6000 + 17 * (-4000) = 10000
So, (6000, -4000) satisfy the above equation.
The general terms of x and y that satisfy the above equation are,
x = 6000 - 17t
y = - 4000 + 13t
We know that x and y are greater than 0,
Condition for x > 0,
6000 - 17t > 0
t < $\dfrac{6000}{17}$
t < 352.94
Similarly, for y > 0, we get,
-4000 + 13t > 0
13t > 4000
t > $\frac{4000}{13}$
t > 307.6
So, the value of t that satisfies the condition is in the range [308, 352]. In this range, we have to calculate the value of t at which |x - y| is the minimum.
The values are equal when 6000 - 17t = -4000 + 13t
t = $\dfrac{10000}{30}\ =\ 333.34$
But we know t has to be an integer, so x and y are closest when t = 333 or t = 334
At t = 333, the values of x and y are
x = 6000 - 17*333 = 339
y = -4000 + 13 * 333 = 329
|x - y| = 10
At t = 334, the values x and y are,
x = 6000 - 17 * 334 = 322
y = -4000 + 13 * 334 = 342
|x - y| = 20.
Hence, the values x and y are 339 and 329.
Now, the cost incurred by David is calculated as,
Cost = 17 * 339 + 13 * 329 = 10040.
Hence, the correct answer is option D.

questions.question_text: Glen borrowed a certain amount from Steve at a compound interest of 20% for two years. Glen invested the money borrowed in a certain ratio in Schemes A and B. He experienced an overall loss of 10% on the money invested in Scheme A, whereas the money invested in Scheme B saw a 50% increase in the same period. What is the ratio of the money invested in both the schemes if he made no profit after two years by paying back the money from the schemes to Steve?
questions.solution_text:
Let the money borrowed by Glen be P. The amount after two years of compounding annually at a rate of 20% becomes,
Money after 2 years = $P\left(1\ +\ \dfrac{20}{100}\right)^2\ =\ 1.44P$
Let the amount invested in Scheme A be aP and the amount invested in Scheme B be bP.
The amount in Scheme A after two years becomes 0.9aP.
The amount in Scheme B after two years becomes 1.5bP.
Since he made no profit, the amount from the schemes must be equal to the money to be paid.
0.9aP + 1.5bP = 1.44P ----(1)
and we also know that a + b = 1 ---(2)
Equation (1) becomes,
0.9a + 1.5b = 1.44  ---(3)
Equation (2) * 0.9 becomes,
0.9a + 0.9b = 0.9  ---(4)
Subtracting (4) from (3), we get,
0.6b = 0.54
$b\ =\ \dfrac{0.54}{0.6}\ =\ \dfrac{9}{10}$
$a\ =\ 1\ -\ \dfrac{9}{10}\ =\ \dfrac{1}{10}$
Ratio = $a\ :\ b\ =\ \dfrac{1}{10}\ :\ \dfrac{9}{10}\ =\ 1\ :\ 9$
Hence, the correct answer is option B.

questions.question_text: A wine shop seller uses a peculiar price-change scheme to sell his goods. He buys a 20-litre bottle of wine, increases its price by p% and later reduces the new price again by p%. After one such price-change cycle, the price of the bottle decreased by £ 15 and after the second price-change cycle, the price of the bottle stood at £ 48. At what price did the wine shop seller buy the wine bottle?
questions.solution_text:
Let $C$ be the cost price of the wine before the price change. After one cycle of price change, a reduction equal to  $C\left(\frac{p^2}{100^2}\right)$ takes place. It is stated that this value is  £ 15.
$C\left(\frac{p^2}{100^2}\right)=£15$...........(i)
Let the price after the reduction be $C'$; then: $C\left(1-\frac{p^2}{100^2}\right)=C'\ or\ \left(C-15\right)=C'$
After the second round of price change, we obtain:$C'\left(1-\frac{p^2}{100^2}\right)=£48$
We can re-write this as: $\left(C-15\right)\left(1-\frac{p^2}{100^2}\right)=48$
Replacing $\left(\frac{p^2}{100^2}\right)$ from (i), we get: $\left(C-15\right)\left(1-\frac{15}{C}\right)=48\ or\ \left(C-15\right)^2=48C$.....(ii)
We can simplify this as $C^2-78C+225=0$ and on solving, we get $C=£75$ [Cost price].
Hence, Option A is the correct choice.

questions.question_text: A and B move toward each other on a straight 150-meter track, with speeds of 2 m/s and 4 m/s, respectively. The moment they meet, a third person, C, starts from A's starting point and moves toward B's end at 7 m/s. After how many seconds will C be equidistant from both A and B (other than the point when C is starting)?
questions.solution_text:
A and B move toward each other on a straight 150-meter track, with speeds of 2 m/s and 4 m/s, respectively. Thus they will meet after 150/(2+4) = 25 seconds
Now, after they meet, C start from the same end as A, and moves towards the other end. Speed of C is 7 m/s. Let us assume that C is equidistant from both A and B after T seconds.
Total distance covered by A from A's end = $2(T+25)=2T+50$
Total distance covered by B from A's end = $150-4(T+25)=50-4T$
Total distance covered by C from A's end = $7T$
Now, the distance between A and C = $\left|5T-50\right|$, and the distance between B and C = $\left|11T-50\right|$. And, it is given that C is equidistant from both A and B. Thus, -
$\left|5T-50\right|=\left|11T-50\right|$
Case - 1 : $5T-50=11T-50$ => $T=0$ seconds. This is the time when A and B meet, and C started. But we have to find the time other than the point when C started.
Case - 2 : $5T-50=-11T+50$ => $16T=100$ => $T=6.25$ seconds.

questions.question_text: What is the least number that should be multiplied with 15! so that the product is a perfect square?
questions.solution_text:
We know that $10!=2^8\times3^4\times5^2\times7^1$
Extending 10! to 15!:
$15!=10!\times11\times12\times13\times14\times15$
$15!=2^8\times3^4\times5^2\times7^1\times11\times\left(3\times2^2\right)\times13\times\left(7\times2\right)\times\left(5\times3\right)$
Or, $15!=2^{11}\times3^6\times5^3\times7^2\times11\times13$
Now, we know that for sum to be a perfect square, all its prime factors should have an even number of power. 
However, we have, 2, 5, 11 and 13 that has an odd number of power.
If we multiplied 15! with the product of 2, 5, 11 and 13, we will get the even powers for all four. 
Hence, the least number that should be multiplied with 15! to get a perfect square: $2\times5\times11\times13=1430$

questions.question_text: Lewis and Max are racing in the opposite direction on a straight road of length $168$ km. After meeting, Max takes $108$ minutes and Lewis takes $\dfrac{100}{3}$ minutes to reach the other end. Find the speed of the faster person (in km/hr).
questions.solution_text:
Since Lewis and Max are racing in opposite directions on a straight road, we can use the formula for the time it takes them to meet.
The formula is: 
Meeting Time = square root of the product of time taken by the two persons to reach the respective ends after meeting
$=\sqrt{\ 108\times\ \dfrac{100}{3}}=\sqrt{\ 3600}=60$ minutes
So, total time for Lewis will be $=\dfrac{100}{3}+60=\dfrac{280}{3}$ minutes
Total time for Max will be $=108+60=168$ minutes
Clearly, Lewis takes less time to complete the race
So, he is the faster racer
So, speed of faster racer (Lewis) = Distance/Time = $\dfrac{168}{\dfrac{\dfrac{280}{3}}{60}}=\dfrac{168\times\ 60}{\dfrac{280}{3}}=108$ km/hr.
Alternate Explanation:
We also have another formula to find the ratio of speeds of Lewis and Max.
Ratio of their speeds = square root of the inverse ratio of time taken to reach other end after meeting.
Let, speed of Lewis be $S_L$ km/hr and speed of Max be $S_M$ km/hr
So, $\dfrac{S_M}{S_L}=\sqrt{\dfrac{\ \dfrac{100}{3}}{108}}=\sqrt{\ \dfrac{100}{3\times\ 108}}=\sqrt{\ \dfrac{25}{81}}=\dfrac{5}{9}$
From this we can infer, Lewis is the faster racer.
Also, we can say until meeting, distance covered by Max and Lewis is in the ratio 5:9
So, distance covered by Lewis until meeting = $\dfrac{9}{5+9}\times\ 168=\dfrac{9}{14}\times\ 168=108$ km
Meeting time (we calculated in the previous part)=60 minutes = 1 hour
So, speed of Lewis (faster runner)=$\dfrac{108}{1}=108$ km/hr.

questions.question_text: Find the sum of all integral values of $x$ for which the inequality $\dfrac{x^3+3x^2-481x-483}{x^3+4x^2-305x+300}\le0$ is satisfied
questions.solution_text:
We can see that the numerator becomes 0, if we put $x=-1$
So, $\left(x+1\right)$ is a factor of the numerator
Similarly, the denominator becomes 0, if we put $x=1$
So, $\left(x-1\right)$ is a factor of the denominator
The inequality looks like $\dfrac{\left(x+1\right)\left(x^2+2x-483\right)}{\left(x-1\right)\left(x^2+5x-300\right)}\le0$
The quadratics in the numerator and the denominator can be factorized as
$\dfrac{\left(x+1\right)\left(x+23\right)\left(x-21\right)}{\left(x-1\right)\left(x+20\right)\left(x-15\right)}\le0$
The LHS will be negative or 0 for the following values of $x$
$x\in\left[-23,\ -20\right)U\left[-1,\ 1\right)U\left(15,\ 21\right]$
Summing the values, we get
(-23)+(-22)+(-21)+(-1)+16+17+18+19+20+21 = 44.
Hence, the answer is 44.

questions.question_text:
A solid metal cube with side length 18 cm is melted and poured into two bowls, Bowl A and Bowl B, in the ratio 5:4 respectively. Bowl A is used to make cylindrical rods of radius 3 cm and height 8 cm, and Bowl B is used to make spherical balls of radius 3 cm. Due to surface finishing, each rod uses 10% more material than its geometric volume, and each ball uses 5% more. If all the metal is used, what is the maximum total number of rods and balls that can be made?

Assume that $\pi=\frac{22}{7}$
questions.solution_text:
The volume of the cube:
$Side^3=18^3=5832\ cm^3$
The total volume is divided into Bowl A and Bowl B in the ratio 5:4. Thus, the volume allocated to
Bowl A: $\dfrac{5}{9}\times5832\ cm^3\ =\ 3240\ cm^3$
Bowl B: $\dfrac{4}{9}\times5832\ cm^3\ =\ 2592\ cm^3$
Bowl A is used to make cylindrical rod with radius 3 cm and height 8 cm. So, the volume of each rod:
$\pi r^2h=\frac{22}{7}\times3^2\times8=226.285\ cm^3$
Since we need an additional 10% of the material equal to the rod's volume for furnishing and polishing, the total volume required to make a rod = $226.285\ \times\ 1.1=248.9135\ cm^3$
Let the maximum number of rods that can be made be x
Hence, $248.9135x\le3240$ 
$x\le13.016$
Hence, there can be a maximum of 13 formed. 
Similarly, Bowl B is used to make spherical Balls:
The volume of each spherical ball with radius 3 cm is:$\frac{4}{3}\pi\ r^3=\frac{4}{3}\times\frac{22}{7}\times\ 3\ ^3$
Since we need an additional 5% of the material equal to the ball's volume for furnishing and polishing, the total volume required to make a ball = $\frac{4}{3}\times\frac{22}{7}\times\ 3\ ^3\times1.05=118.8\ cm^3$
Let the maximum number of balls that can be made be y. 
Hence, $118.8y\le2592$
$y\le21.8$
Hence, the maximum number of balls and rods that can be formed = 13 + 21 = 34

questions.question_text: In 2020, the ratio of the area of water bodies to the forest area to the land area is 1:2:2. Every year, 12.5% of the forest area becomes land, and after that, m% of the water body area becomes forest. Find the value of m, if the ratio of the water body area in 2021 to the land area in 2022 is 3:10.
questions.solution_text:
Let us assume the proportionality constant for the first ratio to be 8t. So, in 2020, the water body area will be 8t, the forest area will be 16t, and the land area will be 16t.
For convenience, let us assume $\frac{m}{100}=x$
Land area in 2021 = $\frac{1}{8}\cdot16t+16t\ \ = 18t$
Forest area in 2021 = $x\cdot 8t+14t\ = 14t+8xt$
Water area in 2021 = $1-\frac{m}{100}\cdot 8t\ =(1-x)8t$
Water area in 2022 = $1-\frac{m}{100}\cdot (1-x)8t\ =(1-x)(1-x)8t$
Land area in 2022 = 18t+$\frac{\left(14t+8xt\right)}{8}$
We are told that the ratio of water area in 2021 to land area in 2022 = 3:10
$\frac{\left(1-x\right)8t}{18t+\frac{\left(14t+8xt\right)}{8}}=\frac{3}{10}$
T is common in every term in both numerator and denominator. So, we can cancel out t.
$\frac{\left(1-x\right)8}{18+\frac{\left(14+8x\right)}{8}}=\frac{3}{10}$
$\frac{\left(1-x\right)64}{144+\left(14+8x\right)}=\frac{3}{10}$
$\frac{\left(1-x\right)64}{158+8x}=\frac{3}{10}$
$\left(1-x\right)640=474+24x$
$640=474+24x+640x$
$\Rightarrow$ 664x = 166
x = 0.25
So, m = 25%

questions.question_text: A boat travels at 10 km/hr in still water. The river's current flows at 2 km/hr. The boat covers a distance of 48 km from point A to point B and then returns the same 48 km from B to A. On the following day, if the boat's speed increases by X%, its total travel time for the round trip decreases by 30%. Find the value of X, assuming the river's speed remains constant on both days.
questions.solution_text:
Speed of boat = 10 km/hr
Speed of river = 2 km/hr
Distance from A to B = 48 km (Downstream)
Speed of (boat + river) in downstream from A to B = 10+2 = 12 km/hr
Total time taken by boat from A to B = 48/12 = 4 hours.
Now, the boat moves from B to A upstream.
Distance travelled = 48 km
Speed of boat and river combined in upstream from B to A = 10-2 = 8 km/hr
Total time taken by boat from B to A = 48/8 = 6 hours.
Total Journey time from A to B and B to A on day 1 = 4+6 = 10 hours.
The next day, the speed of the boat is increased by X%.
Let us assume the boat's speed is now B km/hr.
Speed of river is same on both days, so it is 2 km/hr.
Now, it is given that the to and fro journey from A to B and B to A on day 2 will take 30% less time.
Hence, on day it will take 7 hours. (10*0.7 = 7)
Distance = 48 km
Speed of (boat + river) in downstream from A to B = (B + 2) km/hr
Total time taken by boat from A to B = $\dfrac{48}{\left(B+2\right)}$ hours
Similarly, speed of (boat+river) in upstream from B to A = (B - 2) km/hr
Distance = 48 km
Total time taken = $\dfrac{48}{\left(B-2\right)}$ hours
We know, $\dfrac{48}{B+2}+\dfrac{48}{\left(B-2\right)}=7$
$48\left(2B\right)=7\left(B^2-4\right)$
=> $7B^2-96B-28=0$
$B\ =\dfrac{96\pm\ \sqrt{96^2+\left(4\times7\times28\right)}}{2\times7}$
$B\ =\dfrac{96\pm\ \sqrt{9216+784}}{2\times7}$
$B\ =\dfrac{96\pm\ \sqrt{10000}}{2\times7}$
$B\ =\dfrac{196}{14}$ or $B\ =\dfrac{-4}{14}$ (Negative value not possible)
B = 14 km/hr
Thus, % the increase in the boat's speed was 40% (10 to 14 is a 40% increase)

questions.question_text: We are given an isosceles right-angled triangle EBC with the right angle at C and |BC| = 2. Calculate the area of the trapezoid ABCD (AB || CD) in which E is the midpoint of AD.
questions.solution_text:
Let F be the midpoint of the side BC, and let us consider the right-angled triangle EFC.
We are given that the length of BC is 2cm, which makes EC also 2cm, as it is an isosceles triangle. As F is the midpoint of BC, the lengths of CF and FB are 1 cm each.
The length of EF can be calculated using the Pythagoras Theorem,
$EF^2\ =\ EC^2\ +\ CF^2$
$EF^2\ =\ 4\ +\ 1\ =\ 5$
$EF=\sqrt{\ 5}$
The value of h can be calculated as,
Area of CEF = $\dfrac{1}{2}\times\ CF\ \times\ EC\ =\ \dfrac{1}{2}\ \times\ EF\ \times\ h$
$1\ \times\ 2=\ \sqrt{\ 5}\ \times\ h$
$h\ =\ \dfrac{2}{\sqrt{\ 5}}$
The area of the trapezium can be calculated as 
$\dfrac{1}{2}\ \times\ 2h\ \times\ \left(DC\ +\ AB\right)\ =\ h\ \times\ \left(2\ \times\ EF\right)\ =\ 2\times\ h\ \times\ EF$
Area = $2\ \times\ \dfrac{2}{\sqrt{\ 5}}\ \times\ \sqrt{\ 5}\ =\ 4$
Hence, the correct answer is option B.

questions.question_text: The three altitudes of a triangle are 60, 48 and 80. Find the area of the triangle.
questions.solution_text:
In a triangle, the ratio of the altitudes is inverse to the ratio of the corresponding sides. Let the sides be a, b and c. 
Hence, if the altitudes are 60, 48 and 80, a : b : c = $\dfrac{1}{60}:\dfrac{1}{48}:\dfrac{1}{80}$
Upon solving, we get, a : b : c = 4 : 5 : 3.
Now, let the side a = 4x so the side b and c will be 5x and 3x. 
Using Heron's formula: $\sqrt{s\left(s-a\right)\left(s-b\right)\left(s-c\right)}$
$s=\dfrac{\left(4x+5x+3x\right)}{2}=6x$
Putting the values in the heron's formula, we get: $\sqrt{6x\times2x\times x\times3x}=6x^2$
Hence, the area of the triangle = $6x^2$
We also know that Area of the triangle = $\dfrac{1}{2}\times Base\times Height$
Putting the values, we get, $6x^2=\dfrac{1}{2}\times4x\times60$
Upon solving, we get, x = 20.
Hence, putting the values in $6x^2$, we get the area of the triangle to be 2400 $cm^2$

questions.question_text: Two trains start 1800 km apart. Train A departs Shimla at 8:00 AM at 60 km/h. Train B departs Pune at 10:00 AM at 90 km/h. A bird begins flying from Pune at 8:00 AM at 120 km/h towards Shimla. When the bird meets Train A, it starts shuttling between the trains until they meet. Calculate the total distance (in km) flown by the bird.
questions.solution_text:
As both the bird and Train A start at the same time, we can calculate the time it takes to meet using relative velocity.
The combined velocity will be 60 km/h + 120 km/h = 180 km/h
So, the time taken to meet will be $\dfrac{1800}{180}=10$ hours
In this time, the bird would have flown $10\times120=1200$ km
Train A would have covered 1800-1200 = 600 km
Train B started 2 hours after Train A, so it would have travelled for 8 hours
Train B would have covered $8\times90=720$ km
So, the remaining distance between Train A and B will be 1800 - 600 - 720 = 480 km
Now the time taken to cover this 480 km by the relative velocity of Train A and B will be
$\dfrac{480}{60+90}=\dfrac{480}{150}=3.2$ hours
In this time the bird will fly $3.2\times120=384$ km
So, the total distance covered by the bird is 1200 + 384 = 1584 km.
Hence, the answer is 1584.

questions.question_text: Anant buys a circular plot of land. He carved out a triangle using a chord that subtends 150 degrees at the centre and the circle's centre. The cost per unit square of flooring the triangular plot to the cost of flooring the rest of the land is 5:3. If the flooring costs Anant 13900 rupees, find the cost of flooring only the triangular plot. (Use $\pi=\frac{22}{7}$)
questions.solution_text:
Let us draw the figure in question,
We are told that AOB is cut away and floored at a rate different from the rest. 
The area of the triangle AOB will be, $\dfrac{1}{2}r^2\sin150$, considering the radius of this circle to be r. 
The rest of the area will be, $\pi r^2-\dfrac{r^2}{4}$
Let us take the flooring rate per unit square in AOB, which will be 5X, and for the rest of the circle, it will be 3X. 
The ratio of the total costs will be, 
$\dfrac{\dfrac{r^2}{4}\left(5X\right)}{\left(\pi r^2-\dfrac{r^2}{4}\right)\left(3X\right)}=\dfrac{\dfrac{5}{4}}{\left(\dfrac{22}{7}-\dfrac{1}{4}\right)\left(3\right)}=\dfrac{35}{243}$
We are given the total cost as 13900. We can find the individual cost of the triangle alone using the ratio. 
$\dfrac{35}{278}\left(13900\right)=1750$
Hence, the answer is 1750.

questions.question_text: A cricket coach assigns numbers 1 to 11 to his players according to their batting numbers. During their warmup, they're made to stand in a line. What is the probability that the players with composite numbers assigned are arranged in increasing order from first to last?
questions.solution_text:
The composite numbers from 1 to 11 are 4,6,8,9,10. So, we need the number of ways these numbers come in numerical order. There is only one way of arranging these numbers in numerical order.
We can arrange the 11 players in 11 positions. We should select five places to arrange the players assigned composite numbers out of these.
That can be done in $^{11}C_5$ ways. We can arrange other players for the remaining six positions, which can be done in 6! ways. 
The total number of ways this can be done = $^{11}C_5\cdot6!\ =\dfrac{\left(11\cdot10\cdot9\cdot8\cdot7\right)}{5!}\cdot6!\ =\left(11\cdot10\cdot9\cdot8\cdot7\right)\cdot6$
The number of ways to arrange all the players in 11 positions is 11!.
Required probability = $\dfrac{\left(11\cdot10\cdot9\cdot8\cdot7\cdot6\right)}{11!}=\dfrac{1}{5\cdot4\cdot3\cdot2\cdot1}=\dfrac{1}{120}$

questions.question_text: Three natural numbers, $P, Q$ and $R$, are such that $P\times Q\times R=360,\ PQ+R=39\ $ and $QR+P=53\ $. Find $P+R-Q$.

So, we are given that P, Q and R are natural numbers.
PQ+R=39....... Equation 1
QR + P = 53........ Equation 2
PQR = 360......... Equation 3
From equation 1, we can get, 
R = 39 - PQ....... Equation 4
Putting equation 4 in equation 2, we get,
Q(39-PQ) + P = 53
or, $39Q-Q^2P+P=53$
Now, we can notice that this equation is heavily dependent on Q as the coefficient of Q is 39 and the final outcome is 53 which is quite close. 
Hence, we can try putting values for Q and see what we get:
If Q = 1, 39 = 53 which is not possible. 
If Q = 2, 25 = 3P which is not possible as P has to be a natural number. 
If Q = 3, 64 = 8P and we get, P = 8.
Putting Q and P in equation 3, we get, 
3*8*R = 360
R = 15
Hence, P + R - Q = 8 + 15 - 3 = 20

questions.question_text: A number S has 36 factors. Find the difference between the maximum and the minimum number of factors $ S^2$ can have.
questions.solution_text:
We are told that a number has 36 factors. 
Let us represent the number as follows, $S=p^aq^br^c..$
The number of factors would be: (a+1)(b+1)(c+1)...
When the number is squared, we have the following, $S^2=p^{2a}q^{2b}r^{2c}..$
The number of factors will be: (2a+1)(2b+1)(2c+1)...
The smallest number of factors for $S^2$ will be when the number $S$ has only one prime factor and that is raised to the power 35. 
That time the number of factors for $S^2$ will be (2(35)+1)=71. 
The largest number of factors for $ S^2$ will be when the number $S$ has as many prime factors as possible. We can prime factorise 36 to get the following: $36=2\times2\times3\times3$ 
The prime factors will be raised to the power 1, 1, 2, and 2, respectively. 
That time the number of factors for $S^2$ will be, (2+1)(2+1)(4+1)(4+1) which will equal 225 factors. 
Hence, the difference between the maximum and minimum number of factors will be 225-71=154.
Therefore, the answer is 154.

Sarah purchased notebooks from a supplier at Rs. 150 per notebook. For every additional notebook she sells after the first one, the selling price decreases by Rs. 8 compared to the selling price of the previous notebook. Sarah makes a 120% profit by selling six notebooks using this pricing strategy. What is Sarah's profit (in Rs.) from selling five notebooks?
questions.solution_text:
Sarah buys each notebook for Rs. 150.
We are told Sarah makes a 120% profit by selling 6 notebooks. Let the selling price of the first notebook be x. The selling prices for the 6 notebooks are:
1st notebook: x
2nd notebook: x−8
3rd notebook: x−16
4th notebook: x−24
5th notebook: x−32
6th notebook: x−40
Total SP = x + (x−8) + (x−16) + (x−24) + (x−32) + (x−40)
Total SP = 6x − (8+16+24+32+40) = 6x−120
We know the profit is 120% of the total cost price. The total cost price for 6 notebooks is:
Total CP = 6 × 150 = 900
The profit of 120% on Rs. 900 is: Profit=1.2 × 900 = 1080
Total SP = Total CP + Profit = 900 + 1080 = 1980
6x − 120 = 1980 
6x = 2100 OR x = 350
So, the selling price of the first notebook is Rs. 350.
Now, the total selling price of the first 5 notebooks: 350 + 342 + 334 + 326 + 318 = 1670
Cost price of 5 notebooks: 5*150 = 750
Hence, the profit made by Sarah: 1670 - 750 = Rs. 920

questions.question_text: Find the sum of values of x which satisfy the expression, $\log_4x^4+\log_{0.25}\left(x^{\log_2x}\right)=0$
questions.solution_text:
The given expression is $\log_4x^4+\log_{0.25}\left(x^{\log_2x}\right)=0$
This can be written as, $\frac{1}{2}\log_2x^4-\frac{1}{2}\log_2\left(x^{\log_2x}\right)=0$
This can be simplified to, $\log_2x^4=\log_2\left(x^{\log_2x}\right)$
We can write this as, $4\log_2x=\left(\log_2x\right)\left(\log_2x\right)$
Considering $\log_2x=z$, we write the equation as, $4z=z^2$
Here, z=0 or z=4
For z=0, $\log_2x=0$ x=1
For z=4, $\log_2x=4$, x=16
Sum of values of x will be 17.

questions.question_text: Two friends, Rohan and Karan, are working on a project. Together, they can complete the project in 15 days. However, if Rohan completes one-fourth of the project and then Karan takes over to complete the remaining three-fourth of the project, they will finish the project in 28 days. How many days would Rohan alone take to complete the entire project if it is known that the number of days taken by each is an integer?
questions.solution_text:
Let Rohan can complete the project in 'R' number of days and Karan can do the same in 'K' days.
So, the total work done by Rohan and Karan in a day will be $\dfrac{1}{R}\ \&\ \dfrac{1}{K}$ respectively. 
We are given that both of them complete the project in 15 days so the work done by together in a day = $\dfrac{1}{15}$
Or, we can say, $\dfrac{1}{R}+\dfrac{1}{K}=\dfrac{1}{15}$ ....... Equation 1
Further, we are given that if Rohan completes one-fourth of the project and then Karan takes over to complete the remaining three-fourth of the project, they will finish the project in 28 days.
Since Rohan complete the whole project in R number of days, it will take him R/4 days to complete one fourth of the project. 
Similarly, Karan will take 3K/4 days to complete the remaining the project. 
This way, they complete the project in 28 days. 
Hence, we can say, $\dfrac{R}{4}+\dfrac{3K}{4}=28$
Or, $R+3K=112$ or, we can say, $R=112-3K$
Putting R in equation 1, 
$\dfrac{\left(112-3k+k\right)}{k\left(112-3k\right)}=\dfrac{1}{15}$
$15\left(112-2k\right)=112k-3k^2$
$3k^2-142k+1680=0$
We  know 70 + 27 = 142 and 70*72 = 3*1680
Hence, $\left(3k-70\right)\left(k-24\right)=0$
We get K = 70/3 or 24
Since it is given that the number of days taken by them is integral, we can eliminate 70/3.
Now,  If K = 24, R = 40

questions.question_text: A container has pipes of different types: Type I, Type II, and Type III, where Type I is an outlet pipe and Type II and Type III are inlet pipes. A Type I pipe can empty the container in 1 hour, and Type II and Type III pipes together can fill it in 50 minutes. It takes 5 Type II and 1 Type I pipe to fill the container in 24 minutes. How much time will it take Type III to fill the container?
questions.solution_text:
A container has pipes of different types: Type I, Type II, and Type III.
Inlet Pipes = Type II and Type III, Outlet Pipe = Type I
Type I pipe can empty container in 1 hour or 60 minutes.
Type I = 60 minutes
Type II and Type III pipes to fill it in 50 minutes.
Type II + Type III = 50 minutes
It takes 5 Type II and 1 Type I pipe to fill the container in 24 minutes.
5 Type II + Type I = 24 minutes.
Let the volume of the container be the LCM of (60,50,24) = 600 litres.
Therefore, in 1 minute,
Type I pipe can empty the container with a volume of 10 litres (600/60 = 10)
Type II + Type III can fill the container with a volume of 12 litres (600/50 = 12)
5 Type II + Type I can fill the container with a volume of 25 litres (600/24 = 25)
5 Type II + Type I = 25
5 Type II - 10 = 25
5 Type II  = 35 litres in 1 minute.
Type II = 7 litres in 1 minute.
Type II + Type III = 12 litres in 1 minute.
7 + Type III = 12 litres in 1 minute
Thus, Type III pipe can fill 5 litres in 1 minute.
Therefore, the time taken by Pipe III to fill the container = 600/5 = 120 minutes.
Or 2 hours.

questions.question_text: A mixture of orange lemonade has orange juice and lemon juice in a ratio of 7:2, and another mixture of kiwi lemonade has kiwi juice and lemon juice in a 2:5 ratio. In a 100L beaker with 50L of water, an unknown quantity of orange lemonade and kiwi lemonade is added to fill up the beaker. What is the sum of the quantity of orange juice and kiwi juice in the beaker(in litres) if the ratio of the concentration of orange juice and lemon juice in the mixture is 14:9?
questions.solution_text:
Given that the ratio of orange juice and lemon juice in orange lemonade is 7:2 and the ratio of kiwi juice and lemon juice in kiwi lemonade as 2:5. In a 100l beaker, if 50l is water, then the rest of the solution is made of orange lemonade and kiwi lemonade.
Let the quantity of orange lemonade be 9x, and kiwi lemonade is 7y. Then orange juice becomes 7x, kiwi juice becomes 2y and lemon juice becomes 2x + 5y
9x + 7y = 50  --(1)
we are also given ratio of orange juice and lemon juice as 14:9, so orange juice in the mixture is 7x, and lemon juice is 2x + 5y.
$\dfrac{7x}{2x\ +\ 5y}\ =\ \dfrac{14}{9}$
$9x\ =\ 4x\ +\ 10y$
$x\ =\ 2y$
Substituting it in equation 1, we get,
9(2y) + 7y = 50
25y = 50
y = 2 and x = 4.
Quantity of orange juice = 7x = 7* 4 = 28
Quantity of kiwi juice = 2y = 2 * 2 = 4
Sum of the quantities = 28 + 4 = 32.
Hence, the correct answer is option C.

questions.question_text: If $2^{2x+3}+2^{x+3}=160$, find the integral value of $x$.
questions.solution_text:
We have: $2^{2x+3}+2^{x+3}=160$
We see $2^3=8$ is common in left hand side and right hand side, so dividing both sides with $2^3$
We get: $2^{2x+3-3}+2^{x+3-3}=\frac{160}{8}$
$2^{2x}+2^{x}=20$
Or,$\left(2^x\right)^{^2}+2^x=20$
Let $2^x=a$
We get: $a^2+a=20$
$a^2+a-20=0$
$a^2+5a-4a+20=0$
$a\left(a+5\right)-4\left(a+5\right)=0$
$\left(a-4\right)\left(a+5\right)=0$
Now, we have $a=4\ or\ -5$
Equating both with $2^x$
$2^x=-5$ is not possible for any integral value of x. 
$2^x=4\ \longrightarrow\ x=2$
Hence, x = 2

questions.question_text: In a Comic-Con challenge, four men and four women need to be selected. Team Marvel consists of five men and seven women, while Team DC consists of four men and six women. How many different ways can people be selected for the challenge, ensuring that five people are chosen from Team Marvel and three people from Team DC?
questions.solution_text:
We are told 4M and 4W are to be selected. It is given that 5 people from Team Marvel are to be selected and 3 from Team DC. 
Team Marvel consists of 5M and 7W. 
Team DC consists of 4M and 6W. 
5 people from Team Marvel can be selected as, 
(4M, 1W), (3M, 2W), (2M, 3W), (1M, 4W)
To complement this, the 3 people from Team DC can be selected as, 
(0M, 3W), (1M, 2W), (2M, 1W), (3M, 0W)
Combination 1: (4M, 1W)+(0M, 3W), this can be chosen in $^5C_4\cdot^7C_1\cdot^6C_3$
Combination 2: (3M, 2W)+(1M, 2W), this can be chosen in $^5C_3\cdot^7C_2\cdot^4C_1\cdot^6C_2$
Combination 3: (2M, 3W)+(2M, 1W), this can be chosen in  $^5C_2\cdot^7C_3\cdot^4C_2\cdot^6C_1$
Combination 4: (1M, 4W)+(3M, 0W), this can be chosen in $^5C_1\cdot^7C_4\cdot^4C_3$
Combination 1: (5)(7)(20)=700
Combination 2: (10)(21)(4)(15)=12600
Combination 3: (10)(35)(6)(6)=12600
Combination 4: (5)(35)(4)=700
Total combination being the sum of them, which is 26,600 ways.

questions.question_text: Ravi buys milk using a container that holds 1250 ml, but pays only for 1000 ml. While selling, he adds 80 ml of water to every 920 ml of milk and marks up the cost price by 60%. What is the maximum discount he can offer on the marked price while still making a 100% profit?
questions.solution_text:
Let the cost price of 1000 ml of milk be Rs. X.
Ravi got 1250 ml of milk for the cost price of 1000 ml. 
So, the effective cost price = Rs. $\dfrac{X}{1250}\times1000\ =\dfrac{X}{1.25}$
Now, in every litre of milk, he has added 80 ml of water, so the actual milk he is selling per litre = 1000ml - 80 ml = 920 ml.
So, the cost price of this 920 ml of milk: $\dfrac{X}{1.25}\times0.92$
Now, Ravi wants to earn 100% profit, so the selling price has to be equal to twice of $\dfrac{X}{1.25}\times0.92$.
Hence, selling price = $2\times\dfrac{X}{1.25}\times0.92$
Now, he marked up the cost price by 60%, so the marked price = $1.6X$
Let the maximum discount he can allow be z%.
So, the selling price = MP - Discount
$1.6X\times\left(1-\dfrac{z}{100}\right)$
This selling price should be equal to twice the cost price. 
Hence, $1.6X\times\left(1-\dfrac{z}{100}\right)$ = $2\times\dfrac{X}{1.25}\times0.92$
z = 8%

Determine the total interest paid (in rupees) over the three years.

questions.question_text: Srinu and Bhanu can complete the work together in 30 days. If Bhanu works for n days, Srinu can complete the remaining work in 55 days. If Srinu works for n days, Bhanu can complete the remaining work in 39 days. How many days will it take to finish the work if Bhanu works on the first half of the work and Srinu finishes the remaining work?
questions.solution_text:
Let us assume the work done by Srinu in one day as S units and Bhanu as B units.
Total work = 30S+30B $\rightarrow 1$
We are told that if Bhanu works for n days, Srinu can complete the remaining work in 55 days.
In this case, the total work = nB+55S $\rightarrow 2$
Upon equating eq 1 and 2, we get 30S+30B = nB+55S
25S = (30-n)B
$\dfrac{S}{B}=\dfrac{\left(30-n\right)}{25}$
We are also told that if Srinu works for n days, Bhanu can complete the remaining work in 39 days.
In this case, the total work = 39B+nS $\rightarrow 3$
Upon equating eq 1 and 3, we get 30S+30B = 39B+nS
9B = (30-n)S
$\dfrac{S}{B}=\dfrac{9}{\left(30-n\right)}$
We can equate both equations. $\dfrac{\left(30-n\right)}{25}=\dfrac{9}{\left(30-n\right)}$
$(30-n)^2=225$
$(30-n)=\pm15$
$n=15\ or\ 45$
But only n = 15 satisfies the condition that Srinu and Bhanu can complete the work together in 30 days
B:S = 5:3
So, Bhanu does five units of work in one day, and Srinu does three in one day. Total work = 8*30 = 240
Time taken to finish the first half by Bhanu = $\dfrac{120}{5}=24$
Time taken by Srinu to finish the second half = $\dfrac{120}{3}=40$
Total time taken = 24+40 = 64

questions.question_text: The time zones of cities A, B and C are AST, BST and CST respectively. A flight which travels at a constant speed of 600 kmph leaves A at 10:00 A.M AST and reaches B at 2:00 P.M BST. After halting for an hour at B, the flight reaches C at 6:00 P.M CST. If the distance between A and B is 3600 kms and between B and C is 1200 kms. Which of the following can be the distance between A and C assuming cities A and B lies on same latitude .
questions.solution_text:
It is provided that the speed of the flight is 600 kmph. 
Distance between A and B = 3600 kms.
Time taken from A to B = $\dfrac{\ 3600}{600}$ = 6 hours journey from A to B .
Here, as it is given that flight starts at 10 am AST and reaches B at 2 pm BST . As we deduced 6 hours journey from A to B, it implies it should have been {10 am + 6 hours} AST = 4 pm AST = 2 pm BST {Inference 1}.
Now, after halting for 1 hour at B, flight starts its travel towards C. That is given flight starts at 3 pm BST and reaches C at 6 pm CST. 
We also know the distance between B & C is given to be 1200 kms. As flight travels at 600 kmph : 
Time taken from B to C = $\dfrac{\ 1200}{600}$ = 2 hours journey from B to C .
Here, as the flight starts at 3 pm BST at B, it should be reaching C in 2 hours i.e by 5 pm BST . And it is said flight reaches C at 6 pm CST .
it implies : 5 pm BST = 6 pm CST {Inference 2}. 
By using Inference 1 & Inference 2, we can conclude that : If time at B is "X" hours then it is {X+2} hours in city A & {X+1} hours in city C.(Example : 2 pm at BST = 3 pm at CST = 4 pm at AST) . 
B = X hrs BST
C = {X + 1} hrs CST
A = {X + 2} hrs AST
Due to rotation of earth, as one moves from West to east the time advances with longitudinal difference . Hence it can be said that : 
1. C lies to the East of B.
2. A lies to the East of C. 
Hence, it can be deduced that C lies in between A & B only. 
From the triangle inequality we can say that : {1200 + D} > 3600 
So, D > 2400 kms .
Minimum case : 
If, all three cities are collinear, then we get $D_{\min}$ = 3600-1200 = 2400 kms. 
Maximum case : 
As we deduced that city C must lie towards east of B only (i.e towards right of B) . The maximum distance AC can be made possible if CB is perpendicular to AB :
It will form a right angled triangle with right angled at B : 
$D^2=1200^2+3600^2$ 
$D_{\max}$ = 3794.7 kms.
Therefore, the possible value of "D" should be greater than or equal to 2400 kms and definitely less than or equal to  3794.7 kms .
Hence, the only satisfying option is 2700 km.

questions.question_text: What is the minimum value of the expression $\left|x-2\right|+\left|x-5\right|+\left|x+8\right|-\left|x+15\right|+x-5$?
questions.solution_text:
The minimum value will always lie at the inflection points in such questions.
Here, the points are 2, 5, -8, -15.
At x = 5, $\left|x-2\right|+\left|x-5\right|+\left|x+8\right|-\left|x+15\right|+x-5$ = 3+0+13-20+5-5 = -4
At x = 2, $\left|x-2\right|+\left|x-5\right|+\left|x+8\right|-\left|x+15\right|+x-5$ = 0+3+10-17+2-5 = -7
At x = -8, $\left|x-2\right|+\left|x-5\right|+\left|x+8\right|-\left|x+15\right|+x-5$ = 10+13+0-7-8-5 = 3
At x = -15, $\left|x-2\right|+\left|x-5\right|+\left|x+8\right|-\left|x+15\right|+x-5$ = 17+20+7-0-15-5 = 24
So, the answer is -7.

questions.question_text: Let AB be the diameter of the circle, and C be the point on AB such that AC: CB is 6:7. Let D be the point on the circle such that CD is perpendicular to AB, and DE be the diameter passing through the centre of the circle. Find the ratio of the area of $\triangle ABD$ to the area of $\triangle CDE$.
questions.solution_text:
Let the value of length AC be 6x, and the length of CB be 7x. Let the radius of the circle be r.
We know that the length of AB has to be 2r.
$2r\ =\ 6x\ +\ 7x\ =\ 13x$
$r\ =\ 6.5x$
AO = 6.5x = 6x + CO
CO = 6.5x - 6x = 0.5
We can see that CO is the median of the triangle CDE, and the area of CDE = 2 * area of COD
Area of COD = $\dfrac{1}{2}\ \times\ CO\ \times\ CD\ =\ \dfrac{1}{2}\ \times\ 0.5x\ \times\ CD\ =\ \dfrac{x}{4}\ \times\ CD$
Area of CDE = 2 * Area of COD = $2\times\ \dfrac{x}{4}\ \times\ CD\ =\ \dfrac{x}{2}\ \times\ CD$
Area of ADB = $\dfrac{1}{2}\ \times\ AB\ \times\ CD\ =\ \dfrac{1}{2}\ \times\ 13x\ \times\ CD\ =\ \dfrac{13x}{2}\ \times\ CD$
$\dfrac{Area\ of\ ADB}{Area\ of\ CDE}\ =\ \dfrac{\frac{13x}{2}\ \times\ CD}{\frac{x}{2}\ \times\ CD}\ =\ 13$
Hence, the correct answer is option B.

questions.question_text: Prakash works as a sales manager at Reddy Electronics and has a monthly revenue target of selling 40 air conditioners at a profit of 10%. However, if he marks up the price by 'M' per cent on the cost price and then offers a discount of 20% on the marked price, he can complete his revenue target by just selling 25 air conditioners. Prakash has decided to increase the marked price by 25% further and is not offering any discount. Find the number of air conditioners he needs to sell to achieve his monthly revenue target.
questions.solution_text:
Let the Cost Price (CP) of one AC be ₹100
Since profit is 10%, the selling price in the first case:
SP=100+10% of 100=₹110
So, Revenue target=v40×110 = ₹4400
Second Scenario (Markup = M%, Discount = 20%, sells 25 ACs)
Let markup be M%, so marked price = ₹100 x (1+M/100)
Selling price after 20% discount:
SP = ₹100×(1+M/100)×0.8
Revenue from selling 25 ACs =  25×₹100×(1+M/100)×0.8= ₹4400
Divide both sides by 100:
25×(1+M/100)×0.8=44
1+M/100 = 2.2
M = 1.2
So the markup is 120%.
New Scenario: Further 25% Increase on Marked Price, No Discount
New Marked Price: Old MP = ₹100×2.2 = ₹220
New MP = ₹220×1.25= ₹275
SP = ₹275
We want to get total revenue = ₹4400
So, Number of ACs = 4400/275 =16
Prakash needs to sell 16 air conditioners to achieve his revenue target.

In $\triangle ABC\ $, D is a point on line AB such that AD:BD=3:4 and E is a point on AC such that AE:CE=4:5.

What is area of quadilateral DECB ?

(given area of $\ \triangle ABC=126\ cm^2\ $)
questions.solution_text:
We can make a figure like this,
Since, $\ AD:BD=3:4$
$\dfrac{AD}{BD}=\dfrac{3}{4}=>\dfrac{AD}{AB}=\dfrac{3}{4+3}=\dfrac{3}{7}$
Also,
$\dfrac{AE}{CE}=\dfrac{4}{5}=>\dfrac{AE}{AC}=\dfrac{4}{4+5}=\dfrac{4}{9}$
Now, $\dfrac{area\ of\ \triangle\ ADE}{Area\ of\ \triangle\ ABC}=\dfrac{\dfrac{1}{2}\cdot AD.AE.\sin A}{\dfrac{1}{2}\cdot AB\cdot AC\cdot\sin A}$
$\dfrac{area\ of\ \triangle\ ADE}{126}=\dfrac{3}{7}\cdot\dfrac{4}{9}=\dfrac{4}{21}$
So, $area\ of\triangle\ ADE\ =\ \dfrac{4}{21}\times\ 126=24\ cm^2$
So, area of quadilateral DECB = $126-24=102\ cm^2$ 
Answer: $102\ cm^2$

questions.solution_text:
Let 3x and 4x be initial amounts of milk and water respectively.
Let 4y and 3y be the amounts of milk and water respectively after evaporation.
3(4y-3x)=2(3y-4x) ==> x=6y
Amount of milk evaporated = $\dfrac{7x}{3}$
Amount of water evaporated = $\dfrac{7x}{2}$
Amount of milk evaporated per minute = $\dfrac{2x}{5}$
Amount of water evaporated per minute = $\dfrac{3x}{5}$
For 50% concentration, amounts of both milk and water must be same.
3x - ($\dfrac{2x}{5}$*k) = 4x - ($\dfrac{3x}{5}$*k)
==> k = 5minutes
==> excess time boiled = $\dfrac{5}{6}$ minutes

questions.question_text: The ratio of interior angles of two regular polygons with $n$ and $m$ sides respectively is 4: 5. The difference in the number of diagonals of these polygons is 45. Find the number of diagonals of a regular polygon with $\left(2m-n\right)$ sides. ($n,\ m\le30$)
questions.solution_text:
We know that the interior angle increases with the number of sides of the polygon.
As the ratio of interior angles of two regular polygons with $n$ and $m$ sides respectively is 4 : 5
So, $n<m$
We know that the interior angle of a polygon with $n$ sides is $\dfrac{180\left(n-2\right)}{n}$
So, given $\dfrac{\dfrac{180\left(n-2\right)}{n}}{\dfrac{180\left(m-2\right)}{m}}=\dfrac{4}{5}$
$\dfrac{\left(n-2\right)}{n}\times\dfrac{m}{\left(m-2\right)}=\dfrac{4}{5}$
$\dfrac{mn-2m}{mn-2n}=\dfrac{4}{5}$
$5mn-10m=4mn-8n$
or, $mn-10m=-8n$ 
$m=\dfrac{8n}{10-n}$
As number of sides of both polygons is a natural number greater than 3
$n\ge3$
Also, $n<10$ for the denominator to be positive
Now trying different values of $n$ to get integral values of $m$
1. $n=5$
$m=\dfrac{8\times5}{10-5}=8$
2. $n=6$
$m=\dfrac{8\times6}{10-6}=12$
3. $n=8$
$m=\dfrac{8\times8}{10-8}=32$ not possible as both $n,\ m\le30$
Hence, only two cases satisfy.
Now, given the difference in the number of diagonals of these polygons is 45
CASE 1 $n=5$, $m=8$
Diangonals for polygon $n$ is $^nC_2-n=^5C_2-5=5$
Diangonals for polygon $m$ is $^mC_2-m=^8C_2-8=20$
Difference = 20 - 5 = 15
Doesn't satisfy.
CASE 2 $n=6$, $m=12$
Diangonals for polygon $n$ is $^nC_2-n=^6C_2-6=9$
Diangonals for polygon $m$ is $^mC_2-m=^{12}C_2-12=54$
Difference = 54 - 9 = 45
Satisfies.
Hence, $n=6$ and $m=12$
So, the number of diagonals of a polygon with $2m-n=24-6=18$ sides is 
$^{18}C_2-18=135$

questions.question_text: Kushal invested an equal sum in two banks. The Bank of Hyderabad offers a 40% interest rate compounded quarterly, while the State Bank of India provides a 46% interest rate compounded annually. If the difference in interest earned from both banks over one year is ₹4,100, find the total interest earned from the Bank of Hyderabad in one year if it offered a 50% interest rate compounded semi-annually, with the investment amount remaining the same.
questions.solution_text:
Let us assume the total amount invested in each bank is 100000P
For Bank of Hyderabad
Principal amount = 100000P
Rate of interest = 40% compounding quarterly = 10% per quarter 
Time = 1 year = four cycles for each quarter.
Amount earned by Kushal in 1 year from Bank of Hyderabad = 100000P$\left(1.1\right)^4$
=> 146410P
Interest earned = 46410P
For State Bank of India
Principal amount = 100000P
Rate of interest = 46% compounding annually.
Time = 1 year
Amount earned by Kushal in 1 year from State Bank of India = 100000P*46*1
=> 146000P
Interest earned = 46000P
Difference in the interest earned from both banks = 46410P-46000P = 410P
it is given as 4100
Thus, 410P = 4100
P = 10
So, principal amount = 1000000
The Bank of Hyderabad now offers a 50% interest rate compounded semi-annually.
Principal amount is the same = 1000000
Rate of interest = 50% compounding half-yearly = 25%
Time duration = 2 cycles
Amount after 1 year = 1000000(1.25)^2 = 1562500
Thus, interest earned = 1562500-1000000 = 562500

r = 10% and time cycle = 4

68N = 1428

The cost of 5 pens, 11 pencils,
 and 7 erasers equals Rs. 90, while the cost of 3 pens, 8 pencils, 
and 12 erasers equals Rs. 83. If the cost of 49 pens, 112 pencils, and 92 erasers is equal to N, where N is an integer. Find the value of N
questions.solution_text:
Let us assume the cost of 1 pen, 1 pencil and 1 eraser to be A, B and C, respectively.
Therefore, from the given information in the question, we can form the two equations:
5A+11B+7C = 90 -----equation (1)
3A+8B+12C = 83 -------------equation (2)
We know that the cost of 49 pens, 110 pencils, and 92 erasers is  Rs. N,
=> 49A+112B+92C = N -------equation (3)
We need to find the value of N
Let us multiply equation (i) by a and equation (ii) by b and add them,
and now, we equate the coefficient of M and O with equation (iii)
5aA+11aB+7aC =90a
3bA +8bB+12bC = 83b
(5a+3b) = 49 ----equation (iv)
(7a+12b) = 92 ----equation (v)
Solving these equations (iv) and (v),
we get a = 8 and b = 3
Thus, checking the coefficient of B,
11a+8b = 112
Thus, we can now multiply equations (i) and (ii) with 8 and 3 and add them, we will get
49A + 112B + 92C = 90*8 + 83*3
49A + 112B + 92C = 720 + 249
49A + 112B + 92C = 969
Therefore, the value of N is 969
Thus, option B is the correct answer.

Meanwhile, the deer takes 4 steps forward in a second and 3 steps backwards in the next second, and it continues the same pattern. If the distance between the lion and the deer is 85 steps, what is the least amount of time (in integer seconds) the lion needs to catch the deer? In the first second, the lion is taking 6 steps towards the deer, and the deer is taking 4 steps away from the lion. So, relatively, the lion is getting 2 steps closer to the deer in the first second.

The value of $\frac{85}{3}\ =\ 28.33$ and 85 is not a multiple of 3, so the lion after 28*2 = 56 seconds is 28*3 = 84 steps closer to the deer, and the distance initially was 85 steps. So, the lion needs at least 57 seconds to catch the deer.
Hence, the correct answer is option D.

questions.question_text: If the product of all the values of $x$ that satisfy the equation $e^{5\left(\log_ex\right)^2\ +\ 3}\ =\ x^8$ is A, then what is the value of $\log_eA$?
questions.solution_text:
The given equation is $e^{5\left(\log_ex\right)^2\ +\ 3}\ =\ x^8$ 
Applying log on both sides, we get,
$5\left(\log_ex\right)^2\ +\ 3\ =\ 8\log_ex$
Let the value of $\log_ex$ be t, and by substituting it, the equation becomes,
$5t^2\ -\ 8t\ +\ 3\ =\ 0$
(5t - 3)(t - 1) = 0
$t=\dfrac{3}{5},\ x\ =\ e^{\frac{3}{5}}$
$t=1,\ x\ =\ e^1$
Product of the values = A = $e^{\dfrac{3}{5}}\ \times\ \ e^1\ =\ e^{\dfrac{8}{5}}$
$\log_eA\ =\ \log_ee^{\frac{8}{5}}\ =\ \dfrac{8}{5}$
Hence, the correct answer is option B.

questions.question_text: a,b, x and y are single digit natural numbers and the sum of two 2-digit natural numbers ab and xy is a three-digit number 1aa. HCF(a, b) = 2, HCF(x,y) = 3. What is the value of x+y+a+b ?
questions.solution_text:
When these two numbers are added, we are getting a three-digit number as the sum. a, x are single-digit natural numbers. from which we can infer that a carry is being generated.  
a+x after giving out a carry, we still got 'a'. We know that x is a single-digit number. This is possible only when there was a carry from the units digit place.
So, a+x+1 = 10 +a
This gives us x = 9.
b+y = 10+a
We are told that HCF(a,b) = 2 and HCF(x,y) = 3.
So, a and b are even, and y can be 3 or 6.
10+a is even, and b is also even. Hence, y has to be even. So, y = 6
b-a = 10-y = 4
The only possible pair of single-digit numbers with HCF 2 and difference 4 is (2,6).
So, b= 6 and a = 2.
a+b+x+y = 2+6+9+6 = 23

questions.question_text: B is twice as efficient as A. The time taken by A, B, and C together to finish the work together is 50% less than the time taken to finish when A and B work together. If x:y is the ratio (in simplest form) of the time A alone takes to finish the work to the time B and C together take, then find $x^2+y^2$?
questions.solution_text:
Let us assume the total amount of work as N units and A does one unit every day. So, B does two units of work every day.
The time taken by A and B together to finish the work is $\frac{N}{1+2}=\frac{N}{3}$
We are told that A, B, and C finish the work in 50% less time. That is, A, B, and C finish the work in $\frac{N}{6}$
Let us assume that C does c units of work every day.
Time taken to finish the work by all three together = $\frac{N}{1+2+c}=\frac{N}{6}$
From this, we get c = 3.
The time taken by B and C together to finish the work is $\frac{N}{2+3}=\frac{N}{5}$
So, x:y = N:$\frac{N}{5}$ = 5:1
$x^2+y^2$ = 25+1 = 26

questions.question_text: If a and b are integers, find how many pairs of (a,b) satisfy the inequality $25a^2+b^2\le400$?
questions.solution_text:
We have: $25a^2+b^2\le400$
Or, $\dfrac{25a^2}{400}+\dfrac{b^2}{400}\le1$
This is the equation of an ellipse centered at the origin with:
semi-major axis along b-axis: $\sqrt{400}=20$
semi-major axis along a-axis: $\sqrt{16}=4$
So a ranges from −4 to 4, and b from −20 to 20
For a = $\pm\ 4$
$25a^2=25\times16=400⇒b^2\le0⇒b=0$ (1 solution)
For a = $\pm\ 3$
$25a^2=25\times9=225⇒b^2\le175⇒∣b∣\le\left[\sqrt{175}\right]=13⇒b=−13,\dots,13⇒$ 27 values
For a = $\pm\ 2$
$25a^2=25\times4=100⇒b^2\le300⇒∣b∣\le\left[\sqrt{300}\right]=17⇒b=−17,\dots,17⇒$ 35 values
For a = $\pm\ 1$
$25a^2=25\times1=25⇒b^2\le375⇒∣b∣\le\left[\sqrt{375}\right]=19⇒b=−19,\dots,19⇒$ 39 values
For a = 0
$25a^2=25\times0=0⇒b^2\le400⇒∣b∣\le\left[\sqrt{400}\right]=20⇒b=−20,\dots,20⇒$ 41 values
Total number of integer solutions : 2*(1+27+35+39) + 41 = 245

questions.question_text: Rushi invested ₹ 5000 in a mutual fund. In the first year, his investment grew by a certain percentage. However, due to a recession in the market the following year, the investment fell by a percentage equal to one-fifth of the growth rate in the first year. After two years, his investment was ₹6750. Find the percentage of loss in the second year if it is known that the value of his investment never exceeded ₹10000 during the two years.
questions.solution_text:
Let percentage of growth in first year be $5x\%$
So percentage of loss in second year will be $x\%$
So, $5000\left(1+\dfrac{5x}{100}\right)\left(1-\dfrac{x}{100}\right)=6750$
or, $\left(1+\dfrac{5x}{100}\right)\left(1-\dfrac{x}{100}\right)=\dfrac{6750}{5000}=1.35$ ----->(1)
Let $\dfrac{x}{100}=k$
So, from equation (1),
$\left(1+5k\right)\left(1-k\right)=1.35$
or, $4k-5k^2=0.35$
or, $100k^2-80k+7=0$
or, $\left(10k-1\right)\left(10k-7\right)=0$
or, $k=\dfrac{1}{10}$ or $\dfrac{7}{10}$
or, $x=10$ or $70$
But, $x=70$ is rejected because in that case, after the first year the investment will become $5000\left(1+5\times\ \frac{70}{100}\right)=22500$ which is greater than $10000$
So, $x=10$
so, percentage loss in second year is $10\ \%\ \ $

questions.question_text: There are six numbers - a,b,c,d,e,f - such that their average is 11. The average of a,b, and c is e, the average of d and e is b, and the average of e and f is c. Find the value of e, if the value of a is 3.
questions.solution_text:
$\dfrac{a+b+c}{3}=e$ => $a+b+c=3e$ => $b+c=3e-a\rightarrow1$
Also, $\dfrac{d+e}{2}=b$ => $d+e=2b\rightarrow2$
And, $\dfrac{e+f}{2}=c$ => $e+f=2c\rightarrow3$
Adding eq. 2 and eq. 3 -
=> $d+2e+f=2(b+c)$        (substituting the value of (b+c) from eq. 1)
=> $d+2e+f=6e-2a$
=> $d+f=4e-2a\rightarrow4$
Now, the average of all 6 numbers is 11.
=> $\dfrac{a+b+c+d+e+f}{6}=11$
=> $(a+e)+(b+c)+(d+f)=66$     (substituting the value of (b+c) and (d+f) from eq. 1 and eq. 4)
=> $(a+e)+(3e-a)+(4e-2a)=66$        
=> $8e-2a=66$        (And we are given the value of a = 3)
=> $8e=72$ => $e=9$

questions.question_text: If a 3-digit number is picked whose sum of the digits is 9, what is the probability that the number has either 1 or 2 or both?
questions.solution_text:
The number of three-digit numbers with the sum of the digits as 9 can be calculated as,
Let the three-digit number be xyz and we know that x + y + z = 9 and $x\ \ge\ 1\ ,\ \ y\ge\ 0\ ,\ z\ge\ 0$
Let a = x + 1, and the equation becomes,
a + y + z = 8
Number of possibilities = $^{8\ +\ 3\ -1}C_{3\ -\ 1}\ =\ ^{10}C_2\ =\ 45$ 
The numbers with 1 or 2 in it are,
8, 1, 0 - 4 numbers
7, 2, 0 - 4 numbers
7, 1, 1 - 3 numbers
6, 2, 1 - 6 numbers
5, 3, 1 - 6 numbers
5, 2, 2 - 3 numbers
4, 4, 1 - 3 numbers
4, 3, 2 - 6 numbers
Total = 4 + 4 + 3 + 6 + 6 + 3 + 3 + 6 = 35 ways.
Probability of the number containing either 1 or 2 or both = $\dfrac{35}{45}\ =\ \dfrac{7}{9}$
Hence, the correct answer is option B.

questions.question_text: Find the number of integral values of $p$ such that the equation $x^2-\left(p+2\right)x+\left(2p+9\right)=0$ has negative real roots.
questions.solution_text:
The equation given is, $x^2-\left(p+2\right)x+\left(2p+9\right)=0$
The conditions we need to check for two negative roots will be, we already notice the coefficient of the $x^2$ term is positive, so taking that into account, we have: 
1. $D\ge0$
2. The sum of the roots is negative 
3. Product of roots is positive
1.  $D\ge0$: 
$\left(p+2\right)^2-4\left(2p+9\right)\ge0$
$\left(p^2+4+4p\right)-4\left(2p+9\right)\ge0$
$p^2-4p-32\ge0$
$\left(p+4\right)\left(p-8\right)\ge0$
So we have either, $p\le-4\ or\ p\ge8$
2. $p+2<0$
We get: $p<-2$
So, the earlier case of $p>8$ is eliminated. 
3. $2p+9>0$
We get: $p>-4.5$
The final condition is, $p\in\ \left(-4.5,\ -4\right]$
The only value that satisfies this condition is p=-4.

questions.question_text: A man has 100 kg of grains of 2 types, A and B, in a ratio of 2:3. Grain A sells for Rs.10 less per kg than Grain B. Sita and Gita each purchase some amount of Grain A and B, and at the end, Sita pays Rs 200 more than Gita. If it is known that no grain is left with the man, and Gita buys 20kg of grain B, how many kg of grain A did Sita buy?
questions.solution_text:
We are given that the man has 2 types of grain in 2:3 ratio, and the total grain with the man is 100 kgs.
$\therefore$  quantity of grain A= $\dfrac{\ 2}{\left(2+3\right)}\times\ 100=\ \dfrac{\ 2}{5}\times\ 100=40\ kgs$
and quantity of grainB= $100-40=60kgs$
let Cost per kg of grain A be Rs k, then Cost per kg of grain B will be Rs (k+10)
Further, lets assume that Sita buys $\ x\ kg$ of grain A, and $\ y\ kg$ of grain B
while Gita buys $\ m\ kg$ of grain A and $\ n\ kg$ of grain B . 
$\ \therefore\ \ x+m=40\ ......\left(1\right)\ $
$\&\ \ y+n=60\ ......\left(2\right)\ $
Given , Gita buys $20\ kg\ $ of grain B , $i.e\ n=20\ $
$\therefore\ y=60-20=\ 40\ \ \ \left(eqn\ 2\right)$
Now, Sita pays Rs 200 more than Gita.
Amount paid by Sita= $x\times\ k\ +y\times\ \left(k+10\right)$
Amount paid by Gita= $m\times\ k\ +n\times\ \left(k+10\right)$
$\therefore\ x\times\ k\ +\ y\times\ \left(k+10\right)-\left\{m\times\ k\ +n\times\ \left(k+10\right)\right\}=200$
$or,\ \left(x+y-m-n\right).k\ +10.\left(y-n\right)=200$
$or,\ \ \left(x-m+40-20\right).k+10.\left(40-20\right)=200$
$or,\ \ \left(x-m+20\right).k+200=200$
$or,\ \ \left(x-m+20\right).k=0$
Now , k= cost per Kg cannot be 0, hence $x-m+20=0\ $
$or,\ x-m=-20\ .....\left(3\right)$
Solving Eqn 1 and 3, 
$x=10\ kg$
Hence, Amount of grain Sita bought=$10\ kg$

questions.question_text: Two points M and N are present on sides of a square PQRS such that M bisects SR and N divides PS such that PN:NS=2:1. If PM and RN intersect at O and the ratio of area(QPR) and area(QPOR) can be expressed as $\dfrac{p}{q}$ such that p,q are coprime, then |p-q|=?
questions.solution_text:
The following figure is obtained based on the question, The lines PR and OS are constructed.
Let the side of the square be 6x units .
We are given that PM bisects SR, and RN divides PS in 2:1 ratio. 
Hence, SM=RM=3x units and PN=4x units , SN=2x units.
Now, in $\triangle\ OSR$ , OM is the midpoint, hence $ar\triangle OSM=ar\triangle\ ORM=m\ sq\ units\left(say\right)$
Again, $\triangle\ OSP$, ON bisects PS in 2:1 ratio. So, $\frac{ar\triangle OPN}{ar\triangle\ ONS}=\frac{2}{1}$
Let, $ar\triangle ONS=\ n\ sq\ units$ then $ar\triangle ONP=\ 2n\ sq\ units$ 
Now, let $ar\triangle POR=\ K\ sq\ units$ 
We now consider $\triangle PSR$, in which PM is a median ( since it bisects SR)
So, $ar\triangle PSM=ar\triangle\ PRM$ 
or, 2n+n+m=K+m or K=3n
Again, RN divides PS in ratio 2:1, so $ar\triangle PRN=2.ar\triangle\ RNS$
or, 2n+3n=2(n+m+m) 
or, 3n=4m 
So we have the relation as K=3n=4m, and the area are updated in the figure.
Now, PR is a diagonal of the square PQRS. So, ar(PQR)=ar(PSR)= 2n+3n+n+m+m=6n+2m=6n+1.5n=7.5n 
Required ratio is $\frac{ar\left(QPR\right)}{ar\left(QPOR\right)}=\frac{7.5n}{\left(7.5+3\right)n}=\frac{75}{105}=\frac{5}{7}$
GCD(5,7)=1, hence we have p=5, q=7 .So, |p-q|=|5-7|=2

questions.question_text: f(x) is a function such that $f\left(3x\right)+2f\left(\frac{48}{x}\right)=6x$ and $x\notin\ 0$. What is the value of 2f(18)+5f(8)?
questions.solution_text:
Let us put x = 6
We get $f\left(18\right)+2f\left(8\right)\ =\ 6\cdot6\ =\ 36$ $\rightarrow 1$
Now let us put x = $\frac{8}{3}$
We get  $f\left(3\cdot\frac{8}{3}\right)+2f\left(\frac{48}{\frac{8}{3}}\right)=6\cdot\frac{8}{3}=16$
f(8)+2f(18) = 16  $\rightarrow 2$ 
Equations 1 and 2 can be seen as linear equations in two variables.
Upon solving them, we get 
f(18) = $-\frac{4}{3}$, f(8) = $\frac{56}{3}$
2f(18)+5f(8) = $-\frac{8}{3}+\frac{280}{3}\ =\ \frac{272}{3}=90.67$

questions.question_text: Ashim sold 150 kgs of alphonso mangoes by marking up the price by 20% and offered free totapuri mangoes with every purchase. The price of Alphonso mangoes is 2.5 times the price of Totapuri mangoes. If it is known that he made a profit of $\dfrac{100}{11}\%$, how many kgs of totapuri mangoes did he give out for free to purchasers ?
questions.solution_text:
Let, price of Totapuri mangoes be Rs. x per kg.
Then, price of Alphonso mangoes is Rs. 2.5x per kg
Let us assume that he offers k kgs of Totapuri mangoes for every 1 kg of alphonso sold.
Then, effective cost price for 1 kg alphonso becomes 2.5x+kx =Rs (2.5+k)x
Ashim sells the Alphonso by marking up the price by 20%. 
So, selling price of 1kg  Alphonso mangoes is= $\left(1+20\%\right)\times\ 2.5\ x=Rs.\ 3x$ 
His profit percent is given to be $\dfrac{100}{11}\ \%\ $
So, $\dfrac{3x-\left(2.5+k\right)x}{\left(2.5+k\right)x}\times\ 100=\dfrac{100}{11}$
or, $\dfrac{0.5-k}{2.5+k}=\dfrac{1}{11}$
or, $11\left(0.5-k\right)=2.5+k$
or, $k=\dfrac{1}{4}kg\ $
So Ashim gives away $\dfrac{1}{4}kg\ $ of Totapuri for every 1 kg alphonso sold. Since as he sold 150 kg of Alphonso , so he should have given out $\dfrac{150}{4}=37.5\ kg$ of totapuri mangoes. 
Alternate Explanation,
Let cost price of totapuri mangoes be ₹1/kg
So, cost price of Alphonso mangoes will be ₹2.5/kg
So, marked price of Alphonso mangoes = ₹(2.5*1.2)/kg=₹3/kg
Now let "X" kg of Totapuri mangoes be given for free.
So, total cost price = $\left(1\right)\left(X\right)+\left(2.5\right)\left(150\right)$
Total selling price = $150\times\ 3$
So, $\left(X+2.5\times\ 150\right)\left(1+\dfrac{\dfrac{100}{11}}{100}\right)=450$
or, $X+2.5\times\ 150=450\times\ \dfrac{11}{12}$
or, $X=412.5-375=37.5$ 
So, Totapuri mangoes = $37.5\ kg$

questions.question_text: Amit invests a sum in a scheme at 20% interest compounded semiannually. Every 6 months, he withdraws 50% of his initial investment and reinvests it at 30% pa simple interest in another scheme. He can withdraw only if the full withdrawal amount is available. If not, no withdrawal is made. What is his overall profit % at the end of 2 years?
questions.solution_text:
Let the amount invested be 100x in the first scheme where the amount is compounded semiannually at 20%. 
Thus, the amount after the first six months will be = $100x\times1.1=110x$. 
Now he withdraws 50% of his initial investment, but only when the withdrawal amount is available. So he has to withdraw 50x, which he can, thus the invested amount now will be 60x.
This withdrawn amount is reinvested at 30% Simple interest. 
So, from now till the end of 2 years, the total time is 1.5 years. 
So, this amount will become = $50x\left(1+\dfrac{30\left(\frac{3}{2}\right)}{100}\right)=50x\left(1.45\right)=72.5x$ ---------------- 1
Now, the remaining 60x in the first scheme will be compounded again semiannually. 
Thus, the amount will become = $60x\times1.1=66x$. 
Again, he can withdraw 50% of his initial investment. 
Thus, the amount left will be 16x.
This withdrawn amount is again reinvested at 30% Simple interest in the second scheme. 
So, from now till the end of 2 years, the total time is 1 year. 
So, this amount will become = $50x\left(1+\dfrac{30\times\ 1}{100}\right)=50x\left(1.3\right)=65x$ -------------- 2
Now, the remaining 16x in the first scheme will be compounded again, becoming = $16x\times1.1=17.6x$. 
But now he cannot withdraw any amount, because the complete withdrawal amount is not there. 
Thus, this money will continue to be invested. 
So, for the next 6 months, this amount will become = $17.6x\times1.1=19.36x$. -------------3
So, at the end of two years, he will have = $72.5x+65x+19.36x=156.86x$   (Adding the amount received in 1, 2 and 3)
And, his invested amount is 100x. 
So, his net profit % = $\dfrac{156.86x-100x}{100x}\times100=56.86\%$

questions.question_text: A man commutes 100 km using a bus, a train, and by walking. The bus speed is 30 kmph, the train is 20 kmph, and walking 5 kmph. While going to the office, he travels T hours each by bus and train, then walks the remaining distance. While returning, he travels 2T hours each by train and on foot, then covers the rest by bus. If the total time for both journeys is the same, find the total distance covered by him using the train for the round trip.
questions.solution_text:
The bus's speed is 30 kmph, the train's 20 kmph, and walking's 5 kmph. While going to the office, he travels T hours each by bus and train and then walks the remaining distance.
This means he travels (30T) km by bus, and (20T) km by train while going. Now, the remaining distance is (100-50T) km, which he completes by walking. Thus, the time for which he walks = $\dfrac{100-50T}{5}=20-10T$
Thus, the total time while going to the office = $T+T+\left(20-10T\right)=20-8T\rightarrow1$
While returning, he travels 2T hours each by train and on foot, then covers the rest by bus. 
This means he travels (40T) km by train, and (10T) km by walking while returning. Now, the remaining distance is (100-50T) km, which he completes by bus. Thus, the time for which he travels in bus = $\dfrac{100-50T}{30}$
Thus, the total time while returning from the office = $2T+2T+\dfrac{100-50T}{30}\rightarrow2$
Since the time taken in both journeys is equal, we will equate eq. 1 and 2 -
=> $20-8T=4T+\dfrac{100-50T}{30}$

questions.question_text: Two mixtures, A and B, are made by mixing water, salt and sugar in a 2:3:4 ratio, and water, sugar and lime juice in a 1:3:2 ratio respectively. The two mixtures are then combined and boiled, which results in 80% of the water evaporating. The remaining water makes up only 5% of the remaining solution. What is the ratio of salt and lime juice in the mixture?
questions.solution_text:
We are given that mixture A contains water salt and sugar in 2:3:4 ratio, and mixture B contains water, sugar and lime juice in 1:3:2 ratio.
Lets assume that there is a total of 9x of solution A and 6y of solution B. 
Then, on combining A and B,
Volume of new solution =9x+6y
amount of water=2x+y
amount of salt=3x
amount of sugar=4x+3y 
amount of lime juice = 2y
Now, 80% of the water is evaporated, which means $\dfrac{80}{100}\times\ \left(2x+y\right)$ amount of water is gone.
So amount of water left is $\dfrac{\left(2x+y\right)}{5}$ 
And volume of the solution after evaporation  is $\left(9x+6y\right)-\dfrac{4\left(2x+y\right)}{5}=\dfrac{37x+26y}{5}$
Amount of water remaining is 5% of the solution
Hence, $5\%\ \ of\ \dfrac{37x+26y}{5}=\dfrac{2x+y}{5}$
$or,\ 37x+26y=20\times\ \left(2x+y\right)$
$or,\ 37x+26y=40x+20y$
$or,\ 3x=6y$
$or,\ x:y=2:1$
Hence we have, amount of salt= 3x and amount of lime juice=2y=x 
So ratio of salt to lime juice =$\dfrac{3x}{x}=3:1$

questions.question_text: A boat takes 2 hours to travel downstream a river from port A to B and takes 3 hours to come back. Due to high tide, the stream's speed increases by two times its original speed on a particular day. On that day, the same boat travels from port A to port B and returns. What will the percentage increase/decrease be in the total journey time of the boat, assuming it travels with the same speed on both days?
questions.solution_text:
Let original speed of boat be $b$ km/h and speed of stream be $s$ km/h
Also, let distance from port A to port B be $D$ km
Now, in the first case,
$\dfrac{D}{b+s}=2$ and $\dfrac{D}{b-s}=3$
or, $b+s=\dfrac{D}{2}$
$b-s=\dfrac{D}{3}$
Upon solving, 
$b=\dfrac{5D}{12}$ and $s=\dfrac{D}{12}$
Now, in the second case,
Speed of stream increases by 2 times the original speed
So, new speed of stream is $3s$
or, new speed of stream is $3\times\ \dfrac{D}{12}=\dfrac{D}{4}$
So, time required for downstream journey = $\dfrac{D}{b+3s}=\dfrac{D}{\dfrac{5D}{12}+\dfrac{D}{4}}=1.5$ hours
time required for upstream journey = $\dfrac{D}{b-3s}=\dfrac{D}{\dfrac{5D}{12}-\dfrac{D}{4}}=6$ hours
So, total time required = $1.5+6=7.5$ hours
Original time was $2+3=5$ hours
So, percentage increase = $\dfrac{7.5-5}{5}\times\ 100=50\ \%\ $

questions.question_text: If the value of $\log70=a$, $\log28=b$, and $\log245=c$, then find the value of $\log5$?
questions.solution_text:
$\log70=\log2+\log5+\log7=a\rightarrow1$
$\log28=2\log2+\log7=b\rightarrow2$
$\log245=\log5+2\log7=c\rightarrow3$
Subtracting 1 from 3 -
$\log7-\log2=c-a\rightarrow4$
Subtracting 4 from 2 -
$3\log2=b-c+a$
$\log2=\dfrac{(b-c+a)}{3}$
Multiply eq. 1 by 2, and then subtracting eq. 3 from it -
$2(\log2+\log5+\log7)-(\log5+2\log7)=2a-c$
$2\log2+\log5=2a-c$
Putting the value of log2 - 
$\log5=\left(2a-c\ \right)-2\left(\dfrac{b-c+a}{3}\right)$
$\log5=\left(\dfrac{6a-3c-2b+2c-2a}{3}\right)$
$\log5=\dfrac{4a-2b-c}{3}$

questions.question_text: Mr. X bought 16 identical toys for his three grandchildren. Find the number of ways in which he can distribute the toys among his grandchildren such that none of the grandchildren receives more than 7 toys.
questions.solution_text:
The simplest way to solve this question is to assume how many ways there are so that the children get equal to or fewer than 7 toys. 
We know that the maximum number of toys the three children can get is 7. 
Let a, b and c be the three integers that represent the number of toys less than or equal to 7. 
Hence, the three children would receive the toys in the following way:
$7-a+7-b+7-c=16$
a, b and c can be greater than or equal to 0 but less than 8. 
Hence, we can say, 
$21-a-b-c=16$
Or, $a+b+c=5$
Now, we know that n things can be distributed among r different persons in $^{n+r-1}C_{r-1}$
Hence, the number of ways of distributing 5 among 3 is $^7C_2=21$
Hence, there are 21 ways.

questions.question_text: Find the last two digits of $\left(2^{50}-2^{20}\right)$
questions.solution_text:
For $2^{10n}$ - 
if $n=odd$ => Last two digits = $24$
if $n=even$ => Last two digits = $76$
For example - $2^{10}=1024$, last two digits 24. 
$2^{20}=1024*1024$, so for the last two digits, we will multiply $24\times\ 24=576$, thus last two digits are 76.
Last two digits for $2^{30}=76*24=1824$, thus the last two digits are 24. And hence, the cyclicity continues, which proves the above general formula
Thus, Last two digits of $2^{50}=24$  and last two digits of $2^{20}=76$ 
Now, for $2^{50}-2^{20} $, we know that the last two digits are 24 and 76, respectively. But if we subtract 76 from 24, we will get the result as negative. Thus, for $2^{50}$, we will take a carry of '1' from the last third digit. Thus-
Last two digits of $2^{50}-2^{20}=124-76=48$

questions.question_text: 10 inlet pipes fill the tank in 4 hours, and n outlet pipes empty half the tank in 3 hours. If (n+1) inlet pipes and $\dfrac{n}{2}$ outlet pipes are opened, then the tank is filled in 24 hours. Find the ratio of the efficiency of the inlet to the outlet pipes.
questions.solution_text:
Let the efficiency of inlet pipes be a, and the outlet pipes be b.
10 inlet pipes fill the tank in 4 hours, thus the capacity of the tank will be = $10\times4\times a=40a$ litres
n outlet pipe empties half the tank in 3 hours; thus, the capacity of half the tank = $n\times3\times b=3nb$ litres. Thus, the capacity of the full tank is = $6nb$ litres.
=> $40a=6nb$ => $a=\dfrac{3nb}{20}\rightarrow1$
Now, (n+1) inlet pipes and $\dfrac{n}{2}$ outlet pipes are opened, and the tank is filled in 24 hours.
=> $\left(\left(n+1\right)a-\left(\dfrac{n}{2}\right)b\right)\times24=6nb$     (substituting the value of a from eq. 1)
=> $\left(\left(n+1\right)\left(\dfrac{3nb}{20}\right)-\left(\dfrac{n}{2}\right)b\right)=\dfrac{nb}{4}$
Cancelling the terms n and b from both LHS and RHS -
=> $\left(n+1\right)\dfrac{3}{20}-\dfrac{1}{2}=\dfrac{1}{4}$
=> $\left(n+1\right)\dfrac{3}{20}=\dfrac{3}{4}$
=> $n+1=5$ => $n=4$
Substituting the value of n in eq. 1 -
$a=\dfrac{3\times4\times b}{20}$
=> $\dfrac{a}{b}=\dfrac{3}{5}$
Alternate Explanation,
Let the volume of the tank be $1$ litre, and it takes 10 * 4 = 40 hours for the inlet pipe to fill the tank. Thus - 
Efficiency of one inlet pipe = $\dfrac{1}{40}$ litre/hr
And n outlet pipes empty half the tank in 3 hours. Thus, 0.5 litres of the tank gets emptied by outlet pipes in n * 3 = 3n hours. Thus - 
Efficiency of one outlet pipe = $\dfrac{\dfrac{1}{2}}{3n}=\dfrac{1}{6n}$ litre/hr
So, $\left(\dfrac{\left(n+1\right)1}{40}-\dfrac{n}{2}\times\ \dfrac{1}{6n}\right)=\dfrac{1}{24}$
or,$\dfrac{n+1}{40}-\dfrac{1}{12}=\dfrac{1}{24}$
or, $\dfrac{n+1}{40}=\dfrac{3}{24}=\dfrac{1}{8}$
So, $n=4$
So, efficency of inlet pipe to outlet pipe = $\dfrac{\dfrac{1}{40}}{\dfrac{1}{6n}}=\dfrac{6n}{40}=\dfrac{6\times\ 4}{40}=\dfrac{3}{5}$

questions.question_text: When $\left(5x^2+16x-10\right)^2-\left(x^2+14x-8\right)^2$ is divided by 6A, the quotient is $\left(x^2+5x-3\right)$, with no remainder. Find A.
questions.solution_text:
We know that Dividend = Divisor*Quotient.
Here, the dividend is $\left(5x^2+16x-10\right)^2-\left(x^2+14x-8\right)^2$, the divisor is 6A and the quotient is given as $\left(x^2+5x-3\right)$
Now, we notice the dividend: $\left(5x^2+16x-10\right)^{^2}-\left(x^2+14x-8\right)^{^2}$
We know that $A^2-B^2=\left(A+B\right)\left(A-B\right)$
Hence, we can say, $\left(5x^2+16x-10\right)^{^2}-\left(x^2+14x-8\right)^{^2}$ = $\left(5x^2+16x-10+x^2+14x-8\right)\left(5x^2+16x-10-x^2-14x+8\right)$
We get the dividend as $\left(6x^2+30x-18\right)\left(4x^2+2x-2\right)$
We can factorise the dividend:
$12\left(x^2+5x-3\right)\left(2x^2+x-1\right)$
Now, putting in the equation ,  Dividend = Divisor*Quotient.
$12\left(x^2+5x-3\right)\left(2x^2+x-1\right)$ =$6A\times\left(x^2+5x-3\right)$
We get A = $2\left(2x^2+x-1\right)$

or, $X\ =\ \dfrac{88}{3}$

questions.solution_text:
A large sphere of radius R cm is melted to form N smaller spheres of radius r cm.
=> $\dfrac{4}{3}\pi R^3=N\times\ \dfrac{4}{3}\pi r^3$
$=>R=N^{\frac{1}{3}}\times\ r$

And each smaller sphere is painted red at Rs. 1/cm²
=> Cost of painting all smaller spheres = $N\times\ 1\times\ 4\pi r^2$
The total painting cost remains the same for both cases.

Eliminating $4\pi$ both sides and then taking root-
=> $6\times\ R=N^{\frac{1}{2}}\times r$

=> $6=N^{\frac{1}{6}}$

questions.question_text: A man works 8 hours daily and can finish a work in 14 days. If he decreases his work hours by 20%, by what percentage should his efficiency increase so that he can still complete the work in the stipulated time?
questions.solution_text:
The man can finish the work in 14 days If he works 8 hours a day. So he requires a total of $14\times\ 8=112$ hours to complete the work.
Let the total work be 112 units, in that case his efficiency is 1 unit/hr.
The man decreases his work hours by 20%, which means he works $0.8\times\ 8=6.4$ hours daily.
He needs to finish his work in 14 days only, so he has a total of $14\times6.4=89.6\ $ hours.
The total work however will remain unchanged at 112 units.
So his efficiency y in the second case should be $\dfrac{112}{89.6\ }=1.25\ $ units per day.
So percentage increase in efficiency is $\dfrac{1.25-1}{1}\times\ 100=25\%$

$\angle DAC=90^{\circ}$. This means that - $AD^2+AC^2=DC^2$ => $AD^2=DC^2-AC^2\rightarrow1$

Substituting the value of $AD^2$ from eq. 1

questions.question_text: In a class of 20 students, 60% are boys, and the rest of the students are girls. The average weight of boys is 55 kg. The weights of all the students in the class are distinct integers. If the average weight of the class is 45 kg, then what is the maximum weight of the girl who weighs the least?
questions.solution_text:
In the class of 20 students there are 60% boys and the rest are girls.
Thus, there are 12 boys and 8 girls.
Average weight of the class = 45 kg
Thus, the total weight of the class = 45*20 = 900 kg
Average weight of the boys = 55 kg
Thus, the total weight of the boys = 55*12 = 660 kg
Hence, the total weight of the girls = 900 - 600 = 240 kg.
Therefore, the average weight of girls = 30 kg.
To find the maximum weight of the girl who weighs the least we will have to distribute the weights of the girls around the average.
This can be done as:-
26, 27, 28, 29, 31, 32, 33 and 34.(Since the weights of all the students are distinct)
Thus, the maximum weight of the girl who weighs the least = 26 kg
Hence, option B is the correct answer.

100m + 80w + 60c = 100m + 125w
=> 60c = 45w

10 men, 5 women, and 10 children:
We know that the total work = 100m + 125w
Let x be the number of days taken by 10 men, 5 women, and 10 children to complete the work.
x*(10m+5w+10c) = 100m + 125w
x*(10m+5w+7.5w) = 100m + 125w
x*(10m+12.5w) = 100m+125w
=> x = 10 days.
Therefore, option B is the right answer.
