questions.question_text: A shopkeeper mixes milk and water in the ratio 3:5. He marks up the price of the mixture and sells one litre of the mixture at a price which is equal to the average price of one litre of milk and water.  If it is known that water is not available free of cost and milk does not cost more than five times the cost of water, then the maximum profit earned by the shopkeeper cannot exceed
questions.solution_text:
Let the price of milk be $x$ and the price of water be $y$.
Now, the shopkeeper mixes milk and water in the ratio $3:5$.
The cost of 1 litre of the mixture for the milkman = $\dfrac{3x+5y}{5+3}$ = $\dfrac{3x+5y}{8}$
Average price of 1 litre of milk and water = $\dfrac{x+y}{2}$
We have to find the maximum possible profit that the shopkeeper could have made provided milk does not cost more than 5 times the cost of water. Therefore, x=5y will be the limiting condition.
Substituting x = 5y and calculating the profit percentage, we get,
Profit percentage =$\dfrac{\frac{6y}{2}-\frac{20y}{8}}{\frac{20y}{8}}$
=> Profit percentage = $\dfrac{\frac{4y}{8}}{\frac{20y}{8}}$
=> Profit percentage = $\frac{4}{20}$ = $20$%.
The maximum possible profit percentage cannot exceed $20 %$ and hence, option B is the right answer.

questions.question_text: One of the angles of an isosceles triangle is $120^{o}$. What is the circum-radius of this triangle if its shorter side is 12m
questions.solution_text:
In any obtuse angled triangle, the obtuse angle is always between the two equal sides.
If the obtuse angle is between the unequal parts, this angle will occur twice which is improbable. 
(This is because angles opposite to equal sides are equal)
The shorter side will be the two equal sides of an isosceles triangle.
Let the triangle be ABC and O be the centre of the circumcircle formed by this triangle.
We have $\angle{ABC}=120^{o}$
The line BO is an angular bisector of $\angle{ABC}$ as the triangle is isosceles. 
Hence, $\angle{OBC}=60^{o}$
Since OB = OC, $\angle{OBC}=\angle{OCD}=60^{o}$
Hence, the triangle OBC is equilateral as all sides are $60^{o}$
Therefore, Circum-radius = shorter side BC =12m
Alternative Approach :
According to sine rule $\frac{a}{sin{\angle{A}}}=\frac{b}{sin{\angle{B}}}=\frac{c}{sin{\angle{C}}}=2R$ where R is circum radius
Hence $\dfrac{12}{sin{\angle{30^o}}}=\dfrac{12}{\frac{1}{2}}=24$ = 2R
R = 12cm

questions.question_text: Cities A and B are 1500 km apart and lie in different time zones. A plane departs from city A at 9 AM and reaches city B at 1 PM. Then, the plane departs from city B at 3 AM and travels at twice the speed with which it traveled from city A to city B. It reaches city A at 2 AM. What is the minimum time difference between the 2 cities (in hours)?
questions.solution_text:
Let the time difference between the 2 cities be ‘d’ hours.
We can see that the plane reached city A before the time it left from city B.
Therefore, city A must lag city B (in time).
Let the speed of the plane from A to B be x.
x ( 4-d) = 2x(-1+d) = 1500
4x - xd = -2x + 2xd
3xd = 6x
d = 2.
Therefore, the time difference is 2 hours.

Number of quadilaterals formed using all non collinear points = 7C4 = 35
Number of quadilaterals formed using 3 non collinear points and one from a collinear set = 7C3*5C1 = 175
Number of quadilaterals formed using 2 non collinear points and 2 from a collinear set = 7C2*5C2 = 210
Total = 210+175+35 = 420

=> f(x+2) + f(x+1) + f(x-1) = f(x+1)

Substitute f(x) = f(x+1) + f(x-1)

questions.question_text: A toy shop owner sources a rare toy from various retailers who sold the toy to him at different rates. He got 40% of his stock from a retailer who sold it to him at 100/piece, 25% of his stock from a retailer who sold it to him at 120/piece and 35% of the stock from retailer who sold it to him at 80/piece. The shop owner decides to keep a single marked price for all the pieces of the toy. What should be the marked price if he wants to earn 20% profit after offering 20% discount ?
questions.solution_text:
Let the total stock of the toy with the toy shop owner be $100x$ units 
Total cost of stock from the first retailer = $\dfrac{40}{100} \times 100x \times 100 = 4000x$ 
Total cost of stock from the second retailer = $\dfrac{25}{100} \times 100x \times 120 = 3000x $ 
Total cost of stock from the third retailer = $\dfrac{35}{100} \times 100x \times 80 = 2800x $ 
Total cost of the stock = $4000x+3000x+2800x = 9800x $
Cost price of the toy for the retailer per piece = $\dfrac{9800x}{100x}$ = ₹98/piece 
Let the marked price be $₹y$
Given, $y \times \dfrac{4}{5} = 98 \times \dfrac{6}{5} $ 
$ y = 98 \times \dfrac{6}{4} = ₹147$

questions.question_text: Eight men and three women can complete a certain work in nine days, which eleven men and x women take six days to complete. If x men and six women take nine days to complete the same work, find x?
questions.solution_text:
Let us assume that work done by one man and one woman in day is denoted by M and W respectively.
Then we can say that (8M + 3W)*9 = (11M + xW)6
$\Rightarrow$  6M = (6x - 27)W
$\Rightarrow$  $\frac{M}{W}$ = $\frac{6x - 27}{6}$               ... (1)
$\Rightarrow$       (8M + 3W)*9 = (xM + 6W)*9
$\Rightarrow$       (8 - x)M = 3W
$\Rightarrow$  $\frac{M}{W}$ = $\frac{3}{8 - x}$                ... (2)
By equating (1) and (2)
$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{6x - 27}{6}$ =   $\frac{3}{8 - x}$
$\Rightarrow$ $2x^2$ - 25x + 78 = 0
$\Rightarrow$ x= 6, 6.5 
We know that x is an integer hence x = 6 (Answer)

questions.question_text: What is the maximum number of acute interior angles that a 12 sided closed figure can enclose?
questions.solution_text:
The total angle enclosed by a closed polygon is (n-2)*180$^{\circ}$.
Hence, a 12 sided polygon will enclose 1800$^{\circ}$.
For an angle to be acute, it has to be less than 90 $^{\circ}$. Hence, we will use 90$^{\circ}$ for the ease of calculation.
If all 12 are acute angles, then the sum of angles will be 12*90$^{\circ}$ = 1080$^{\circ}$.
This case is not possible.
If 11 of them are acute and 1 is obtuse, then 11*90$^{\circ}$ + obtuse angle = 1800$^{\circ}$.
=> The measure of the obtuse angle is 810$^{\circ}$. But, angle enclosed by a polygon cannot be greater than 360$^{\circ}$. Hence, this case is also not possible.
If 10 angles are acute, the sum of the 2 obtuse angles will be 900$^{\circ}$. The measure of the obtuse angle = 450$^{\circ}$.
Hence, this case is also not possible.
If 9 angles are acute, the sum of the remaining 3 obtuse angles will be 1800$^{\circ}$ - 810$^{\circ}$ = 990$^{\circ}$.
The measure of the obtuse angle can be 990$^{\circ}$/3 = 330$^{\circ}$. Hence, this case is possible.
Hence, the maximum number of acute angles possible is 9.

questions.question_text: In a GP the sum of the first six terms is 28 times the sum of the first three terms.If the fourth term is 108, then find the second term in the series ?
questions.solution_text:
Let a be the first term and r be the common ratio.
given, $a\frac{(1 - r^6)}{1 - r} =  28 a\frac{(1 - r^3)}{1 - r}$...(1)
On rearranging we get, 27 = $r^3(28 - r^3)$...(2)
also given, $ar^3 = 108$
$r^3 = \frac{108}{a}...(3)$
substituting (3) in (2)
$27 = \frac{108}{a}(28 - \frac{108}{a})$
$= a^2 -112a + 432 = 0$
On solving we get a = 4 and 108.
a $\neq$ 108 as then we will get r = $\pm$ 1 which does not satisfy the condition given in (1)
thus a = 4 and r = 3 (r $\neq$ -3 as it does not satisfy (1))
∴ the second term = $ar = 12$

questions.question_text: Raman had a cubic metal solid. He kept it on a fixed base and hammered it such that the height reduced but the cross-section as viewed from the top was exactly the same as that before the hammering. As a result of the hammering, the density of the solid increased by 10%. What will be the percentage increase/decrease in the total area? (Enter your answer as the closest integer.)
questions.solution_text:
Since the cross-section viewed from the top remains the same but the density increases, the height will decrease and the volume will decrease too.
Since the new density is 10% more, the new volume will be $\frac{a^3}{1.1}$, where a is the side of the original cube.
Since the cross-section from the above is the same, its area will be $a^2$ only. Hence the new height= $\frac{a}{1.1}$.
Original Surface area = $6a^2$.
New surface area= $2\left(a^2+\frac{a^2}{1.1}+\frac{a^2}{1.1}\right)=\frac{6.2a^2}{1.1}$
Change in surface area= $6a^2-\frac{6.2a^2}{1.1}$=$\frac{.4a^2}{1.1}$
Percentage change= $\frac{400}{66}=6.06\%$

questions.question_text: How many numbers will divide 2460 and 2640 leaving the same remainder?
questions.solution_text:
Suppose a number K leaves the same remainder R when it divides 2460 and 2640.
So, 2460 - R = K*p for some natural number p
Similarly, 2640 - R = K*q for some natural number q
When we subtract the two equations, we get 2640 - 2460 = K*(q-p) or 180 = K*(q-p)
Hence, all the numbers which are factors of the difference (180) between the given numbers will divide both the numbers leaving the same remainder.
So, all the factors of (2640 - 2460) = 180 will be such numbers.
So, we have to find the numbers of factors of 180.
$180 = 2^2 * 3^2 * 5$
Number of factors = (2 + 1)(2 + 1)(1 + 1) = 18
So, there are 18 such numbers which will divide 2460 and 2640 leaving the same remainder.
Hence, option c is the correct answer.

questions.question_text: If the points A(2, a), B(b,2) C(-2,4) lie on the same line, then pick the correct relation between a and b?
questions.solution_text:
Since the lines are collinear then the slope of the line calculated using (2, a) and (-2,4) will be the same as (b,2) and (-2,4)
Hence, $\ \frac{\ 2+2}{a-4}=\ \frac{\ b+2}{2-4}$
=> $\ \frac{\ 4}{a-4}=\ \frac{\ b+2}{-2}$
=> $\left(a-4\right)\left(b+2\right)=-8$
=> ab+2a-4b-8=-8
=> ab+2a-4b=0
=> $\frac{1}{4}+\frac{1}{2b}-\frac{1}{a}=0$  (divide by 4ab)
=> $\frac{1}{a}-\frac{1}{2b}=\frac{1}{4}$

Product of roots $(m*n)$ = 28/2 = 14
$(1+m+m^2)(1+n+n^2)$

$\Rightarrow$ $1+(m+n)+(m*n)^2+mn(1+m+n)+(m+n)^2-2m*n$
$\Rightarrow$ $1+8+(14)^2+14(1+8)+(8)^2-2*14$
$\Rightarrow$ $367$
Hence, option C is the correct answer.

=> New Marked Price = 0.96M
Hence discount percentage = $\ \frac{M-S}{M}\times\ 100$  = $\ \frac{0.16M}{0.96M}\times\ 100$ = 16.67%

questions.question_text: A large cube is cut into n smaller cubes such that all n cubes have equal dimensions and no part of the larger cube remains. If the surface area increases by 4 times, what is the value of n?
questions.solution_text:
Since all the cubes are of the same dimensions, let us say that we are forming cubes that have half the length of the original cube. In that case, we need to have three mutually perpendicular cuts parallel to the faces of the cube.
In this case, the surface area becomes twice. because we are introducing one more set of surfaces.
Similarly, when we cut this into a cube such that the side of the smaller cubes is one-fifth of the side of the older cube, we increase the surface area by 4 times, or to five times, and we get 125 cubes.

x = 6

$203=210-y$
y = 7 years.

So the portion of work done by 12 workers in one day= $\frac{\frac{W}{16}}{W}$
= 1:16
D is the correct answer.

questions.question_text: Three unbiased dice are rolled simultaneously. What is the probability the sum of the numbers obtained on the three dice is at least 16?
questions.solution_text:
When three dice are rolled, the maximum sum that can be obtained is 18.
So, in the given question, the sum can be 16 or 17 or 18
For the sum to be 16, there can be two possibilities:
1. (6 , 6 , 4) - total cases = $\frac{3!}{2!}$ = 3
2. (6, 5, 5) - total cases = $\frac{3!}{2!}$ = 3
For the sum to be 17, there can be only one possibility:
1. (6, 6, 5) - total cases = $\frac{3!}{2!}$ = 3
For the sum to be 18, there is only one case which is (6, 6, 6)
So, the no. of favourable outcomes = (3 + 3 + 3 + 1) = 10
Total no. of outcomes = 6 * 6 * 6 = 216
Required probability = $\frac{10}{216}$ = $\frac{5}{108}$
Hence, option D is the correct answer.

S will be a square when [2n+119] is equal to 15k where k is a square,
2n+119=15k
The minimum value of k can be 9, hence 2n+119=15*9 =135   =>2n=16  =>n=8
Then the last term = n+119=8+119=127

questions.question_text: A triangle ABC of perimeter 70 cm is circumscribed by a circle of radius 15 cm such that AB is the diameter. Find the area of the triangle(in cm$^2$).
questions.solution_text:
Consider the following figure:
ACB will be a right angle. (Angle in the semicircle)
Now, AB+BC+AC=70
Now, AB = 15*2 = 30 cm
=> BC+AC = 70-30 = 40 cm ......(1)
Also, $BC^2+AC^2=30^2$  (Using pythagoras) ......(2)
Squaring the first equation and subtracting the second equation from it, we get
2BC*AC = 40*40-30*30 = 700  .....(3)
Area of triangle ACB = $\frac{1}{2}\times\ BC\times\ AC$ = 700/4 = 175 cm$^2$ (dividing equation 3 by 4)

questions.question_text: In how many ways can 10 children be seated in 10 seats from left to the right such that 2 particular children are never together?
questions.solution_text:
Number of ways in which the 2 particular children are not together = Total number of ways - Number of ways in which they are together
Total number of ways = 10!
Number of ways in which 2 particular children are together = (10-1)!.2!=9!2!
Hence, the number of ways in which the 2 particular children are never together = $10!-9!2!=9!\left(10-2\right)=9!.8$

questions.question_text: A solution is made up of alcohol and water in an unknown ratio. If one-fourth of this solution is taken out and replaced with water, the ratio is reversed. What is the volume of water(in liters) in the final solution if the volume of the solution is 35 liters?
questions.solution_text:
Consider total volume of solution = L and the ratio of alcohol and water is a:b
Volume of alcohol = aL/(a+b)    Volume of water = bL/(a+b) 
After taking out L/4 solution, the ratio will remain same.
Volume of alcohol = 3aL/4(a+b)    Volume of water = 3bL/4(a+b) 
After adding L/4 water, Volume of alcohol = 3aL/4(a+b)    Volume of water = 3bL/4(a+b) + L/4
New ratio of volume of alcohol to water = $\frac{\frac{3aL}{4(a+b)}}{\frac{3bL}{4(a+b)}+\frac{L}{4}}$ = $\frac{b}{a}$
$\frac{3a}{3b+a+b} = \frac{b}{a}$
$\frac{3a}{4b+a} = \frac{b}{a}$
$3a^{2} = 4b^{2}+ab$   $3a^{2} -ab-4b^{2}= 0$     $3a^{2} +3ab-4ab-4b^{2}= 0$
$(a+b)(3a-4b)=0$   $\frac{a}{b}$ = 4/3    (If (a+b)=0, one value is negative, ignore negative value)
Since in final solution ratio becomes 3:4, volume of water = 35*(4/7) = 20 liters
C is the answer.

questions.question_text: The sum of lengths of the parallel sides of a trapezium is 30 cm. The lengths of parallel sides are in the ratio 3:7. One of the non-parallel sides is perpendicular to the other two sides. If the area of the trapezium is 135 $cm^2$, find perimeter of the trapezium.
questions.solution_text:
Let us look at a diagram of the situation. 
Let the lengths of the parallel sides be $3x$ and $7x$. 
Since we know that the sum of lengths of the parallel sides is 30 cm, 
$3x+7x = 30 \Rightarrow x = \dfrac{30}{10} \Rightarrow x =3$
Thus the lengths of the sides are 9 cm and 21 cm respectively.
Let the given figure be the figure of the trapezium : 
Here, AB=9 cm and CD=21 cm.
Let us draw a perpendicular from C on BD meeting BD at point E. 
Here, ABCE is a square with side 9 cm. Therefore, $\triangle BED$ is a right angled triangle. 
Let the length of ED be $y$ cm. 
Then area of $\triangle BED, A' = \dfrac{1}{2} \times BE \times ED $
$ \Rightarrow A' = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 9 \times y $
Since the area of the trapezium is given, 
Area of trapezium = Area of square + Area of triangle 
$\Rightarrow 135 = (9 \times 9)+(\dfrac{9y}{2}) $
$\Rightarrow 15 = 9+ \dfrac{y}{2} \Rightarrow y = 2 \times 6 = 12 $
Applying pythagoras theorem on $\triangle BED$, $12^2+9^2 = BD^2 $
$ \Rightarrow BD^2 = 225 \Rightarrow BD = 15 $cm 
Thus, perimeter of the trapezium = 9+21+9+15 = 54 cm

questions.question_text: Two racers are running to and fro from points A and B at 3m/s and 7m/s respectively. If the distance between A and B is 2000m, what is the total distance covered by both the racers, till they meet for the 2nd time?
questions.solution_text:
Two racers are running from point A and B respectively at 3m/s and 7m/s.
The racers will meet for the first time at $2000\times\ \frac{3}{10}=600m$ from A.
Now they will move in the direction opposite to each other till the racer from B reach A, after that, both racers will move in the same direction.
When the faster racer reaches A, then the slower racer will cover x km till then
Thus, 
$\frac{x}{3}=\frac{2000}{7}$    (Equating time taken)
x= $\frac{6000}{7}$
The relative speed at that point of time = 7-3=4m/s
After reaching A, the time taken by the faster racer to catch the slower racer = $\frac{6000}{7\times4}$
Distance travelled by the faster racer from A till he meets the slower racer for the second time =7 * $\frac{1500}{7}$=1500m
This distance will also be equal to the total distance travelled by the slower racer(from the figure) = 1500m
The distance travelled by the faster racer = Distance from B to A + 1500 = 2000+1500 m
Total distance travelled= 1500+(2000+1500)=5000m

Now if we increase the proportion of A, then it will bring the final concentration to less than 50%, but if we increase B, we get a value more than the required fifty percentage alcohol solution; hence, we can have a ratio less than 3:7 but not more than it. Hence, option c is right.

Or $43X\ +53Y\ \ge 57X\ +\ 47Y$
Or $\frac{X}{Y} \le \frac{3}{7}$
Or $\frac{X}{Y} \le 0.428$
Only option C has a ratio of X and Y less than or equal to 0.42.
Thus, the correct option is C.

questions.question_text: In a test, there are 100 questions. Each question that is correctly answered fetches +3 and a question that is wrongly answered fetches -2. Every question needs to be attempted. If the passing score is 40% of the maximum possible score in the test, how many questions need to be correct to get a score that is double the passing score?
questions.solution_text:
Total possible score is 100 x 3 = 300
New passing score = 2 x 40% of 300 = 240
Now we can assign +3 to all questions and then subtract (+3 + 2) for each incorrect question.
Hence, if the number of incorrect questions is x,
300 - 5x = 240
5x = 60
x = 12
Hence, the number of correct questions = 100 - 12 = 88.

We can form a pyramid by stacking one sphere on a base of three spheres. The centres of the spheres forming the bottom layer are 'r' cms above the wooden floor. On connecting the centres of the spheres, we obtain a tetrahedron as shown below: 
Calculating 'h'  from the above setup and adding it to twice the radius of the sphere will render us our desired answer. 
Since AP bisects the equilateral triangle forming the base, $\angle\ PAB\ =\ 30^{\circ\ }$

We can find h in terms of 'r' by using the Pythagoras theorem: $h^2+a^2=4r^2$

Thus, Option A is the correct choice.

questions.question_text: What is the minimum value that the function $f(x) = \dfrac{x^2+3x-6}{x^2+3x+6} $ ?
questions.solution_text:
We can simplify the given expression as follows : 
$f(x) =\dfrac{x^2+3x-6}{x^2+3x+6} $
$\Rightarrow f(x) =\dfrac{x^2+3x+6-12}{x^2+3x+6} $
$\Rightarrow f(x) =1 - \dfrac{12}{x^2+3x+6} $ ------(1)
We can see that the value of function f(x) will be minimum when the value of expression $\dfrac{12}{x^2+3x+6}$ is maximum. The value of expression $\dfrac{12}{x^2+3x+6}$ will be maximum when the value of $x^2+3x+6$ is minimum. 
Let, U(x) = $x^2+3x+6$. We know that U(x) will be minimum at x = -b/2a and then minimum value will be equivalent to -D/4a. {Where D is the discriminant and 'a' is the coefficient of $x^2$}
Therefore, U(x)$_{min}$ = $\dfrac{-(3^2-4*1*6)}{4*1}$ = $\dfrac{15}{4}$.
Hence, f(x)$_{min}$ = $1-\dfrac{12}{\frac{15}{4}}$ = $\dfrac{-11}{5}$. Therefore, option C is the correct answer.

questions.question_text: If $2<a<4$ and [a] = The greatest integer less than a, What is the probability (p) of $[a^{2}] = [a]^2$?
questions.solution_text:
Given function is $[a^{2}] = [a]^2$
Let us consider RHS
If $[a]^2$ = 4
then $2 \leq a<3$
If $[a]^2$ = 9
Then $3 \leq a<4$
Let us consider LHS
If $[a^{2}] = 4$
Then $2<a \leq \sqrt{5}$
If $[a^{2}] = 9$ 
Then $3\leq a < \sqrt{10}$ 
Hence, the range satisfying $[a^{2}] = [a]^2$ is $(2, \sqrt{5})$ and $[3,\sqrt{10})$
Required probability = $\frac{\sqrt{5}-2 +\sqrt{10}-3}{4-2}$ = $\frac{2.23-2+3.16-3}{2}$ = $\frac{0.39}{2}$ ~0.2
Hence, option D is the correct answer.

questions.question_text: How many straight lines can be drawn with 15 points on a plane of which 7 are collinear?
questions.solution_text:
If we select any 2 points, we can draw a straight line.
So, total number of straight lines = $15_{C_2}$

questions.question_text: Pawan and Rushit decide to run on a circular track from the same point in the same direction. The length of the track is 2 km. Ramesh, a bystander, notices that when they (Pawan and Rushit) first meet, Pawan is already in his fourth round and has completed 500 m. How much head start should Pawan give Rushit if he wants a race of 2340 meters  (on a linear track) to end in a draw? (Speed of Pawan is greater than that of Rushit)
questions.solution_text:
When they first met, Pawan had completed 3 + 500/2000 = 3.25 laps.
In this time, Rushit would have completed 1 less round than Pawan.
Thus, Rushit would have completed 2.25 laps.
Thus, the ratio of the speed of Pawan and Rushit is 3.25:2.25 = 13:9
Let the speed of Pawan be 13 m/s and the speed of Rushit be 9 m/s.
Time required by Pawan to complete a race of 2340m = 2340/13 = 180s
The distance covered by Rushit in 180 seconds = 180*9 = 1620 m
Thus, if Pawan wants the race to end in a draw, then he should Rushit a head start of 2340-1620 = 720 m.
Hence, option A is the correct answer.

Find the range of ‘x’ for which the following inequality holds true.
$\frac{x^2 - 15}{x^2 + 5} \geq \frac{2x^2 - 16}{x^4 + 5x^2}$

questions.question_text: In a geometric progression, the sum of the first 8 terms is equal to the sum of the first 10 terms. The third term of the series is 4. The sum of the first 99 terms of the series is

So 99th term in the series = 4
The sum of the first 98 terms of the series will be 0.
Hence, the sum of the first 99 terms of the series is 4

questions.question_text: The smallest altitude of a right-angled triangle of area 216 cm$^2$ is 14.4 cm. What is the perimeter of the triangle?
questions.solution_text:
We know that the length of an altitude in a triangle is inversely proportional to the length of the side on which it is drawn.
So, the smallest altitude in a right-angled triangle must be drawn on its hypotenuse.
Let the base of the triangle be '$b$', perpendicular be '$p$' and the hypotenuse be '$h$'
Area of the triangle = 216 cm$^2$
or, $\dfrac{1}{2} * b * p = 216$
or, $bp = 432$..........(i)
Also, the length of the altitude drawn on the hypotenuse is 14.4 cm
So, area of the triangle can be written as
$\dfrac{1}{2} * h * 14.4 = 216$
=> $h = 30$ cm
We also know that in a right angled triangle
$b^2 + p^2 = h^2$ [Pythagoras Theorem]
or, $b^2 + p^2 = 30^2 = 900$
Adding '$2bp$' to both the sides, we get
$b^2 + p^2 + 2bp = 900 + 2bp$
Putting the value of $bp$ from (i), we get
$(b + p)^2 = 900 + 2*432 = 1764$
or, $(b + p) = \sqrt{1764} = 42$
Thus, the perimeter of the triangle = $(b + p + h) = (42 + 30) = 72$cm
Hence, option C is the correct answer.

questions.question_text: A family consisted of four members. In the year 2008, a 60 years old person dies and the average age of the family decreased by 8. Then in the year 2012, a baby is born. In which year the average age of the family will again be equal to the original average age of the family just before the person had died.
questions.solution_text:
Assume the average age before the person dies = a
Then the sum of ages = 4a
After the person dies, the average = $\frac{\left(4a-60\right)}{3}=a-8$
=> a = 36
So, the new average = 36-8 = 28
In the year 2012, the age of each person will increase by 4, hence the average will also increase by 4.
Before the baby is born, the average = 28+4 = 32
=> the sum of ages = 32*3 = 96
After the baby is born, the sum of ages will remain the same, but the number of members will increase to 4.
Hence, the new average = $\frac{96}{4}=24$
It will take 12 years for the average to become 24+12 = 36
Hence the year will be 2012+12 = 2024.

questions.question_text: The salaries of 21 employees of a company is in arithmetic progression with common difference greater than 0. The salaries are arranged in ascending order and ranked such that employee with the least salary is ranked 1. Three employees ranked 7th 10th and 18th leave the company. Which of the following is true?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The new average is less than the original average.

options.label: B
options.option_text: The new average is more than the original average.

options.label: C
options.option_text: The new average is equal to the original average.

questions.solution_text:
Assuming the terms to be a-10d,a-9d,a-8d…….a,a+d………a+10d
Original Average = 21a/21= a
Salary of 7th rank employee = a-4d
Salary of 10th rank employee = a-d
Salary of 18th rank employee = a+7d
Sum of the salary of 7th, 10th and 18th ranked employees = 3a+2d
Final Average=(21a-(3a+2d))/18 = (18a-2d)/18 = a-(d/9)
The new average is less than the original average.
Hence A is the answer.

Now, 2 cases can be formed:
From here, we can be sure that there's definitely a positive real root.

f(3) = 27-9-9-9 = 0 ...( x=3 is a root)

Determinant of the equation $x^2+2x+3=0$ is -8, which means the roots of the quadratic will be imaginary and in conjugate pairs.
So in total, we have 1 positive real root, a pair of imaginary roots and 0 negative real roots.

If the rate of interest is same and compounded annually, after n year the amount = $A\left(1+\frac{60}{100}\right)^n>16A$

=> n>$\frac{4\times\ 0.3010}{4\times\ 0.3010-1}=\ \frac{\ 1.2040}{0.2040}$
=> n>5.9
Minimum value of n=6

questions.question_text: If $A^2$ has 51 factors, how many factors will $A^5$ have?

If $A^2$ has 51 factors, it can either be of the form $A^2=a^{50}$ or $A^2=a^{16}\times\ b^2$, where 'a' and 'b' are prime numbers.
Case 1: $A^2=a^{50}$
$A=a^{25}$
=> $A^5=a^{125}$ and this will have (125+1) = 126 factors.
Case 2 : $A^2=a^{16}\times\ b^2$
$A=a^8\times\ b$
=> $A^5=a^{40}\times\ b^5$ and this will have ((40+1)(5+1)) = 246 factors.
So, both cases are possible.

Pipe C is closed after the tank is one-third full. Pipe B is closed after the tank is half full and A is used to fill the rest of the tank. If it took 110 minutes to fill the tank, what is the time taken to fill the tank if only A and B are open?
questions.solution_text:
Consider flow rate of A, B and C to be 1x, 2x and 3x tanks per minute,  and the capacity of tank as 1.
The pipes A,B,C are open till the tank is 1/3rd full. Total capacity of the pipes during that duration = 1x + 2x + 3x = 6x
Hence time taken for the tank to get till 1/3rd = $\dfrac{\frac{1}{3}}{6x} = \dfrac{1}{3\times6x}$
The pipes A,B are open from 1/3rd to 1/2 full i.e. they filled 1/6th tank. Total capacity of pipes during that duration = 1x + 2x = 3x
Hence time taken for the tank to get till 1/2 full from 1/3rd = $\dfrac{\frac{1}{6}}{3x} = \dfrac{1}{6\times3x}$The pipe A is open from 1/2rd to full tank i.e. it filled 1/2 tank. Total capacity of pipes during that duration = 1x 
Hence time taken for the tank to get full from 1/2nd = $\dfrac{\frac{1}{2}}{x} = \dfrac{1}{2\times x}$
$\frac{1}{3\times6x}+\frac{1}{6\times3x}+\frac{1}{2\times x}=110$
$\frac{11}{18}x=110$
=> $\frac{1}{x}=180$
Then time taken by A and B = $\frac{1}{x+2x}$ = 60 minutes

questions.question_text: Vessel A contains a solution of milk and water in the ratio 1:3. If 8 litres of the mixture is replaced with milk, then the new ratio becomes 3:5. Had p litres of mixture been replaced with milk, the amount of water and milk in the vessel would have become equal. Find the value of p.
questions.solution_text:
Assuming the amount of milk is x and the amount of water is 3x.
If 8 litres of mixture is removed, water and milk will be removed in the ratio 1:3. Hence, 2 litres of milk and 6 litres of water is removed. Also, 8 litres of milk is added.
=> $\dfrac{x-2+8}{3x-6}=\frac{3}{5}$
=> $\dfrac{x+6}{3x-6}=\frac{3}{5}$
=> 5x+30 = 9x-18
=> x=12
After replacing p litres of the mixture, the ratio of milk and water will become 1:1. In removal, p/4 milk will be removed and 3p/4 water will be removed. While adding p milk will be added.
=> $\dfrac{12-\frac{p}{4}+p}{36-\frac{3p}{4}}=\frac{1}{1}$
=> $\dfrac{12+\frac{3p}{4}}{36-\frac{3p}{4}}=1$
=> $\dfrac{3p}{2}=24$
=> p = 16

questions.question_text: 'Ring Throw' is a game in which there are ten objects arranged in a row. The participant has to throw three identical rings simultaneously such that each ring must encircle a different object. The participant will win only if the rings land on three different objects such that no two objects are adjacent to each other. The winner of the game is called a 'Ringham'. In how many different ways can a participant become a Ringham?
questions.solution_text:
Total number of ways of selecting 3 different objects from 10 objects = $^{10}C_{3} = 120$ ways
A participant can win only when no encircled objects are adjacent to each other.
So, we have to eliminate the cases where two rings or three rings land on objects adjacent to each other.
Number of ways of selecting three objects in which exactly two objects are adjacent
Case I: When the first and the second objects are selected
In this case, third object cannot be selected.
So, total number of ways = 7
Case II: When the last and the second last objects are selected
In this case, the eighth object cannot be selected
So, total number of ways = 7
Case II: When the two objects are selected such that none of them is from the extremes
In this case, the objects preceding as well as succeeding the selected pair cannot be selected
So, total number of ways = 7 * 6 = 42
Number of ways of selecting exactly three adjacent objects = 8
Therefore, the number of ways of selecting three objects such that no two are adjacent to each other
=120 - (7 + 7 + 42 + 8) = 56 ways.
Hence, 56 is the correct answer.

questions.question_text: A tank can be filled with two liquids A and B of different viscosity. Due to the viscosity, the liquids travel at different speeds in the pipe. The tank is equipped with 3 similar pipes. Liquid A can fill the tank in 10 hours if all the three pipes are used. Liquid B can fill the tank in 12 hours if 2 pipes are used. If a pipe can dispense only 1 liquid at a time, what is the minimum time needed to fill that tank with liquids A and B mixed in the ratio 3:7 ?
questions.solution_text:
Let us first calculate the time needed for a liquid to fill the tank if only 1 pipe is used. 
Since A takes 10 hours when 3 pipes are used, it will take 3 x 10 = 30 hours when only 1 pipe is used. 
Since B takes 12 hours when 2 pipes are used, it will take 2 x 12 = 24 hours when only 1 pipe is used. 
Let the capacity of the tank be $120x$ units. 
Speed of liquid A = $\dfrac{120x}{30} = 4x$ units/pipe/hour.
Speed of liquid B = $\dfrac{120x}{24} = 5x$ units/pipe/hour.
Now, volume of liquid A needed $V_{a} = \dfrac{3}{3+7} \times 120x = 36x$ units 
Volume of liquid B needed $V_{b} = \dfrac{7}{3+7} \times 120x = 84x$ units 
For the minimum amount of time, we first fill the required amount of liquid A (since it is the slower of the two liquids) as fast as possible. We do that by using all the three pipes to fill the tank with liquid A.
Thus, time  needed to fill the tank with the required amount of liquid A $t_{a} = \dfrac{36x}{4x \times 3} = 3$ hrs
Time needed to fill the tank with the required amount of liquid B $t_{b} = \dfrac{84x}{5x \times 3} = 5.6 hrs = 5 hr 36 min$
Thus the total time needed = 3 hr + 5 hr 36 min = 8 hr 36 min

Area of triangle = ½*base*height => 48 = ½ * 8* height

For height = 12 units, the vertex A should lie on either x=-18 or x=6.

questions.question_text: Four racers are running around a circular track at speed 1m/s, 3m/s, 4m/s and 6m/s in the same direction. What is the number of distinct points around the circular track at which two or more racers meet?
questions.solution_text:
The racers are running in the same direction, thus the number of points of intersections between any two racers= |a-b|, where a and b are the ratio of the speed of the racers.
The number of pairs of racers: $^4C_2$=6
Thus, 
1. The number of points of intersections between the first racer and second racer =  |1-3|=2 points i.e  $\left\{\pi\ ,\ 2\pi\ \right\}$
2. The number of points of intersections between the first racer and third racer = |1-4|=3 points i.e $\left\{2\pi\ ,\ \frac{2\pi\ }{3},\ \frac{4\pi\ }{3}\right\}$
3. The number of points of intersections between the first racer and fourth racer = |1-6|=5 points i.e $\left\{2\pi\ ,\frac{2\pi\ }{5},\frac{4\pi\ }{5},\frac{6\pi\ }{5},\frac{8\pi\ }{5}\right\}$
4. The number of points of intersections between the second racer and third racer = |3-4|=1 point i.e $\left\{2\pi\ \right\}$
5.The number of points of intersections between the second racer and fourth racer = (3,6) |1-2|=1 point i.e $\left\{2\pi\ \right\}$
6. The number of points of intersections between the third racer and fourth racer = (4,6) |2-3|=1 point i.e $\left\{2\pi\ \right\}$
Thus,  number of different points of intersection: $\left\{2\pi\ ,\frac{2\pi\ }{5},\frac{4\pi\ }{5},\frac{6\pi\ }{5},\frac{8\pi\ }{5},\pi\ ,\frac{2\pi\ }{3},\frac{4\pi\ }{3}\right\}$ 8 points
Option C

questions.question_text: In a rectangle ABCD where AB = 24 cm and BC = 9 cm. Points E and F are midpoints of side AB and CD. A circle is drawn in such a way that its centre coincides with rectangle’s centre. Find out the length of the diameter of the circle if both the lines DE and BF are tangents to the circle?
questions.solution_text:
Let us draw the diagram.
We know that E and F are the midpoints of AB and CD hence AE = EB= DF = FC = 12 cm
Changing the given lengths in coordinate system by assuming D at the origin and B at (24, 9).DC will become x axis and DA will become y axis. We can find out the coordinate of each point.
We can see from the symmetry that DE is parallel to line FB. The diameter of circle is essentially the perpendicular distance between line DE and FB 
Equation of line DE 
$\Rightarrow$  y - 0 = $\frac{9 - 0}{12 - 0}$(x - 0)
$\Rightarrow$  3x - 4y = 0         ... (1)
Similarly the equation of line FB
$\Rightarrow$  y - 0 = $\frac{9 - 0}{24 - 12}$(x - 12)
$\Rightarrow$  3x - 4y = 36      ...  (2)
Distance between parallel lines DE and FB
d = |$\frac{36 - 0}{\sqrt{3^2+4^2}}$|
d = 7.2 cm
Therefore we can say that diameter of the circle = 7.2 cm
Hence option A is the correct answer.

questions.question_text: There are 3 test-matches going on.The first one is between India and Australia. The probability that India wins is $\frac{1}{6}$. The probability that Australia wins is $\frac{1}{5}$. The second test is between Sri Lanka and England where the chances of Sri Lanka winning is $\frac{1}{10}$ and England winning is $\frac{1}{5}$. In the third match between South Africa and Pakistan, the chances of South Africa winning is $\frac{1}{3}$ and that of Pakistan winning is $\frac{1}{8}$. Find the probability that all 3 matches end in a draw.
questions.solution_text:
In the match between India and Australia,
P(India wins) = $\frac{1}{6}$
P(Australia wins) = $\frac{1}{5}$
P(Draw) = $1-\frac{1}{5}-\frac{1}{6}=\frac{19}{30}$
In the match between Sri Lanka and England,
P(Sri Lanka wins) = $\frac{1}{10}$
P(England wins) = $\frac{1}{5}$
P(Draw) = $1-\frac{1}{10}-\frac{1}{5}\ =\ \frac{7}{10}$
In the match between South Africa and Pakistan,
P(South Africa wins) = $\frac{1}{3}$
P(Australia wins) = $\frac{1}{8}$
P(Draw) = $1-\frac{1}{3}-\frac{1}{8}=\frac{13}{24}$
P(All matches draw) = P(Match 1 draw) + P(Match 2 draw)+ P(Match 3 draw)
=$\frac{19}{30}\times\ \frac{7}{10}\times\ \frac{13}{24}=\frac{1729}{7200}$

questions.question_text: A coin of diameter $3 cm$ is thrown on a square mat of area $100 cm ^2$. What is the probability that the coin will fall entirely within the square?
questions.solution_text:
The area of the square mat is $100 cm^2$. Therefore, the side of the mat must be $\sqrt{100}$ = $10 cm$. 
The centre of the coin must be at least $1.5 cm$ away from the edge of the mat if the coin were to lie completely within the mat. Therefore, the area within which the centre of the coin can fall will be a square of side $10 - 2*1.5$ = $7 cm$.
Therefore, the area inside which the centre of the coin can fall = $49 cm^2$.
Total area = $100 cm^2$.
Therefore, the probability is $\frac{49}{100}$ = $0.49$. Hence, option D is the right answer.

questions.question_text: A number is represented as 1212 in base N and as 250 in base N+2. Find the sum of even factors of the number.
questions.solution_text:
The number in base 10 = $N^3+2N^2+N+2\ $ = $2\left(N+2\right)^2+5\left(N+2\right)$
Thus,
$N^3+2N^2+N+2\ =\ 2\left(N+2\right)^2+5\left(N+2\right)$
$N^3+2N^2+N+2\ =\ 2\left(N^2+4N+4\right)+5\left(N+2\right)$
$N^3+2N^2+N+2\ =\ 2N^2+8N+8+5N+10$
$N^3-12N-16=0$
By hit and trial we see that N = -2 satisfies the equation, hence N+2 is a factor. Dividing the expression by N+2, we get,
$N^3-12N-16=\left(N+2\right)^2\left(N-4\right)$
So it has 2 factors, N = -2 and N = 4.
Since base cannot be negative, N = 4 is the right base.
N + 2 =6
So, in base 6, the number is 250.
Hence in base 10 (decimal system), N = $2\times\ 6^2+5\times\ 6=72+30=102$
102 = $2\times\ 3\times\ 17$
Hence, sum of even powers = $2^1\left(3^0+3^1\right)\left(17^0+17^1\right)=2\times\ 4\times\ 18=144$

Where a and k are constant, and p is the number of people in the lift.

The lift will stop moving when it speed is zero. In that case
$a+k\sqrt{p}=0$
$40=10\sqrt{p}$
$a+k\sqrt{p}=0$
=> p=16

questions.question_text: The difference between compound interest and simple interest on a certain sum borrowed at R% per annum for a period of 2 years is Rs.384 and for a period of 3 years is Rs.1344. Find the time in which the sum becomes 6 times itself at simple interest.
questions.solution_text:
Let the borrowed sum be P 
Now, we know that 
The difference between compound interest and simple interest for a period of 2 years is given by: $P\left(\frac{R}{100}\right)^2$ 
The difference between compound interest and simple interest for a period of 3 years is given by:$P\left(\frac{R}{100}\right)^2\left(\frac{R}{100}+3\right)$
so, substituting the given values we get :
$P\left(\frac{R}{100}\right)^2$=384         (1)
$P\left(\frac{R}{100}\right)^2\left(\frac{R}{100}+3\right)$ = 1344     (2)
Dividing equation (2) and (1) we get
$\left(\frac{R}{100}+3\right)$=$\frac{1344}{384}$
⇒$\left(\frac{R}{100}+3\right)$=$\frac{7}{2}$
⇒$\left(\frac{R}{100}\right)$=$\frac{1}{2}$
⇒R=50%
Now let sum becomes 6 times itself in T years at simple interest
We know that 
Amount = Principal (sum borrowed)+Interest(in this case it is simple interest)
⇒6P=P+$\frac{\left(P\times\ 50\times\ T\ \right)}{100}$
⇒5P=$\frac{PT}{2}$
⇒T=10
Hence the sum becomes 6 times itself in 10 years.

questions.question_text: What is the minimum value of the expression $\frac{3x^2-7}{3x^2+1} + \frac{2x^2-5}{2x^2+5}$?

Expression 1: $\frac{3x^2-7}{3x^2+1}$
$=1-\frac{8}{3x^2+1}$
To minimize the given expression we have to maximize $\frac{8}{3x^2+1}$
This will be maximum when $3x^2+1$ will be minimum.
The least value of $3x^2+1$ is 1 when $x=0$
Thus the minimum value of the given expression 1 is 
$=1-8=-7$
Expression 2: $\frac{2x^2-5}{2x^2+5}$
$=1-\frac{10}{2x^2+5}$
To minimize the given expression we have to maximize $\frac{10}{2x^2+5}$
This will be maximum when $2x^2+5$ will be minimum.
The least value of $2x^2+5$ is 5 when $x=0$
Thus the minimum value of the given expression 2 is 
$=1-2=-1$
Thus the minimum value of the given expression is $-7-1 = -8$

questions.question_text: A and B start from a point P on a circular track. Both move in the opposite direction such that ratio of their speeds is 7:11. If circumference of the 44 meters. What is the shortest distance between the points where they meet for 5th time and the point where they meet for the 8th time?
questions.solution_text:
Circumference = 2$\pi$= 44
=> r= 7 m
Divide the circumference into 7+11 =18 equal parts.
Then they will meet for the first time when A moves 7 parts in his direction and B moves 11 parts in the opposite direction.
Now consider the movement of A, A moves 7 parts between two points, hence between 5th and 8th meeting point he will travel (8-5)*7 = 21 parts.
Now the distance along the circumference between two points = 21 mod 18 = 3 parts
Now 3 parts will subtend angle (3/18)*360 = 60 at the centre.
Therefore the radii joining two points and the line joining two points will form an equilateral triangle. 
Hence the distance between two points  = radius = 7m

The numbers are not of the form 6k±1 and hence, a cannot be 4

questions.question_text: A milkman bought 15 litres of milk and mixed it with 3 litres of mineral water (which is not free). He claims to his customers, who do not know about mixing, that he is making a profit of 10% only. However, his actual profit is 20%. What is the ratio of the cost of milk/litre and water/litre.
questions.solution_text:
Let the CP of milk be Rs. 100/litre
As he is claiming 10% profit, SP of the total mixture = Rs. [(15 + 3) * 110] = Rs. 1980
Actual profit = 20%
Let actual CP be Rs. x. 
Then, x + 20% of x = Rs. 1980
Solving for x, we get x = Rs. 1650
So, Actual CP = Total CP of milk + Total CP of water
Or, Total CP of water = Rs. 1650 - (15 * 100) = Rs. 150
Or, CP of water = Rs. 50/litre
Required ratio = 100:50 = 2:1
Hence, option C is correct.

questions.question_text: A hose-pipe is attached to the bottom of a cylindrical water tank with a base radius 15m and height 10m. The speed of discharge of water from the hose pipe is 30 m/sec. If the radius of the hose-pipe is 2cm, what is the time taken to empty the full tank?
questions.solution_text:
The volume of tank = Speed of discharge * time * area of cross-section of the pipe
$\pi\ \times\ 15^2\times\ 10=\ \left(30\right)\times\ \left(time\right)\ \times\ \pi\ \times\ 0.02\times\ 0.02$              (2 cm = 0.02 m)
=>Time = $\frac{\left(15\times\ 15\times\ 10\right)}{30\times\ 0.02\times\ 0.02}$ seconds = 187500 seconds 
=> TIme = $\frac{187500}{60\times\ 60} \ =\ 52.08$ hours

questions.question_text: A broken clock loses 45 seconds in 3 minutes, while another damaged clock gains 30 seconds in 6 minutes. Both clocks were set right at 9 AM in the morning. What will be the absolute value of the difference in the angle made by the minute and hour hand of the two clocks on the next day at 3 PM?
questions.solution_text:
The first clock loses 45 seconds in 3 minutes or 15 minutes an hour while the second clock gains 30 seconds in 6 minutes or 5 minutes per hour. In the next 30 hours (from 9 AM to 3 PM the next day), the first clock would have lost 7 hours 30 minutes, while the second clock would have gained 2 hours 30 minutes. Thus, at 3 PM, the first clock would show the time as 7:30 AM, while the second will display 5:30 PM.
The angle between the hour hand (H) and minute hand (M) = $ \theta\ =\left | 30H-\frac{11}{2}M \right |$ ; for the first clock  $\theta\ =45^{\circ\ }$ while for the second clock $\theta\ =15^{\circ\ }$
The absolute difference of the values = $30^{\circ\ }$
Hence, Option A is the correct choice.

questions.question_text:
Ram and Shyam are running on different circular tracks. In the time that Ram completes 4 rounds of his track, Shyam completes 3 rounds of his track. 
If Ram and Shyam interchange their tracks the time taken by both of them to complete 1 round is same. What is the ratio of speeds of Ram and Shyam?
questions.solution_text:
Let the radius of Ram’s track be a and that of Shyam’s track be b.
In the time that Ram travels 4 rounds, Shyam travels 3 rounds so
Distance travelled by Ram in 4 rounds = 4*2πa 
Distance travelled by Shyam in 3 rounds = 3*2πb, So if both of them take same time then the ratio of their speeds is given by
$\frac{\textrm{speed of Ram}}{\textrm{Speed of Shyam}} = \frac{4*2πa }{3*2πb} = \frac{4a}{3b}$ (I)
Now when they interchange their tracks
They cover 1 round in same time, so we have
$\frac{\textrm{speed of Ram}}{\textrm{Speed of Shyam}} = \frac{2πb }{2πa} = \frac{b}{a}$ (II)
So we have $\frac{4a}{3b} = \frac{b}{a} $
=> $ \frac{a^{2}}{b^{2}} = \frac{3}{4}$
=> $\frac{a}{b} =\sqrt{\frac{3}{4}}$
Putting this value in equation II, we get
$\frac{\textrm{speed of Ram}}{\textrm{Speed of Shyam}}$ = $\sqrt{\frac{4}{3}}$

questions.question_text: The cost of 5 apples, 7 bananas and 9 mangoes is Rs 204 and the cost of 8 apples, 5 bananas and 2 mangoes is Rs 159. Find the total cost of 1 apple, 1 banana and 1 mango.

Let the cost of 1 apple, 1 banana and 1 mango be a, b and c respectively.
5a + 7b + 9c = 204
8a + 5b + 2c = 159
Coefficients are in AP in both the equations.
The differences of coefficients in the first equation are 2 and the differences of coefficients in the second equation are 3.
Hence, multiply the first equation by 3 and multiply the second equation by 2.
15a + 21b + 27c = 612
16a + 10b + 4c = 318
=> 31a + 31b + 31c = 930
=> a + b + c = 30

questions.question_text: Point B is taken at random in a circle of radius r units. Let x be the distance of the point B from the centre and y be the shortest distance of B from the circle's circumference. What is the probability that x$\ge\ $2y?
questions.solution_text:
The distance of the point B from the centre is of x units. The distance of the point from the nearest point on the circle will be (r-x) units, where r is the length of the radius. 
It is given that $x\ge2\left(r-x\right)\ $
=>$x\ge2r-2x\ $
=>$3x\ge2r\ $
=>$x\ge\ \frac{\ 2r}{3}$
Now, the point selected at random must lie anywhere between the two circle (the region which is not coloured), because the boundary of the blue circle is the minimum distance of the point from the circle. 
So, area of the unshaded region= $\pi\ r^2-\pi\ x^2=\pi\ \left(r^2-\frac{4r^2}{9}\right)=\ \frac{\ 5\pi\ r^2}{9}$
The sample space can be the entire circle with radius r units, which is $\pi\ r^2$
Therefore, required probability= $\ \frac{\ 5\pi\ r^2}{9\pi\ r^2}=\ \frac{\ 5}{9}$

questions.question_text: If the area of the largest(in terms of area) right-angled triangle inscribed in a circle C decreases by 51% when the radius of the circle is decreased by p%, what is the value of p? Round off to the nearest integer.
questions.solution_text:
The following figure shows a right-angled triangle inscribed in a circle.
Let the radius of the circle be r. Hence, the largest right-angled triangle will have the hypotenuse as the diameter and the remaining two sides equal. Hence, it is isosceles as well.
Area = $\frac{1}{2}\left(2r\right)\left(r\right)=r^2$
Now let the new radius be $r_1$
Hence, the new area = $r_1^2$
Since $r_1^2=\frac{100-51}{100}r^2$
$r_1^2=\frac{49}{100}r^2$
$r_1=\frac{7}{10}r$
$\frac{r-r_1}{r}=\frac{r-\frac{7}{10}r}{r}=\frac{3}{10}$
Hence, there is a 30% reduction in r's value.

questions.question_text: It takes 1 pipe of type A, 2 pipes of type B and 2 pipes of type C to fill an empty tank completely in 3 hours. Instead, if 2 pipes of type A and 1 pipe of type B are used as inlets, and 1 pipe of type C is used as an outlet, the tank is filled in 12 hours. What will be the time taken to fill the tank using 5 pipes of type A and 4 pipes of type B all used as inlets?
questions.solution_text:
Assuming the flow rate of pipe A, pipe B and pipe C is a, b and c respectively and the capacity of the tank is A units.
Then, 3(a+2b+2c) = A
=> a+2b+2c = $\frac{A}{3}$.......(1)
Also, 12(2a+b-c) = A
=> 2a+b-c = $\frac{A}{12}$ ......(2)
Now,  the combined flow rate of 5 pipes of type A and 4 pipes of type B = 5a+4b
(a+2b+2c)*3 = (2a+b-c )*12
6c = 7a+2b
Let x be the number of days taken by 5 pipes of type A and 4 pipes of type B all used as inlets to fill the tank
(5a+4b) * x = (a+2b+2c)*3
(5a+4b)*x= 10a+8b
x = 2
So, time taken to fill A completely = 2 hours

$ 4\times(x-2n)=(y-2n)$

Let the sides of the triangle be $x$ and $y$
It is given that,

Adding $4$ to both sides of the equation

or,  $(x + 2)(y + 2) = 144$
Applying AM $\geq $ GM

Replacing the value of $(x + 2)(y + 2)$ by $144$ , we get
$\dfrac{(x + 2) + (y + 2)}{2} \geq \sqrt{144}$
or,  $(x + y + 4) \geq 24$
or,  $(x + y) \geq 20$
=>  $2(x + y) \geq 40$
Thus, the perimeter of the rectangle is at least $40$ units.
Hence, option C is the correct answer.

So, we can select the chocolates in 26 ways and then arrange each in 5! ways.
Total no. of permutations = 26 x 5! ways.

Let the distance between P and Q be 'D'.
It is given,
$\frac{36}{V_A}+\frac{D}{0.8V_A}+\frac{66}{60}=\frac{D}{V_B}$ ........ (1)
If B travels one kilometre in t minutes, then A travels one kilometre in t - 2 minutes.
Speed of A = $\frac{60}{t-2}$
Speed of B = $\frac{60}{t}$
It is also given that A covers distance D in 30 minutes, i.e. speed of A = $V_A$ = 2D ........ (2)
$\frac{60}{t-2}=2D$
$60=2tD-4D$
$t\ =\ \frac{\ 60+4D}{2D}$
speed of B = $V_B$ = $\frac{30D}{15+D}$ ........ (3)
Substituting (2) and (3) in (1), we get
$4D^2-147D-2160=0$
$4D^2-192D+45D-2160=0$
Solving, we get D = 48 km
The answer is option C.

questions.question_text: A cylinder and a cone have the same base radius and the same height. The radius of the cylinder is doubled and its height is tripled while the radius of the cone is tripled and its height is doubled. What is the ratio of the new volumes of the cylinder and the cone?
questions.solution_text:
Let the initial radius of cylinder and cone be ‘r’ and height be ‘h’
So for cylinder, the new radius is 2r and height is 3h
The volume of the cylinder is $ \pi (2r)^{2}*3h = 12 \pi r^{2}h$
The new radius of cone is 3r and its new height is 2h
So the required volume is $\frac{1}{3}\pi(3r)^{2}*2h = 6 \pi r^{2}h$
Hence the required ratio is 2:1

questions.question_text: The average weight of 10 items is 20 kg. The weight of each item has an integral value. When the weights are arranged in descending order, the first three weights are 25 kg, 22kg and 21 kg. What can be the lowest possible weight of an item?
questions.solution_text:
The average weight of 10 items is 20 kg.
Then the sum of all the weights is 20*10 = 200kg
Now top three heaviest weights are 25kg, 22kg and 21kg.
Then to minimize the weight of an item, we have to maximise the 4th heaviest to the 9th heaviest items.
The maximum value which the 4th heaviest to the 9th heaviest items can take is 21 kg
Hence, the lowest possible weight of an item = 200-25-22-21*7 = 6 kg

questions.question_text: An ATM machine contains 100 rupee, 200 rupee and 500 rupee notes. The machine contains 200 notes in total and the total value of the notes is Rs. 45,000. If the number of 500 rupee notes and 100 rupee notes are interchanged, then the net value of the notes in the machine increases by Rs. 20,000. What will be the total value of the notes in the machine if the number of 100 rupee notes and 200 rupee notes are interchanged?
questions.solution_text:
Let the number of 100 rupee notes be x, 200 rupee notes be y and 500 rupee notes be z.
It has been given that,
x + y + z = 200 -----------------(1)
100x + 200y + 500z = 45,000 ------------(2)
If the number of 100 rupee and 500 rupee notes are interchanged, then the value increases by 20,000.
Therefore, 500x + 200y + 100z = 65,000--------(3)
Subtracting (2) from (3), we get,
400x - 400z = 20,000
x-z = 50
x = 50+z -------(4)
Multiplying (1) by 200 and subtracting it from (2), we get,
-100x + 300z = 5000
3z - x = 50
x = 3z - 50 ---------(5)
Equating (4) and (5), we get, 
50 + z = 3z - 50
2z = 100
z = 50
We know that x = 50+z
=> x = 100
x+y+z = 200
100 + y + 50 = 200
y = 50
Therefore, x = 100, y = 50 and z =50.
If the number of 100 and 200 rupee notes are interchanged, then the net value will be
50*100 + 100*200 + 50*500 = 5,000 + 20,000 + 25,000.
Total value = Rs.50,000.
Therefore, option B is the right answer.

questions.question_text: The distance between Chandigarh and Amritsar is 500 kms. A train starts from Chandigarh to Amritsar on Monday. In the midst of the journey, a technical glitch forces the driver to reduce the speed of the train by 20%. Had the glitch occurred 40 kms later, the train would have reached Amritsar 7 mins and 30 seconds earlier. Find the original speed of the train (before the glitch).
questions.solution_text:
Let the speed of the train be $a$ km/hr and the point at which the glitch occurs, say P be $x$ kms from Chandigarh. 
In the given case, we do not know the actual distance when the glitch happens. Since the question states the difference between the total time taken to complete the journey, we will express the situation in terms of time taken. 
Total time taken for the journey in the first case $t_{1} = \dfrac{x}{a} + \dfrac{500-x}{0.8a} $ (the first term in RHS is the time take to reach P while the second term in RHS is the time taken to travel the remaining distance at the reduced speed) 
Similarly, total time taken for the journey in the second case $t_{2} = \dfrac{x+40}{a} + \dfrac{500-(x+40)}{0.8a} $ (the first term in RHS is the time taken to reach a point 40 kms ahead of P, say Q and the second term is the time taken to travel the remaining distance at the reduced speed) 
Since in the second case, the train travels faster for a longer duration, the time taken in the first case will be greater. 
Given, $t_{1} - t_{2} = \dfrac{7.5}{60} hr $
$\dfrac{x}{a} + \dfrac{500-x}{0.8a} - (\dfrac{x+40}{a} + \dfrac{500-(x+40)}{0.8a}) = \dfrac{1}{8} hr$
$\Rightarrow \dfrac{x - (x+40)}{a} + \dfrac{500-x-(500-x-40)}{0.8a}) = \dfrac{1}{8} $
$\Rightarrow \dfrac{-40}{a} + \dfrac{40}{0.8a} = \dfrac{1}{8} $
$ \Rightarrow \dfrac{-40}{a} + (\dfrac{5}{4} \times \dfrac{40}{a}) = \dfrac{1}{8} $
$ \Rightarrow \dfrac{-40}{a} + \dfrac{50}{a} = \dfrac{1}{8} $
$ \Rightarrow \dfrac{10}{a} = \dfrac{1}{8} $
$ \Rightarrow a = 80$ km/hr

questions.question_text: Ramesh was supposed to board a flight from an airport which has 15 gates in a straight line. The distance between any adjacent pair of gates is 80 feet. His departure gate was initially assigned at random. After waiting at the assigned gate, Ramesh is informed that the departure gate has been changed to a different gate. If the probability that Ramesh covered a distance of 400 feet or less to reach to the new gate can be represented as $\dfrac{a}{b}$, where ‘$a$’ and ‘$b$’ are relatively prime numbers, then find out the remainder when '$b$' is divided by ‘$a$’?
questions.solution_text:
Total ways of selecting two different gates out of 15 gates = 15*14 = 210.
If Ramesh was assigned previously gate no. 1 or 15 then, there are a total of 5 other gates within 400 feet. 
Similarly, Ramesh was assigned previously gate no. 2 or 14 then there are a total of 6 other gates within 400 feet. 
Ramesh was assigned previously gate no. 3 or 13 then there are a total of 7 other gates within 400 feet.
Ramesh was assigned previously gate no. 4 or 12 then there are a total of 8 other gates within 400 feet
Ramesh was assigned previously gate no. 5 or 11 then there are a total of 9 other gates within 400 feet
Ramesh was assigned previously gate no. From 6 to 10 then, there are a total of 10 other gates within 400 feet. 
Hence total number of favourable cases = 2[5+6+7+8+9]+5*10 = 120
Therefore the required probability = $\dfrac{120}{210}$
$\Rightarrow$ $\dfrac{4}{7}=\dfrac{a}{b}$
We can see that, 7 mod 4 = 3.

questions.question_text: The average of a set of positive integers is 79. If the integer 107 which is also present in the set is removed, the average is reduced by 2. What can be the largest possible number in the new set?
questions.solution_text:
Assume the total number of integers = n, then the sum = 79n
Now, the new average after removing 107 = $\ \frac{\ 79n-107}{n-1}$ = 77
=> 79n-107 = 77n-77
=> 2n = 30 => n=15
Now, the number of integers in the new set = 14, The new sum = 14*77 = 1078
To make one number greatest, we have to assume the rest of the numbers as 1. 
Hence, the largest number = 1078-13*1 = 1065
C is the answer.

questions.question_text:
If p, q and r are 3 natural numbers such that $\dfrac{p}{q}$ = $\dfrac{4}{3}$ then which of the following can be a value of 
{$\dfrac{p}{q}+\dfrac{q}{r}+\dfrac{r}{p}+\dfrac{r}{q}+\dfrac{p}{r}+\dfrac{q}{p}$}
questions.solution_text:
Given, $\dfrac{p}{q}$ = $\dfrac{4}{3}$
Therefore, $\dfrac{q}{p}$ = $\dfrac{3}{4}$
Hence, $\dfrac{q}{p}$+$\dfrac{p}{q}$ = $\dfrac{4}{3}$+$\dfrac{3}{4} = \dfrac{25}{12}$
For any natural number x we know, $x+\dfrac{1}{x} \geq 2$
Hence, $\dfrac{p}{r}+\dfrac{r}{p} \geq 2$
Also, $\dfrac{q}{r}+\dfrac{r}{q} \geq 2$
$\dfrac{p}{r}+\dfrac{r}{p}$ = 2 if $r=p$
$\dfrac{q}{r}+\dfrac{r}{q}$ = 2 if $r=q$ i.e. $r=p=q$
But that is not the case as $\dfrac{p}{q}$ = $\dfrac{4}{3}$
Hence, if $\dfrac{p}{r}+\dfrac{r}{p} = 2$ then $\dfrac{r}{q}+\dfrac{q}{r}$ is definitely greater than 2.
Hence, {$\dfrac{p}{q}+\dfrac{q}{r}+\dfrac{r}{p}+\dfrac{r}{q}+\dfrac{p}{r}+\dfrac{q}{p}$} $> \dfrac{25}{12} + 2 + 2$
Hence, {$\dfrac{p}{q}+\dfrac{q}{r}+\dfrac{r}{p}+\dfrac{r}{q}+\dfrac{p}{r}+\dfrac{q}{p}$} $> \dfrac{73}{12}$
The only option here greater than $\dfrac{73}{12}$ is $\dfrac{27}{4}$ Which comes for r = 6, p = 4 and q = 3.
Hence, option D is the correct answer.

questions.question_text: What is the value of $[\sqrt{0.5}] + [\sqrt{1}]+ [\sqrt{1.5}]+ [\sqrt{2}]+ ……. + [\sqrt{10}]$ where [X] represents the greatest integer function?
questions.solution_text:
We know that $\sqrt{0.5}$ = 0.707; So $[\sqrt{0.5}]$ = 0
For every term from $\sqrt{1}$ to $\sqrt{3.5}$ will be $\geq$ 1 but < 2. Hence [.] will be equals to 1 for each such term.
Total such terms = 6 
For every term from $\sqrt{4}$ to $\sqrt{8.5}$ will be $\geq$ 2 but < 3. Hence [.] will be equals to 2 for each such term.
Total such terms = 10 
For every term form $\sqrt{9}$ to $\sqrt{10}$ will be $\geq$ 3 but < 4. Hence [.] will be equals to 3 for each such term.
Total such terms = 3 
Therefore total value = 1*0 + 6*1 +10*2 + 3*3 = 35

questions.question_text: If the area of a regular hexagon is $6\sqrt{3}$ sq units, find out the area of a regular octagon that shares a side with the regular hexagon.
questions.solution_text:
The area of a regular hexagon = 6 x Area of an equilateral triangle having the same side
$6\sqrt{3}$ = $6\frac{\sqrt{3}}{4}a^2$
a = 2
Now, if we have an octagon of side 2, the area of the octagon = $2\left(1+\sqrt{\ 2}\right)a^2=8\left(1+\sqrt{\ 2}\right)$
The area can also be calculated without the formula.
Area of 4 rectangles + Area of square + Area of 4 triangles
$(4\times\ 2\times\ \sqrt{\ 2})+( 2\times\ 2 ) + (4\times\ \frac{1}{2}\times\ \sqrt{\ 2}\times\ \sqrt{\ 2})=8+8\sqrt{\ 2}$

questions.question_text: If $x^2+4ax+20-2a$ > 0 for all real x, then which of the following holds true for all the values of a?
questions.solution_text:
The co-efficient of $x^2$ is greater than 0, so the discriminant should be less than zero, if the given expression is greater than 0 for all values of x.
$(4a)^2$ - 4*1*(20-2a) < 0
=> $16a^2 - 80+8a$ < 0
=> $2a^2+a-10$ < 0
=> $2a^2 + 5a - 4a - 10$ < 0
=> a(2a+5)-2(2a+5) < 0
=> (a-2)(2a+5)<0
$\frac{-5}{2}$ < a < 2
B is the correct answer.

questions.question_text: In an equilateral triangle, another triangle is formed using 2 vertices of the triangle and the incenter of the equilateral triangle. What is the ratio of the in-radius of the equilateral triangle and the in-radius of the triangle so formed?
questions.solution_text:
Let ABC be the equilateral triangle and I be the incenter. Join BI and IC to form triangle BIC as shown below:-
Let the side of the equilateral triangle be $2\sqrt{3}$ cm
As we know the length of the in-radius of an equilateral triangle = $\dfrac{side}{ 2\sqrt{3}} = \dfrac{2\sqrt{3}}{2\sqrt{3}} $
Thus, the in radius of the equilateral triangle = 1 cm.
Thus, IJ = 1 cm.
We know BC = $2\sqrt{3}$ cm
Thus, $BJ = \sqrt{3}$…..(median bisects the side)
Thus, BI = $\sqrt{1+3} = 2$
Thus, BI = CI = 2 cm.
Area of triangle BIC = $\dfrac{1}{2}*IJ*BC = \dfrac{1}{2}*1*2\sqrt{3} = \sqrt{3}$
Also, Area of triangle BIC = sr
s = $\dfrac{2+2+2\sqrt{3}}{2} = 2+\sqrt{3}$
Thus, $(2+\sqrt{3})*r = \sqrt{3}$
Thus, $r = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{(2+\sqrt{3})}$
Thus, the required ratio = $1:\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{(2+\sqrt{3})}$ = $(2+\sqrt{3}):\sqrt{3}$
Hence, option A is the correct answer.

questions.question_text: Sumitra has to solve 384 questions. She decides to solve a particular number of questions per day to complete the task in a certain number of days. Shalini, her friend, suggests that if she solves eight more questions per day than what Sumitra has decided, she will take eight fewer days to finish the task than what Sumitra has calculated. In how many days can the task be completed if Sumitra follows what Shalini suggested?
questions.solution_text:
Let the number of questions to be solved per day be $x$, and the number of days required be $y$ as per Sumitra's plan.
So, $xy = 384$
As per Shalini, 
$(x + 8)(y - 8) = 384$
or,  $xy - 8x + 8y - 64 = 384$
or,  $8y - 8x = 64$
or,  $y - x = 8$
Putting $y = \dfrac{384}{x}$, we get
$\dfrac{384}{x} - x = 8$
or,  $384 - x^2 = 8x$
or,  $x^2 + 8x - 384 = 0$
On solving, we get $x = -24$ or $x = 16$
But,  $x$ cannot be negative.
So,  $x = 16$
=>  $y = \dfrac{384}{x} = 24$
According to Shalini, number of days required =  $ (y - 8) = 16$ days
Hence, 16 is the required answer.

questions.question_text: Bombs are fired on a bridge such that a probability of a bomb hitting the bridge is 0.5. A minimum of two bombs are required to hit a bridge in order to destroy it. Find the minimum number of hits required such that probability of destroying a bridge is greater than 0.8.
questions.solution_text:
We need the probability of atleast two hits
= 1 - probability of less than two hits
= 1 - (probabilty of 0 hits + probability of 1 hit)
Let n be the number of hits,
Then probability of 0 hits = $(\frac{1}{2})^n$ , since for each turn probability of missing = 1/2
Probability of 1 hit = $n*\frac{1}{2}*(\frac{1}{2})^{n-1}$ = $n*(\frac{1}{2})^n$, since the turn which will hit can be selected in $^nC_1$ ways and probability of hitting in that turn = 1/2 and probability that all other n-1 turns will miss is $(\frac{1}{2})^{n-1}$.
Hence probability of atleast two hits = 1 - $(\frac{1}{2})^n$ - $n*(\frac{1}{2})^n$
The minimum value of n for which the above value is greater than 0.8 is 5

questions.question_text:
If $t>2$, what is the solution set of the inequality

$(t-2)^{t^2 - 6t + 8} > 1$?
questions.solution_text:
Taking logarithm on both sides, we get,
$(t^2 - 6t + 8) log (t-2) > log 1 = 0$
=>$(t - 2)(t - 4) log (t-2) > 0$
For t < 2 and t > 4, (t-2)(t-4) > 0. In this case, for the inequality to hold, log (t-2) > 0
=> t - 2 > 1 => t > 3
The common interval is t > 4
For 2 < t < 4, (t-2)(t-4) < 0. In this case, for the inequality to hold, log (t-2) < 0
=> t - 2 < 1 => t < 3
The common interval is 2 < t < 3
So, the solution set is 2 < t < 3 U t > 4

questions.question_text: One of the roots of the equation $x^2 - (m - 2)x + 6 = 0$ lies between (0, 2) and the other root lies between (3, 4). It is known that $m$ is an integer. What is the sum of all the possible values of $m$?
questions.solution_text:
We know that the graph of a quadratic polynomial cuts x-axis at the points which are also the roots of the quadratic equation. Therefore, the value of the polynomial will be opposite in sign on the two points between which the roots lie.
In this graph, we can observe that the polynomial changes its sign at the roots.
In the given question, one of the roots lie between (0, 2) and the other root lie between (3, 4)
Let $f(x) = x^2 - (m - 2)x + 6$
So, $f(0) > 0$.................(i)
So, $f(2) < 0$.................(i)
So, $f(3) < 0$.................(i)
So, $f(4) > 0$.................(i)
We can write (i) as $6>0$ which is always true
We can write (ii) as
$(14 - 2m) < 0$
$m > 7$
We can write (iii) as
$9-3*(m-2)+6<0$
or $m > 7$
We can write (iv) as
$16-4*(m-2)+6>0$
or, $m<7.5$
Therefore, $m$ belongs to $(7, \dfrac{15}{2})$
Thus, no integral value of $m$ satisfies it.
Hence, option D is the correct answer.

Muthu meets Vivek after 15 seconds with speed 10m/s. Distance covered is 150m.

When Vivek reaches A, Muthu would have covered a Distance of 100m.

Circumference= 150+100+350=600m

questions.question_text: p, q, r and s are four distinct real numbers such that $p^2 - q = q^2 - r = r^2 - s = s^2 - p$, what is the value of (p + q)(q + r)(r + s)(s + p)?
questions.solution_text:
$p^2 - q = q^2 - r$
$p^2 - q^2 = q - r$
=> $ p + q = \frac{q - r}{p - q}$ -(1)
Similarly, $ q + r = \frac{r - s}{q - r}$(2)
$ r + s = \frac{s - p}{r - s}$ - (3)
$ s + p = \frac{p - r}{s - p}$ - (4)
From (1), (2), (3) and (4) we get (p + q)(q + r)(r + s)(s + p) = $\frac{q - r}{p - q} \times \frac{r - s}{q - r} \times \frac{p - q}{r - s} \times \frac{p - r}{ s - p} = 1$

questions.question_text: What is the absolute difference between the number of 3-digit even numbers that have at least one 2 in them and those that do not have any 2 in them?
questions.solution_text:
Number of 3 digit numbers is 999 - 100 + 1 = 900
Since it starts with an even number and ends with an odd number, it has an equal number of even and odd numbers.
So, the number of even numbers = 900/2 = 450.
Now we need to count the number of even numbers with no 2 in it.
Unit's digit can be filled with any of 0, 4, 6 and 8, since it is an even number and does not contain 2. Count = 4
Ten's digit can have any number from 0 to 9 except for 2. Count = 9
Hundred's digit can have any number from 1 to 9 except for 2. Count = 8
Hence, total number of 3-digit even numbers with no 2 in them = $4\times\ 9\times\ 8=288$
Hence, total number of 3-digit even numbers with at least one 2 in them = 450 - 288 = 162
Hence, difference = 288 - 162 = 126

questions.question_text: If |x+1|<6 and |y-1|<6 where x,y are integers, what can be the maximum value of x$^{2}$+y$^{2}$-xy
questions.solution_text:
We have, |x+1|<6 and |y-1|<6
|x+1|<6   => -6<x+1<6  =>  -7<x<5
|y-1|<6 => -6< y-1<6 => -5<y<7.
Since x$^{2}$+y$^{2}$ is positive, the value will be maximized when xy is negative.
The highest negative value of x = -6 and highest positive value of y is 6.
Hence the maximum value of x$^{2}$+y$^{2}$-xy will be (-6)$^{2}$+(6)$^{2}$-(-6)(6) = 108

Consider Circle C1 represented by the curve $x^2+y^2-10x-8y+25=0$ and C2 represented by $x^2+y^2-8x-8y+23=0$. The area formed by the tangent common to C1 and C2, a tangent of C2 parallel to x axis and the line y=x+8 is:

A. 32 sq. units

B. 2 sq. units

C. 16 sq. units
questions.solution_text:
C1 is given as: $x^2+y^2-10x-8y+25=0$, which can be re-written as $x^2-10x+25+y^2-8y+16=16$
Or, C1= $\left(x-5\right)^2+\left(y-4\right)^2=4^2$.
C1 has the centre at (5,4) and radius = 4 units.
Similarly, C2 is given as: $x^2+y^2-8x-8y+23=0$, which when manipulated becomes $x^2-8x+16+y^2-8y+16=9$
or, C2 is given as $\left(x-4\right)^2+\left(y-4\right)^2=3^2$, which has a centre at (4,4) and radius 3 units.
The circles, its common tangent, tangents of C2 parallel to X-axis and the line y=x+8 can be drawn as:
The common tangent is represented by the dotted line x=1. The purple line shows y= x+8
The two tangents of the circle C2 are y=1 and y=7.
So, there are two possible triangles formed using the information given in the question, $\triangle ABC\ \ $ and $\triangle ADE\ $
Point C is simply the intersection of y=7 and x=1. So, C=(1,7)
In $\triangle ABC\ \ $, Base AC= 2 units, height BC= 2 units. So, area= $\ \frac{\ 1}{2}\times2\times2=2\ $sq. units
In $\triangle ADE\ $, Base AE= 8 units, Height ED= 8 units. So, area= $\ \frac{\ 1}{2}\times8\times8=32\ $sq. units
therefore both A and B are correct

questions.question_text:
Mohit and Narayan started a company by investing their life savings. The company faced huge losses because of which its value halved. Narayan took out all of his remaining money but Mohit kept on working hard. He made a 300% profit next month. Meanwhile, Narayan found out a scheme of ‘Double your money in 30 days’ and invested half of the money he had left with him. They met at the end of the month and found out they had exactly the same amount of money, as Narayan lost all the money he had invested in the bogus scheme.

If both of them invested money in multiples of Rs. 1000, which of the following can be the total money they had invested in the company initially?
questions.solution_text:
Let the amount Mohit invested be 1000M and that Narayan invested be 1000N Rupees, where M and N are natural numbers.
The value of the company halved. Hence, their investments will also be halved and will become 500M and 500N respectively.
Mohit made a 300% profit the next month. This means, a profit of 3 times 500M. Thus, the final amount with him at the end of the month will be $4\times\ 500M=2000M$.
Narayan lost half of what he had to a bogus scheme. Thus, the total amount with him at the end will be 250N.
It has been given that 2000M=250N. (Money at the end of the month is the same).
Or N=8M.
Total amount in the beginning= 1000M+1000N = 1000M+8000M = 9000M.
Since M is a natural number, the total sum must be a multiple of 9000. Only Option C satisfies this criterion, and hence, is the correct answer.

questions.question_text: An empty tank can be filled in 70 minutes by water flowing from a pipe of square cross section of side 3 cm at the rate of 4 cm/sec. Now another pipe of a circular cross section is added at the bottom of the tank which empties the tank at the rate of 7 cm/sec. When both the pipes are present the tank when empty gets filled completely in 180 minutes. What is the radius of the circular pipe at the bottom of the tank (in cm)?
questions.solution_text:
Volume of flow of water into the tank per second = Rate of flow * Area of cross section of pipe
In first case with only one pipe, Volume flow per sec = $3^2 \times 4$ = 36 units
In second case, Volume flow per sec = 36 - $ \pi r^2\times7$ = 36- $ 7\pi r^2$ units
Ratio of times taken is the inverse ratio of volumes flow per sec
=> $\frac{70}{180}=\frac{36-7\pi r^2}{36}$
Solving, we get r = 1 cm.

options.label: D

questions.solution_text:
We need to make sure that he gets maximum return on the Principal of 10000Rs for a period of 4 Years . 
For Simple interest the Amount earned = P(1+RT/100)
For Compound Interest the Amount earned is$P\left(1+\frac{R}{\left(100\right)}\right)^N$ .
Now calculating the Amount received for different options .
Option A : First  Compound interest of  20 percent per annum followed by Simple Interest at 10 percent per annum  :
10000(1.2)(1.2) = 14400 
14000(1 +2*0.1) = Rs 17280 .
Option B : First Simple interest of 20 percent per annum followed by Compound Interest at 10 percent per annum :
10000(1+2*0.2) = 14000
14000(1.1)(1.1) = Rs 16940
Option C : First Compound interest of 15 percent per annum followed by Simple Interest at 15 percent per annum :
10000(1.15)(1.15) = 13225
13225(1+2*0.15) = Rs 17192.5
Option D : First Simple  interest of 15 percent per annum followed by Compound Interest at 15 percent per annum :
10000(1+2*0.15) = 13000
13000(1.15)(1.15) = Rs 17192.5
Option A gives you the maximum returns .

questions.question_text: The sum of the last two digits of $(1^3 + 2^3 + 3^3)^{172}$ is
questions.solution_text:
Let us first evaluate the base of $(1^3 + 2^3 + 3^3)^{172}$ 
= $1^3 + 2^3 + 3^3$ = 36
Now we have to find the last two digits of $36^{172}$
= $6^{344}$
The remainder when $6^{344}$ is divided by 100 is calculated using Chinese remainder theorem.
6 and 100 are not co-prime to each other.
Calculate $6^{344}$ mod 25 and $6^{344}$ mod 4 
$6^{20}$ mod 25 is 1   [From Euler theorem, Euler of 25 = 25*(1-$\frac{1}{5}$) = 20]
$6^{344}$ mod 25 = $6^{340}*6^4$ mod 25 = 1*1296 mod 25  = 36*36 mod 25= 11*11 mod 25 = 121 mod 25 = 21
$6^{344}$ mod 4 is 0
25p+21 = 4q+0
Using trial and error p = 3 and q = 24
25p+21 = 25*3 + 21
=96 is the last two digits of $6^{344}$
Sum of the digits = 15
15 is the correct answer.

questions.question_text: Pipe A, pipe B and pipe C are used to fill a tank. The flow rate of pipe C is 25% less than pipe B. To fill the empty tank completely, Pipe A and Pipe B together take one third the time taken by Pipe C alone. If all three pipes can fill the tank in 15 hours, then find the time taken (in hours) by A alone to fill the tank completely.
questions.solution_text:
Assuming the flow rate of pipe A is a  and  that of the pipe B is b, then the flow rate of pipe C = 0.75b
The capacity of the tank = Flow rate of all the tanks*Time taken  = 15(a+b+0.75b) = 15(a+1.75b)
To fill the empty tank completely, pipe A and pipe B together take one-third time than pipe C alone. It means that the flow rate of A and B combined is equal to 3 times that of C.
Hence, a+b  = 3*0.75b
=> a = 1.25b
Hence, the total capacity of the tank = 15(1.25b+1.75b) = 45b
Time taken by A to fill the tank = $\dfrac{45b}{1.25b}\ $  = 36 hours

questions.question_text: PQRS is an isosceles trapezium as shown in the figure. The lengths of the parallel sides are 8 cm and 10cm. The length of the non-parallel side is 8 cm. Which among the following can be the ratio of lengths of one of the parallel sides and the diagonals of the trapezium?
questions.solution_text:
PQRS is an isosceles trapezium and it is inscribed in a circle so it is a cyclic isosceles trapezium.
So all the properties of a cyclic quadrilateral can be applied here.
In an isosceles trapezium, the non-parallel sides are equal.
The diagonals of an isosceles trapezium are equal, so PR = SQ
From Ptolemy Theorem,
PQ*SR+ PS*QR = PR*QS
8*10 +8*8 = PR*PR
PR = 12 cm
The possible ratio of one of the sides and the diagonal = 8:12, 10:12
=2:3, 5:6
B is the correct answer.

questions.question_text: In any given ball, a batsman can hit either of 0, 1, 2, 3, 4 or 6 runs. There is no possibility for wickets or extra runs. The probability of hitting a six is 1/10, the probability of hitting a four is also 1/10. The probability of hitting any other run out of all possible runs is the same. In the final of 2019 WC between New Zealand and England, New Zealand needs to score a minimum of 34 runs in the Super Over (6 balls) to defend the WC Title. What is the probability that New Zealand retains the title?
questions.solution_text:
P(hitting a 6) = $\frac{1}{10}$
P(hitting a 4) = $\frac{1}{10}$
To get 34 runs, they can hit 6,6,6,6,6,4 or 6,6,6,6,5,5 runs. But 5 runs can not be scored in a ball.
P(6,6,6,6,6,4) = $^6C_1\times\ \left(\frac{1}{10}\right)^5\left(\frac{1}{10}\right)=\frac{6}{10^6}$ [$^6C_1\ $ is included since they can hit a 4 in any of the 6 balls].
To get 35 runs, they can hit 6,6,6,6,6,5 runs. But 5 runs can not be scored in a ball, so this is not possible.
To get 36 runs, they can hit 6,6,6,6,6,6 runs.
P(6,6,6,6,6,6) = $\left(\frac{1}{10}\right)^6=\frac{1}{10^6}$
Hence, total probability = $\frac{7}{1000000}$

Profit Percentage =  ((11L/27)x*100)/(16L/27)  = 1100/16 ....(1)
Ratio of profit percentages = 16/(11*8) = 2:11
C is the answer.

questions.question_text: Pipe A can fill a cistern in x minutes. Pipe B can empty half a cistern in y minutes. Pipe C can fill a cistern in z minutes. If A, B and C are kept open, the empty cistern is half-full in 3 minutes. Which of the following is an incorrect representation of possible values of x, y and z respectively?
questions.solution_text:
Let the entire task of filling or emptying the cylinder be 2xyz.
In 1 min, A can fill 2yz, B can empty xz and C can fill 2xy units.
In 3 mins, total units filled = 3(2yz + 2xy - xz) = 2xyz/2
2yz + 2xy - xz = xyz/3
Dividing by xyz throughout.
2/x +2/z = 1/3 + 1/y
Putting the values, all but option A satisfies the equation.

The values of a and x are integers

questions.question_text: A circular skating ring has to be formed such that the internal diameter is 70m and the width is 5m. Inside the inner circle of the track, a rectangular ground has to be formed such that its area is the maximum possible. If a contractor charges Rs 7 per $m^2$ of work done for the circular track and rectangular field, how much money will he earn by completing the above-mentioned work. (Take $\pi = \frac{22}{7}$)
questions.solution_text:
The inner radius of the circle will be $\frac{70}{2} = 35m$ Outer diameter will be 35m+5m = 40m
Area of skating ring will be = $\pi\left(40^2-35^2\right)=375\pi$
Let the sides of rectangles be $a$ and $b$, the area will be  maximum when a=b. Thus it has to be square for the area to be maximum.
Thus, diagonal of square = diameter of inner circles. $a\sqrt{2}=70$
Thus $a=35\sqrt{2}$
Area = $a^2 = 2450$
Total area = $375\pi +2450$
Cost = $7\times (375\pi +2450)$
Cost = $7\times\left(375\left(\frac{22}{7}\right)+2450\right)=8250+17150=25,400$

questions.question_text: Ganapati is a resident of Mumbai. Gajanan is a resident of Pune. For Ganesh Chaturdhi, they plan to meet, but were unsure who would be meeting whom. Ganapati drives towards Pune unaware that Gajanan was coming to Mumbai to meet him. They start at their houses at the same time. They both meet at Lonawala and after a brief chat, decide to continue to their trips and interchange their houses. If Ganapati takes 6 hours to go to Pune from Lonawala and Gajanan takes 9 hours to go to Mumbai from Lonawala, what is the speed of Gajanan if the speed of Ganapati was 24km/hr?
questions.solution_text:
They travelled for the same amount of time before meeting at Lonawala. So, the total time taken by Ganapati = t + 6 hours
Total time taken by Gajanan = t + 9 hours. 
So, ratio of speeds = d/(t+6):d/(t+9) = (t+9)/(t+6)
Distance from Lonawala to Mumbai = 24t
Gajanan takes 9 hours to cover this distance. 
Hence his speed is 24t/9 = 8t/3
But 24: 8t/3 = (t+9)/(t+6) 
So, t (t+9) = 9(t+6)
$t^2$ = 54
The only positive root of this equation is t = 7.34 hours.
So, t = 7.34 hours. 
So, speed of Gajanan = 7.34 * 8/3 = 19.57 km/hr

questions.question_text: In a regular pentagon PQRST, what is the ratio of the area of triangle PRS to the area of the pentagon PQRST?
questions.solution_text:
Each angle of a regular pentagon is 108 degrees. In triangle PTS, angle T = 108 degrees, and PT = TS. So, angle TPS = angle TSP = 36 degrees.
Similarly, angle QPR = 36 degrees. So, angle SPR = 108 - (36 + 36) = 36 degrees as show below,
Also, PS = PR
Area of triangle PSR = ½ * PS * PR * sin 36
Area of the pentagon = Sum of areas of the three triangles = Area of triangle PTS + Area of triangle PSR + Area of triangle PQR
= ½ * PT * PS * sin (angle TPS) + ½ * PS * PR * sin 36 + ½ * PQ * PR * sin (angle QPR)
= ½ * PT * PS * sin 36 + ½ * PS * PR * sin 36 + ½ * PQ * PR * sin 36
Required ratio = ½ * PS * PR * sin 36 / (½ * PT * PS * sin 36 + ½ * PS * PR * sin 36 + ½ * PQ * PR * sin 36)
= PR / (PT + PR + PQ)
PT = PQ = SR
In triangle PSX,
cos (angle PSR) = SX/PS = RS/2*PR
SR = 2 * PR cos (angle PSR) = 2 * PR * cos 72
Ratio = PR / (2 * PR cos 72 + PR + 2 * PR cos 72) = 1 / (4 cos 72 + 1)

questions.question_text: Ram who is a retail seller of rice, buys the product from a whole-seller named Siddharth and then sells it to the customer. Siddharth is a deceitful person. Let Siddharth sell the product to Ram at stated rate of Rs 100/kg
He uses a faulty weighing machine which shows 20% more reading than the actual.

When Ram is selling the product he marks up the rate by 10%, The selling price would be Rs 110/kg
Thus we see that Ram is making a loss. 
Loss = 120-110 = 10
Loss% = $\frac{10}{120}\times100\%\ =\ 8.33\%$
